meetings.title: BOCC Work Session - October 5, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the October 5, 2020 BOCC work session with all five commissioners participating virtually. The board received a presentation from Nana Asante Smith of Black Agenda 919 (backed by 537 petition signatures) urging an institutionalized, funded Joint Racial Equity Commission, reviewed consent agenda items—including $2.4 million in NCORR CDBG-CV eviction diversion funds, DPS CIP/Northern High/DSA bond adjustments, and the UNC-led Back on the Bull Community Health Ambassadors ILA (where Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton pressed for explicit M/WBE and Durham hiring protections)—and heard reports from the ABC Board, Animal Shelter feasibility consultants ($28.2 million new facility vs. $2.4 million interim repairs), Emergency Management on the Eno-Haw Regional Hazard Mitigation Plan, and DPS Foundation on Hope Learning Centers. Commissioners voted unanimously (5-0) to suspend the rules and approve the master Reinvestment Partners contract expanding medically vulnerable homeless housing at the Carolina Duke Inn from 40 to 64 rooms. During the directives review, Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Reckhow renewed criticisms of the administration's $3 million hazard pay and lapsed-salary spending without prior board policy review before the board adjourned unanimously (5-0) into closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After resolving Chair Jacobs's audio connection, Clerk Monica Toomer read citizen comments, including remarks from Faith Polsart regarding internal board conflict and racial/gender bias allegations involving commissioners and county staff. All five commissioners, the county manager, and the county attorney were confirmed present.

agenda_items.title: Work Session Review of Consent Agenda Items (Items 489–557)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis and staff walked commissioners through consent items including IT/SAP and Microsoft renewals, Snow Hill pump station increases ($2.4 million LOBs), $359,582 in DHHS COVID public health funds, Made in Durham ($200,000), $2.4 million in NCORR CDBG-CV eviction diversion funds for DSS, Nighthawk election security ($222,039 CTCL grant), and DPS capital/LOBs adjustments for Northern High School, Elementary C, and Durham School of the Arts. On Item 539 (Back on the Bull Community Health Ambassadors ILA), Commissioner Howerton questioned the lack of explicit M/WBE and Durham-local hiring requirements in UNC's contract, while Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Reckhow raised questions on Snow Hill cost-sharing and DSA renovations.

agenda_items.title: Item 20-0533: Durham County Racial Equity Commission Proposal (Black Agenda 919)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Nana Asante Smith of Black Agenda 919 presented a petition with 537 signatures urging the county, city, and school board to create, staff, and fund a permanent Joint Racial Equity Commission to implement the Racial Equity Task Force's recommendations. Commissioners noted collaboration with Task Force co-chair Judge Elaine O'Neill and highlighted Durham County's newly hired Racial Equity Officer ahead of the Task Force's formal presentation on October 26.

agenda_items.title: Durham County ABC Board Annual Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: ABC Board Manager Nigel Sullivan reported FY2020 sales of $44.2 million (up 9.63%) and Q1 FY2021 sales of $11.3 million (up 14.45%) despite mixed-beverage declines, alongside store modernizations at Riverview, Holloway, Highway 98, Highway 55, and TW Alexander. Commissioner Reckhow commended the $100,000 extra distribution and urged higher future distributions to help offset county revenue declines.

agenda_items.title: Animal Shelter Facility Assessment and Feasibility Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Animal Arts architect Heather Lewis and county staff presented four options for the undersized East Club Boulevard shelter, recommending a new $28.2 million 36,000-square-foot facility on a 6.2-acre site (Option 3) paired with $2.4 million in short-term health/HVAC improvements (Option 4). Commissioners discussed pairing trap-neuter-return (TNR) and stray-hold ordinance reforms with phased CIP planning so interim spending would not be wasted if a new shelter moves forward quickly.

agenda_items.title: Draft Eno-Haw Regional Hazard Mitigation Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief Emergency Manager Leslie O'Connor presented the 2020 four-county Eno-Haw Regional Hazard Mitigation Plan (expanding to include Person County), covering natural, technological, and human-caused hazards and priority mitigation actions such as unincorporated stormwater fees and backup generator hookups at Northern High School. Chair Jacobs urged integrating the plan into the Comprehensive Plan and transit planning ahead of an October 12 resolution vote.

agenda_items.title: Community-Based HOPE Learning Centers Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Megan Gonzales-Smith (DPS Foundation), Alexandra Valladares/Student U representatives, and Drew Cummings updated commissioners ahead of October 12 contract approvals, noting the Foundation committed up to $300,000 to waive $70/week reduced-lunch fees at DPS sites and reporting zero COVID-19 cases in community centers. Commissioners Reckhow, Carter, and Howerton pressed partners for disaggregated October 16 data on Durham Housing Authority students, daily attendance, and transportation barriers.

agenda_items.title: Reinvestment Partners Master Contract for Carolina Duke Inn Homeless Housing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Drew Cummings and Peter Gilbert of Reinvestment Partners presented the coordinated service contract expanding leased rooms for medically vulnerable homeless individuals at the Carolina Duke Inn from 40 to 64, integrated with Project Access, Urban Ministries, and Coordinated Entry, with state non-congregate waiver reimbursement expected. The board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to approve the contract immediately.

agenda_items.title: Board Directives Review, Hazard Pay Oversight, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During directives review, Chair Jacobs questioned why hazard pay follow-up was omitted and staff reported $3 million in hazard pay (with $1.8 million reimbursed by CARES) and $659,000 in COVID overtime since March. Jacobs and Reckhow objected that extending hazard pay via lapsed salaries and broad remote/on-site interpretations had major unapproved budget impacts, after which the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and adjourned at 6:31 p.m.

votes.item_title: Motion to Suspend the Rules for Reinvestment Partners Carolina Duke Inn Contract
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote suspending work-session rules to take immediate action.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Jacobs noted that delaying approval cost community partners money and kept medically vulnerable unhoused residents waiting for rooms.

votes.item_title: Approval of Reinvestment Partners Master Contract for Carolina Duke Inn Non-Congregate Housing
votes.discussion_detail: Approved master contract with Reinvestment Partners, Urban Ministries of Durham, and Project Access expanding Carolina Duke Inn capacity from 40 to 64 rooms, utilizing previously allocated funds expected to be reimbursed under the state non-congregate shelter waiver/FEMA.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn to Closed Session (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
votes.discussion_detail: Board entered closed session to consider personnel qualifications, performance, or complaints/grievances under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6).

disagreements.issue: M/WBE Participation and Local Hiring Accountability in the UNC Back on the Bull Community Health Ambassadors ILA (Item 539)
disagreements.summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton challenged the interlocal agreement transferring county funds to the City of Durham for UNC Gillings School of Public Health's Community Health Ambassadors contract, arguing it lacked explicit M/WBE participation and local Durham hiring protections.
disagreements.side_a_position: Contracts funded with county tax dollars should explicitly document M/WBE participation and local Durham equity hiring standards rather than deferring to an outside university's procurement rules.
side_a_arguments: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton noted the agenda materials contained no M/WBE provisions and questioned why Chapel Hill-based UNC would control hiring for a Durham community program without documented local diversity and equity commitments.
disagreements.side_b_position: The ILA transfers previously approved funds to the City for a scope already geared toward hiring diverse Durham residents to assist businesses of color, and staff can follow up on UNC/City hiring practices.
side_b_arguments: General Manager Jodi Miller explained the ILA simply transfers funds approved on August 24 to the City to contract with UNC, and committed to obtaining UNC and City recruitment/hiring strategies via email.
Chair Wendy Jacobs pointed out that the attached scope of work specified at least 4 of 10 ambassadors must be Latinx and that the program serves businesses and communities of color.
disagreements.resolution: Staff agreed to follow up with the City and UNC to provide written recruitment and equity-hiring details ahead of final consent approval.

disagreements.issue: Board Oversight of COVID-19 Hazard Pay Differential and Use of Lapsed Salaries
disagreements.summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow criticized the administration's $3 million hazard pay expenditure and reliance on frozen/lapsed salaries without explicit board policy approval.
disagreements.side_a_position: Multi-million-dollar hazard pay decisions and the repurposing of frozen-position lapsed salaries have major budget trade-offs and require direct board policy review and clear eligibility boundaries.
side_a_arguments: Chair Wendy Jacobs noted the City of Durham ended hazard pay on June 19 at $433,000, questioned reports of staff opting to work on-site qualifying for differential pay, and stated she had assumed salary freezes would preserve funds for broader community needs.
Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow questioned how long hazard pay would continue and urged clear boundaries and follow-up documentation.
disagreements.side_b_position: Hazard pay was a necessary workforce retention and emergency response measure largely offset by CARES Act and projected 75%/25% FEMA/state reimbursements.
side_b_arguments: County Manager Wendell Davis and Claudia Hager argued the 10% differential prevented retirements/turnover, projected a net local cost of roughly $791,000, and noted peer counties were evaluating hazard pay through December.
disagreements.resolution: Board scheduled a dedicated public discussion of FEMA guidelines and hazard pay policy for the upcoming October 13 regular meeting.

meetings.title: Durham County Government BOCC Live
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the September 29, 2020 meeting with all five commissioners participating virtually, opening with a moment of silence noting Yom Kippur and prayers for victims of gun violence and Breonna Taylor's family. The board unanimously approved prior minutes (5-0), proclaimed October 2020 Domestic Violence Awareness Month, and approved the consent agenda (5-0) with a wording change to NCACC legislative goals. Following a public hearing on UDO Text Amendment TC2000003 regarding development agreements, commissioners voted 5-0 on both the consistency statement and ordinance adoption despite Planning Commission opposition and concerns from Commissioners Reckhow, Jacobs, and Howerton over the lack of codified community-benefit standards, directing staff to return in November with formal guidelines. After Public Health Director Rod Jenkins's COVID-19 briefing, Vice Chair James Hill presented revised Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force bylaws—amending county appointments, adding the DSS director to the resource panel, and allowing a two-thirds extension past 24 months—which the board approved 5-0 alongside recommending member-elected co-chairs before making board appointments and adjourning 5-0 to closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Minutes Approval, and Domestic Violence Awareness Month Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the virtual session, acknowledged Yom Kippur, and held a moment of silence including prayers requested by Commissioner Howerton for gun-violence victims and Breonna Taylor's family. After announcements on Pre-K enrollment, the US 15-501 corridor study, and Triangle Commuter Rail surveys, the board voted 5-0 to approve the August 3 and August 10 minutes and proclaimed October 2020 Domestic Violence Awareness Month with Durham Crisis Response Center director Kent Wallace-Meigs.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (NCACC Legislative Goals and Senior Services)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow requested amending an NCACC legislative goal to reference 'mediation programs' rather than training programs, and commissioners received a brief update on COVID-19 senior services delivery from Durham Center for Senior Life. The board unanimously approved the consent agenda by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC2000003 (Development Agreements)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City-County Planning staff Scott Whiteman and Sarah Young presented UDO text amendment TC2000003 expressly authorizing statutory development agreements while adding Planning Commission public hearings, pre-submittal/neighborhood meetings, and environmental-protection safeguards beyond state law minimums. Commissioners Reckhow, Jacobs, and Howerton noted Planning Commission opposition and the lack of codified community-benefit standards, while Commissioner Carter supported approval; after holding the public hearing, the board adopted the consistency statement (5-0) and ordinance (5-0) while directing staff to bring community-benefit criteria to the November work session.

agenda_items.title: Public Health COVID-19 Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported on Durham County's COVID-19 status past the 200-day mark of pandemic operations, detailing daily case counts, contact tracing, and community prevention efforts alongside General Manager Joanne Pierce.

agenda_items.title: Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Revised Bylaws
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill presented revised task force bylaws changing the county's five appointees to two at-large seats, one justice-involved resident, one community organization leader, and one parent of a murdered child; adding the DSS director to the Community Resource Panel; and allowing a two-thirds membership vote to extend past 24 months. Commissioner Howerton urged letting task force members elect their own co-chairs rather than elected officials appointing them; after clarifying the edits, the board approved the bylaws 5-0 and agreed to raise the co-chair selection issue at the October Joint City-County Committee meeting while immediately opening applications.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler announced board appointments to the Durham Tourism Development Authority (Jennings Brody, Barry Van Deman), Durham County Hospital Corporation, Durham Open Space and Trails Commission (Zia Ming-Awe), Environmental Affairs Board (Melanie Allen), Historic Preservation Commission (Laura Rezelman), and Memorial Stadium Authority (Tyrone Wilson). The board then voted 5-0 to adjourn to closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(1).

votes.item_title: Approval of August 3, 2020 Work Session and August 10, 2020 Regular Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the August 3 work session and August 10 regular session minutes without objection.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted consistency statement for UDO Text Amendment TC2000003 following public hearing.

votes.item_title: Adoption of UDO Text Amendment TC2000003 (Development Agreements)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted UDO amendment authorizing development agreements with added public-hearing, neighborhood-meeting, and environmental safeguards, while requesting staff return in November with community-benefit criteria.

votes.item_title: Approval of Revised Bylaws for Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force
votes.discussion_detail: Approved revised county appointee categories (2 at-large, 1 justice-involved, 1 community org leader, 1 parent of a murdered child), addition of DSS director to the Community Resource Panel, two-sentence termination/extension wording, and recommendation to discuss member-elected co-chairs at the October Joint City-County Committee meeting.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn to Closed Session (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(1))
votes.discussion_detail: Board moved to closed session to consult with county attorney under attorney-client privilege and protect confidential records.

disagreements.issue: Lack of Codified Community-Benefit Standards in UDO Development Agreements Amendment (TC2000003)
disagreements.summary: While all five commissioners ultimately voted to adopt TC2000003, commissioners debated Planning Commission opposition and whether the ordinance was too vague without explicit criteria defining qualifying community benefits.
disagreements.side_a_position: The draft ordinance language is overly broad and lacks clear standards or community-benefit parameters, fueling Planning Commission opposition and transparency concerns.
side_a_arguments: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow described the text as 'very general, very loose' without guidelines and noted Planning Commission concern that the amendment was fast-tracked for a pending development.

Chair Wendy Jacobs agreed with Planning Commissioner Austin that criteria should not depend solely on who holds office, and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton questioned whether the Planning Commission had voted before staff briefings.
disagreements.side_b_position: Staff's added environmental and public-hearing safeguards address major transparency concerns, and Durham County should adopt the tool now following City Council's unanimous approval.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Heidi Carter praised staff for protecting environmentally sensitive standards and adding Planning Commission and neighborhood hearing requirements, viewing development agreements as a valuable tool to secure benefits like affordable housing.
Assistant County Attorney Brian Taylor/attorney staff confirmed every agreement still requires board approval and parameters can be refined afterward.
disagreements.resolution: Adopted 5-0 with explicit direction for staff to return at the November work session to develop formal board guidelines on community-benefit criteria.

disagreements.issue: Co-Chair Selection Process for the Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force
disagreements.summary: Commissioners debated whether the task force's co-chairs should be elected by community task force members or remain appointed by elected officials as already approved by City Council and the School Board.
disagreements.side_a_position: Community members on the task force should elect their own chair/co-chairs and vice chair to preserve community autonomy and avoid political interference.
side_a_arguments: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton argued that residents demanded autonomy without elected officials picking leadership, and Vice Chair James Hill concurred that most boards choose their own officers.
disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid delaying appointment advertising or forcing re-approval delays by City Council and the School Board over co-chair wording, and instead advance the recommendation to the joint committee.
side_b_arguments: Commissioners Heidi Carter and Wendy Jacobs noted that City Council and the School Board had already approved the prior bylaws and warned against holding up urgent recruitment while gun violence persisted.
disagreements.resolution: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow proposed approving the revised bylaws 5-0 immediately to begin advertising seats while placing the co-chair selection proposal on the October Joint City-County Committee agenda.

meetings.title: Durham County Government BOCC Live
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the September 15, 2020 (originally convened September 14) regular session with all five commissioners participating virtually. The board unanimously approved prior minutes (5-0), adopted proclamations for National Preparedness Month and a Women's Commission resolution supporting women's health and equal access to abortion (read by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow), and approved the consent agenda (5-0), including over $1 million in City eviction diversion partnership funds and a renewable energy plan contract. Following a public hearing on Zoning Map Change Z1900051 (Long Beverage at 10500 World Trade Boulevard), the board voted 5-0 on both the consistency statement and ordinance rezoning the 3.12-acre site from Industrial Light with a development plan to straight Industrial Light to accommodate expanded parking and 100 new jobs. Commissioners also received COVID-19 and NCACC/federal CARES Act legislative briefings from Public Health Director Rod Jenkins and Deborah Craig-Ray—including criticism of the 500,000-population federal funding cliff—before entering closed session (5-0) and reconvening to unanimously rescind (5-0) the July 13, 2020 $540,000 Carolina Duke Inn contract.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the virtual session, read the public charge, and held a moment of silence. After announcements covering 2020 general election absentee ballot drop-off tents, early voting across 14 sites, census sweepstakes, and COVID-19 testing at Walgreens, the board unanimously approved prior meeting minutes (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: National Preparedness Month Proclamation and Resolution Supporting Women's Health and Abortion Access
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read the National Preparedness Month 2020 proclamation alongside Chief Emergency Manager Leslie O'Connor and Emergency Management Director Jim Groves, reflecting on simultaneous responses to COVID-19, the county malware attack, and tropical storms. At 00:47:06, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow read a Durham Women's Commission resolution opposing North Carolina abortion restrictions, calling for repeal of the Hyde Amendment, and urging federal passage of the Women's Health Protection Act and EACH Woman Act.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Eviction Diversion Partnership and Renewable Energy Plan)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved and Commissioner Reckhow seconded approval of the consent agenda without pulling items. Chair Jacobs highlighted numerous grant awards, over $1 million in City rental assistance administered through DSS for eviction diversion, and the renewable energy plan contract as the board approved the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change Z1900051 (Long Beverage, 10500 World Trade Blvd)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Grace Smith and applicant representatives Andy Porter and Patrick Byker presented Z1900051 to rezone 3.12 acres from Industrial Light with a development plan (IL(D)) to straight Industrial Light (IL), removing an old four-space parking cap so Long Beverage could expand parking and add ~100 jobs while installing sidewalks on the concurrent site plan. Following the public hearing, commissioners unanimously adopted both the consistency statement (5-0) and rezoning ordinance (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Public Health COVID-19 Update and State/Federal Legislative Goals Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported 230 active COVID-19 cases, 88 cumulative deaths, 7,346 total cases, a declining 7-day average of 28, and a 4.2% test positivity rate, while answering questions about pediatric testing at Holton and pharmacies. At 01:45:44, Deborah Craig-Ray and Rod Jenkins reviewed NCACC and public health legislative goals—including block grants, adult guardianship, Medicaid expansion, and tobacco control—while Chair Jacobs urged drafting a letter opposing the federal CARES Act 500,000-population funding cliff.

agenda_items.title: Directives Review, Closed Session, and Rescission of July 13 Carolina Duke Inn Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed the directives portal, requesting a technical fix for broken links, and voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6). Reconvening in open session at 03:17:02, the board voted 5-0 to rescind its July 13, 2020 vote authorizing a $540,000 contract with Carolina Duke Inn for homeless COVID-19 services before adjourning.

meetings.title: BOCC Work Session - September 8, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the marathon six-hour September 8, 2020 BOCC work session with all five commissioners participating virtually. Commissioners heard ten citizen comments—largely urging approval of the Safety and Wellness Task Force without law enforcement, supporting a My Brother's Keeper (MBK) advisory board, and seeking a ban on retail cosmetic testers—before reviewing 25 consent agenda items, including detention center COVID-19 testing, Back on the Bull funds, and temporary public art. The board received annual updates from Downtown Durham Inc. and the Greater Durham Chamber of Commerce, reviewed $1.2 million in Main Library donor naming recognitions, examined FY2020–21 COVID-19 spending and DSS pandemic operations, and voted unanimously (5-0) to suspend the rules and adopt the amended $8.8 million Coronavirus Relief Fund (CRF) plan (including $2.9 million for the City). Commissioners also debated redesigning the nonprofit RFP around three versus four strategic areas and discussed whether MBK Durham needed a formal advisory board over its existing Milestone Advocacy Teams, before voting 5-0 to remove an Adult Care Home committee member for poor attendance, entering closed session (5-0), and voting 4-0 (with Commissioner Howerton absent) to disclaim a library bequest.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the virtual work session and Clerk Monica Toomer read ten citizen comments, including residents urging Commissioners Howerton, Hill, and Reckhow to pass the Safety and Wellness Task Force without law enforcement participation, a Sephora worker requesting an ordinance banning open cosmetic testers, and Brandon Williams urging creation of an MBK Durham Advisory Board. Chair Jacobs noted the Racial Equity Task Force had requested to present on October 26.

agenda_items.title: Work Session Review of 25-Item Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff walked commissioners through 25 consent items, including election grant preparations, temporary public art/history policy amendments, and detention center COVID-19 testing logistics with the Sheriff's Office. Commissioners also discussed how to structure future COVID-19 funding requests and maintain transparency.

agenda_items.title: Annual Reports: Downtown Durham Inc. (DDI) and Greater Durham Chamber of Commerce
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DDI CEO Nicole Thompson reported on downtown office and residential growth, five COVID-related street-level closures, outdoor dining advocacy, and commercial rent pressures, while Chamber CEO Geoff Durham reported 2,768 new jobs and nearly $2 billion in capital investment alongside the BULLS life-sciences workforce initiative. Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Reckhow pressed both leaders on connecting unemployed and low-income Durham residents to biotech and IT pipelines.

agenda_items.title: Item 20-0394: Main Library Naming Opportunities ($1.2 Million Campaign)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Library Director Tammy Baggett and Durham Library Foundation Executive Director Karen Wells presented donor naming recognitions tied to $1.2 million raised for the Main Library transformation ($2,500 to $100,000 tiers). Chair Jacobs noted the fundraising-linked process differed from the county's 2005 naming policy and agreed with Baggett to update the policy accordingly.

agenda_items.title: Item 20-0474: Review of County COVID-19 Revenues and Expenditures and Amended CRF Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Keith Lane outlined the four funding buckets supporting COVID-19 spending, and General Manager Jodi Miller presented the Round 2 Coronavirus Relief Fund (CRF) plan bringing total county CRF funds to nearly $8.8 million ($2.9 million allocated to the City under S.L. 2020-80), prioritizing testing ($255,000), public health/ambassadors ($1.8 million), food/homeless non-congregate compliance ($815,388), and small-business mitigation/Back on the Bull ($382,098). To meet the September 15 state deadline, the board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and approved the amended CRF plan by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Department of Social Services (DSS) Pandemic Operations Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS Director Ben Rose reported an average of $1.8 million in additional monthly Food and Nutrition Services allotments, 7,431 food/nutrition applications processed at 99% timeliness, COVID Medicaid testing coverage, emergency rental/utility assistance exhaustion, and designation of investigative CPS/APS workers as first responders. He also noted staff flexible schedules to manage remote schooling.

agenda_items.title: Item 20-0487: Durham County Nonprofit Funding RFP Redesign
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Keith Lane and Deputy Manager Claudia Hager proposed shifting the three-year nonprofit RFP (~$750,000 annually, starting with a $353,750 half-year calendar bridge in January 2021) to fewer, larger awards focused on four strategic areas—housing security, food security, child/youth enrichment, and workforce development—managed by departmental subject-matter experts. Commissioners debated whether housing belonged in the pilot given limited county housing expertise and urged tightening the fall review timeline before signaling consensus to launch the four-area RFP.

agenda_items.title: My Brother's Keeper (MBK) Durham Grant Program and Proposed Advisory Board
agenda_items.discussion_summary: MBK Coordinator Edmund Lewis detailed leveraging Dominion Energy funds and Durham Tech skills-build grants ($200,000 line technician and $179,000 equity funding) to connect young Black men to living-wage trades. Addressing DeWarren Langley's proposal for an MBK Advisory Board, Lewis opposed creating a formal hierarchy over his existing Milestone Advocacy Teams, while Chair Jacobs and Commissioners Reckhow and Howerton asked General Manager Deborah Craig-Ray to convene Lewis and Langley to align efforts without slowing down workforce gap-funding.

agenda_items.title: Item 20-0558: Board Removal, Closed Session, and Karen Griffin Library Bequest Release
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and 5-0 to remove an Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee member due to poor attendance, then voted 5-0 to enter closed session solely for attorney-client consultation under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3). Reconvening with four members (Commissioner Howerton absent), the board voted 4-0 to suspend the rules and 4-0 to approve a release agreement disclaiming the county's interest in Karen Griffin's bequest in favor of the Durham County Library Foundation before adjourning.

votes.notes: Mover identified in full audio; seconded by Commissioner Howerton.
votes.discussion_detail: Suspended work-session rules to approve the Round 2 CRF spending plan ahead of the September 15 state submission deadline.

votes.notes: Transcript records 'So moved' and unanimous approval immediately following the 5-0 suspension vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the amended CRF plan incorporating $3.3 million in Round 2 county funds and $2.9 million in municipal pass-through funds to the City of Durham.

votes.discussion_detail: Removed an appointee from the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee due to poor attendance.

votes.notes: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton was absent after closed session.
votes.discussion_detail: Disclaimed Durham County's interest in the bequest of Karen Griffin in favor of the Durham County Library Foundation and authorized the chair to execute the release.

disagreements.issue: Nonprofit RFP Redesign: Inclusion of Housing Security and Review Timeline (Item 20-0487)
disagreements.summary: Commissioners debated whether the redesigned nonprofit RFP should include housing security alongside food security, youth enrichment, and workforce development, and pressed staff on oversight expertise and tight fall deadlines.
disagreements.side_a_position: Limit the redesigned pilot RFP to three areas where the county has dedicated subject-matter expertise rather than splitting limited funds four ways.
side_a_arguments: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow questioned whether housing fell inside the county's core expertise and staffing capacity, suggesting three focused areas might produce stronger results with $353,750 in bridge funding.
disagreements.side_b_position: Retain housing security as one of the four priority target areas and coordinate oversight with DSS and existing community partnerships.
side_b_arguments: Chair Wendy Jacobs noted housing repairs, financial literacy, and land conservancy needs made housing a top community priority, and Deputy Manager Claudia Hager argued DSS housing partnerships could cover oversight.
disagreements.resolution: Commissioner Reckhow accepted keeping all four target areas, and the board gave consensus direction to launch the RFP while tightening the award timeline and keeping commissioners informed.

disagreements.issue: Governance of My Brother's Keeper (MBK) Durham: Proposed Advisory Board vs. Milestone Advocacy Teams
disagreements.summary: Following a citizen-backed proposal from DeWarren Langley to create an official MBK Durham Advisory Board, MBK Coordinator Edmund Lewis defended his community-driven Milestone Advocacy Teams against adding an unnecessary hierarchy, while commissioners urged collaboration.
disagreements.side_a_position: Maintain MBK Durham's existing Milestone Advocacy Teams structure under staff leadership rather than creating a formal advisory board.
side_a_arguments: MBK Coordinator Edmund Lewis argued an advisory board would duplicate existing work, introduce hierarchy and compassion fatigue, and slow direct action connecting Black young men to CDL, skilled trades, and Durham Tech scholarships.
Commissioner Heidi Carter noted Lewis already had a functioning community structure that community members could join without building a new layer of governance.
disagreements.side_b_position: Engage proponents of the MBK Advisory Board in dialogue to strengthen strategic coordination, accountability, and immediate gap-funding deployment.
side_b_arguments: Citizen commenter Brandon Williams urged an advisory council for annual reporting and strategic alignment.

Chair Wendy Jacobs urged consulting the Milestone Advocacy Teams to deploy immediate crisis gap funding (such as Durham Tech Back to Work) rather than solely long-term endowments, while Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Brenda A. Howerton asked General Manager Deborah Craig-Ray to bring Lewis and Langley together without slowing MBK's momentum.
disagreements.resolution: General Manager Deborah Craig-Ray agreed to convene Edmund Lewis and DeWarren Langley to explore alignment and report back to the board.

meetings.title: BOCC Regular Session Meeting - August 24, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the August 24, 2020 regular session, opening with unanimous approval (4-0, with Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton experiencing login difficulties) of prior minutes before all five commissioners approved the consent agenda (5-0), including $1.14 million for Glenn Elementary roof work and $4.1 million for Admin Building 1 with a 1% public art/history set-aside. Following a public hearing, the board voted 5-0 to award $500,000 over seven years in performance-based incentives to Beam Therapeutics ($83 million investment, 201 jobs), heard COVID-19 and Board of Elections briefings, and voted 5-0 to approve $470,250 from the COVID reserve for Food Insight Group (FIG) home-delivered meals. After intense debate over County library non-use and depleted reserve funds, commissioners voted 5-0 to allocate $405,600 for 338 HOPE Learning Center seats for six weeks and voted 5-0 to extend the meeting past 11:00 p.m. On the $318,244 Community Health Ambassadors Program, the board split 4-1—with Wendy Jacobs, Heidi Carter, Ellen W. Reckhow, and James Hill voting Aye and Brenda A. Howerton voting Nay over duplication and budget-planning concerns—before making board appointments and adjourning 5-0 into closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Minutes (4-0), Library Recognition, and Consent Agenda (5-0)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs opened the virtual session with a moment of silence and announcements, and the board approved three sets of prior minutes 4-0 while Commissioner Howerton resolved login issues. After recognizing Durham County Library's architectural awards, all five commissioners approved the consent agenda 5-0, including Item 373 ($80,000 tobacco prevention), Item 411 ($1.14 million public school lottery funds for Glenn Elementary roofing), and Item 413 ($4.1 million Admin Building 1 refurbishment including a 1% public art/history set-aside).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Beam Therapeutics Economic Development Incentive ($500,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Officer Andy Miracle presented a $500,000 performance-based incentive package for cell- and gene-therapy manufacturer Beam Therapeutics ($83 million capital investment and 201 jobs), with Greater Durham Chamber support read into the record. Confirming community-benefit commitments would be embedded in the contract, the board voted 5-0 to approve the award.

agenda_items.title: Public Health COVID-19 Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported 276 active COVID-19 cases, 82 total deaths, and 6,671 cumulative cases, noting a sustained statewide decline since July 7 alongside ongoing contact tracing.

agenda_items.title: Home-Delivered Meals Contract with Food Insight Group (21BCC000025 — $470,250)

Budget staff warned the COVID reserve would fall to $1.825 million, prompting commissioners to demand full budget balances on future proposals before approving the amendment 5-0.

agenda_items.title: HOPE Community Learning Centers Initial Funding ($405,600 for 338 Seats)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners debated opening County libraries for remote learning centers—with Chair Jacobs questioning why libraries remained closed while Student U and the YMCA opened—and weighed funding 338 ready community seats for six weeks from the shrinking COVID reserve. After Commissioner Reckhow secured commitments for immediate outreach to Durham Housing Authority and DSS families and Commissioner Howerton raised Exceptional Children priority, the board voted 5-0 to allocate $405,600.

agenda_items.title: Board of Elections 2020 General Election Readiness Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board of Elections Chair Phil Lehman and Director Derek Bowens outlined COVID-19 social-distancing layouts, 17 days of early voting across 14 sites, poll-worker recruitment, and state/federal election funding ($277,268 under HB 1169 and up to $250,000 in HAVA reimbursements).

agenda_items.title: Community Health Ambassadors Program ($318,244 — Split Vote 4-1)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Recovery and Renewal Task Force Co-Chair Katie Galbraith and Ryan Smith requested $318,244 for the Community Health Ambassadors Program deploying trusted Black and Latinx outreach workers to businesses. After voting 5-0 to extend the meeting until 11:30 p.m., the board split 4-1 to allocate $318,244 from the COVID set-aside (directing staff to shift $89,000 to CRF if eligible), with Jacobs, Carter, Reckhow, and Hill voting Aye and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton voting Nay over duplication and planning concerns.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Lowell Siler reported appointments to CJAC (Dawn Baxton, Melinda Thompson King), Women's Commission (Creatrice High), Homeless Services Advisory Committee (Renee Vaughn), and Library Board of Trustees (4 appointees). disagreements.issue: Community Health Ambassadors Program Funding ($318,244) — Split Vote 4-1
disagreements.summary: The board split 4-1 on allocating $318,244 from the COVID set-aside account for the Recovery and Renewal Task Force's Community Health Ambassadors Program, dividing over program duplication and uncoordinated pandemic spending.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the $318,244 allocation from COVID set-aside funds (while pursuing $89,000 in CRF reimbursement) to address urgent racial disparities and workplace/business COVID clusters.
side_a_arguments: Chair Wendy Jacobs emphasized the proposal emerged directly from minority and immigrant/refugee task force roundtables to reach Latinx and Black businesses and workers lacking resources or trusted health connections.
Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval to fund the full-year program immediately while instructing staff to offset eligible expenses with CRF funds.
disagreements.side_b_position: Opposed funding a $318,244 program perceived as duplicating existing county community health workers, masks, and PPE programs without clearer funding and coordination plans.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton questioned why the budget included $60,000 for PPE, $40,000+ for masks, and community health worker positions when the county already employed community health workers and distributed masks.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 4-1 (Jacobs, Carter, Reckhow, Hill Aye; Howerton Nay).

disagreements.issue: Using County Libraries and Piecemeal COVID Reserve Spending for HOPE Learning Centers ($405,600)
disagreements.summary: Prior to voting 5-0 for the six-week $405,600 HOPE Learning Centers allocation, commissioners debated why County libraries remained closed, whether ad-hoc reserve spending lacked a comprehensive plan, and how to guarantee seats reached the neediest students.
disagreements.side_a_position: Fund the 338 ready community seats immediately for six weeks while requiring strict outreach and data tracking for DHA, DSS, and Exceptional Children students.
side_a_arguments: Commissioner Heidi Carter argued the 338 ready seats would otherwise go to fee-paying families rather than the most vulnerable students if the county delayed.

Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow conditioned her Aye vote on immediate outreach to Durham Housing Authority and elementary schools, while Chair Wendy Jacobs questioned why county libraries could not host learning centers like Student U and the YMCA.
disagreements.side_b_position: Caution against ad-hoc spending from the shrinking COVID reserve without a comprehensive county funding strategy and full public health safeguards.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton supported the centers in principle but criticized making piecemeal funding decisions 'on the fly' without giving staff time to build a strategic plan, and pressed for Exceptional Children priority.
General Manager Joanne Pierce and library leadership cited Urban Libraries Council data and rising youth COVID cases to warn against opening libraries prematurely.
disagreements.resolution: Following partner assurances on DHA/DSS outreach and budget staff confirming COVID reserve capacity, the board approved $405,600 unanimously (5-0).

meetings.title: Joint BOCC-BOE Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the August 18, 2020 Joint Board of County Commissioners and Durham Public Schools Board of Education virtual meeting, opening with unanimous approval of the February 4 and May 19, 2020 joint minutes (5-0 BOCC; unanimous with BOE). DPS leadership briefed both boards on the launch of Plan C virtual learning, device delays tied to federal sanctions, and the urgent $3.3+ million community coalition request for HOPE Learning Centers—prompting Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow to direct County Manager Wendell Davis to assess using County libraries and staff alongside Round 2 CARES Act funds ($3.3 million county share). Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt and COO Julius Monk warned that USDA summer meal waivers would expire September 1, leaving pre-K/non-DPS and delivery gaps ahead of a proposed home-delivery contract. Both boards also reviewed Northern High School and Elementary School C construction timelines, a $3.8 million DPS COVID-19 budget gap covered from fund balance, and pre-K slot reductions alongside threats to local childcare providers, before hearing public comments backing HOPE Centers and adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval of February 4 and May 19, 2020 Joint Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs added a Durham Pre-K update before future meeting dates, and both boards voted unanimously (5-0 BOCC and unanimous BOE) by roll-call voice vote to approve the February 4 and May 19, 2020 joint meeting minutes.

agenda_items.title: Update on DPS Virtual Learning, Device Deployment, and HOPE Learning Centers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Deputy Superintendent Nakia Hardy and COO Julius Monk outlined Plan C synchronous schedules, FHI 360 social-emotional supports, Lenovo Chromebook delays caused by U.S. sanctions, and community-led HOPE Learning Centers aiming to serve 2,100+ vulnerable students. Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Reckhow expressed concern over learning loss and directed County Manager Wendell Davis to assess County libraries, staff, and Round 2 CARES Act funds ($3.3 million county share) ahead of the August 24 BOCC meeting.

agenda_items.title: School Meals and Community Food Security Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt and Dr. Monk reported that Durham Feast delivered over 500,000 meals through July 31, and warned that federal summer meal waivers expiring September 1 would restrict DPS meals to 25 school pickup sites for enrolled students only. Rewalt previewed an August 24 BOCC proposal with Food Insight Group to continue home deliveries for transportation-limited families, while BOE member Alexandra Valladares and community voices urged culturally responsive and grassroots partnerships.

agenda_items.title: Construction Update: Northern High School and Elementary School C
agenda_items.discussion_summary: New DPS Design, Construction, and Sustainability Director Frederick Davis presented renderings and schedules for Northern High School (bidding February 2021, substantial completion June 2023) and Elementary School C on Scott King Road (groundbreaking October 2020, opening August 2022, including pre-K classrooms). Chair Jacobs raised concern over NCDOT shifting off-site traffic and pedestrian safety costs onto school districts and urged close coordination so Vision Zero/Safe Routes to School safety is not compromised.

agenda_items.title: DPS FY2020–21 Budget Development and COVID-19 Fiscal Risks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS CFO Paul LeSieur and Budget Director Alex Modestou detailed state mini-budget flat pay, retirement/health cost hikes, $11.89 million in CARES Act device/connectivity funding, and a $3.8 million local COVID budget gap covered by growing fund balance from $8.3 million to ~$11 million. They warned of major risks from enrollment uncertainty, FFCRA leave without federal reimbursement, and enterprise shortfalls in Child Nutrition and Community Education as BOE members urged county help for free learning-center seats.

agenda_items.title: DPS and Durham Pre-K Enrollment Update, Future Dates, and Public Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Debbie Pittman, Suzanne Cotterman, and Linda Pell reported that social-distancing square-footage rules cut district pre-K slots, DPS waived $56,000 in first-nine-weeks Montessori/Whitted fees, and 40%–46% of licensed private childcare centers faced closure risk at half capacity. After scheduling the next joint meeting for October 20 and reading public comments urging full funding of HOPE Learning Centers, Chair Jacobs adjourned the meeting.

votes.item_title: Approval of February 4 and May 19, 2020 Joint BOCC-BOE Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: BOCC voted 5-0 Aye; DPS Board of Education members present also voted Aye unanimously.
votes.discussion_detail: Clerk Monica Toomer called the joint roll of County Commissioners and Board of Education members to approve the February 4 and May 19, 2020 minutes.

disagreements.issue: County Facility Use (Libraries) and Funding Urgency for HOPE Learning Centers
disagreements.summary: During the DPS virtual learning and budget updates, commissioners and school leaders confronted tension over whether the County could immediately open empty library facilities and commit scarce local/CARES funds for HOPE Learning Centers before September 8.
disagreements.side_a_position: Urgently assess County libraries, volunteer staff, and Round 2 CARES funds to provide free learning-center seats and digital equity for the most vulnerable students.
side_a_arguments: Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow noted the new Main Library sat empty with technology resources and directed the County Manager to return by August 24 with a facilities, staffing, and funding assessment.
BOE members (including Jovonia Lewis) stressed that 83% of DPS students are Black and brown and urged prioritizing free learning-center seats despite Community Ed shortfalls.
disagreements.side_b_position: County administration cautioned that it had not been included in initial cost projections and faced declining revenues and limited fund balance.
side_b_arguments: County Manager Wendell Davis stated County staff had not been directly involved in the HOPE Center cost numbers, noted revenue slowdowns and limited discretionary pots beyond fund balance, and committed to analyzing the $3.3 million county share of Round 2 CARES funding.
disagreements.resolution: Board directed County staff to complete a facilities, staffing, and CARES/fund-balance analysis ahead of the August 24 BOCC regular session.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Committee Meeting Aug 11, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the August 11, 2020 Joint City-County Committee virtual meeting alongside Durham Mayor Steve Schewel, Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson, Council Member DeDreana Freeman, Vice Chair James Hill, Commissioners Brenda A. Howerton and Ellen W. Reckhow, and alternate Commissioner Heidi Carter. The committee opened with an intense policy clash over the proposed Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, as Mayor Schewel and Mayor Pro Tem Johnson pressed for county participation and a three-body drafting group while Commissioner Howerton strongly opposed a two-year study lacking community vetting and Vice Chair Hill questioned excluding law enforcement from membership (with Commissioner Reckhow noting intense community pushback even to a non-voting resource panel). Once a quorum formed, the committee voted unanimously (3-0 BOCC committee; 6-0 combined) to approve the amended May 12 minutes, then received joint updates on the Small Business Recovery Fund (196 grants and $1.28 million in loans/grants across 211 businesses), the Family Justice Center's $85,508 upfit request for the former DCB building, the $1 million City-County eviction diversion partnership, feeding and homelessness programs, and the county's 4% Longtime Homeowner Tax Deferral Program.

agenda_items.title: Technical Setup and Discussion of Joint Community Safety and Wellness Task Force
agenda_items.discussion_summary: While awaiting a City quorum, Chair Jacobs reported that the BOCC remained deadlocked on the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force despite revised bylaws creating a Community Resource Panel for law enforcement and county directors. Mayor Schewel and Mayor Pro Tem Johnson urged forming a three-body drafting team and proceeding regardless, while Commissioner Howerton condemned waiting two years amid gun violence and lacking answers to her five questions, Vice Chair Hill questioned excluding law enforcement, Council Member Freeman criticized the non-collaborative rollout, and Commissioner Reckhow suggested reviewing the two-year timeline and PAC engagement.

agenda_items.title: Approval of May 12, 2020 Joint City-County Committee Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon Council Member DeDreana Freeman joining to establish a quorum, Commissioner Reckhow requested correcting the May 12 minutes where she had been mislabeled 'Council Member Reckhow.' Both delegations unanimously approved the corrected minutes by voice vote (3-0 BOCC committee; 6-0 combined).

agenda_items.title: Small Business Recovery Fund Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Economic Development staff Brian Smith and Carolina Small Business Development Fund CEO Kevin Dick reported on the $3 million joint City-County-Duke fund launched June 18, detailing 196 grants and loans across 211 small businesses in Round 1 and a July 28 Round 2 reopening. Officials discussed improvements to broaden eligibility and accelerate disbursements.

agenda_items.title: Family Justice Center (Former DCB Building) Upfit Budget Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Crisis Response Center leaders Kent Wallace-Meigs and Liz Herron, joined by Deputy Engineering Director Perry Mands, outlined co-located survivor services for the Family Justice Center in the county-owned former DCB building (valued at $1.2M building / $2M+ site). DCRC reported covering $73,604 in IT/security costs via a Governor's Crime Commission grant expiring at the end of September and requested $85,508 jointly from the City and County for interior upfits.

agenda_items.title: City-County Emergency Rental Assistance and Eviction Diversion Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Community Development Director Reginald Johnson and DSS Assistant Director Janine Gordon presented the joint eviction diversion program pairing over $1 million in City CDBG-CV funds (with zero administrative fee holdback) and $500,000 in City legal aid funds with DSS program administration. Eligible city residents under 80% AMI with COVID-19 income loss can enter via either DSS or Legal Aid for up to three continuous months and $6,000 maximum paid directly to landlords and utilities.

agenda_items.title: City-County Feeding and Homeless Programs Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt and City Homeless Systems Manager Colin Davis briefed the committee on Durham Feast (>500,000 meals through July 31), COVID-positive family deliveries, senior/Latinx contracts, 611+ volunteers, the newly established county food security coordinator position, and non-congregate shelter coordination ahead of HUD Round 2 consolidated plan amendments.

agenda_items.title: Longtime Homeowner Tax Deferral Program Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administrator Dwane Brinson presented the county's newly approved Longtime Homeowner Tax Deferral Repayment Plan capping property tax payments at 4% of income for homeowners under age 65 earning <=30% AMI with 10+ years of ownership, alongside the new online Property Tax Assistance Evaluator, Community Land Trust tax options, and home-repair concepts. Mayor Schewel, Mayor Pro Tem Johnson, and Council Member Freeman welcomed the program—asking Brinson to present to City Council and model 60% AMI and 2% scenarios—while commissioners noted they were exploring private donation check-offs and nonprofit financial counseling.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 12, 2020 Joint City-County Committee Minutes (as Corrected)
votes.notes: BOCC committee voting members Howerton, Reckhow, and Jacobs voted Aye (3-0; alternate Heidi Carter also voiced Aye, and City Council members DeDreana Freeman, Steve Schewel, and Jillian Johnson voted Aye for a combined 6-0 committee approval).
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the May 12, 2020 minutes after correcting a reference that misidentified Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow as a Council Member.

disagreements.issue: Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Bylaws, Law Enforcement Role, and Inter-Board Process
disagreements.summary: City and County elected officials clashed sharply over the proposed 24-month Community Safety and Wellness Task Force—dividing over whether it delayed urgent anti-violence action, whether law enforcement should be excluded from voting membership, and whether the rollout respected county partners.
disagreements.side_a_position: Advance a 24-month community-driven task force without law enforcement or staff as voting members (using a separate Community Resource Panel instead) and form a three-body drafting team to finalize bylaws.
side_a_arguments: Mayor Steve Schewel and Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson argued the task force was community-initiated and designed for ongoing engagement alongside immediate crisis-response audits rather than delaying action for two years, and endorsed Commissioner Reckhow's Community Resource Panel compromise to keep voting seats community-only.
Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Heidi Carter favored county participation, though Jacobs acknowledged the board lacked consensus.
disagreements.side_b_position: Withhold county endorsement until urgent action, genuine community vetting, answers to commissioner questions, and proper respect for law enforcement and county process are addressed.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton—citing the loss of two sons to gun violence—rejected waiting two years for 'more talking and analysis,' objected that five questions she posed remained unanswered and that the city 'threw' a pre-packaged plan at the county, and argued it was not broadly community-vetted.

Vice Chair James Hill questioned why excluding the Police Chief and Sheriff from the panel was a dealbreaker given their professionalism in Durham; Council Member DeDreana Freeman agreed the rollout bypassed county committees and felt disrespectful.

Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow expressed concern after receiving dozens of emails opposing even law enforcement presence on the non-voting resource panel, leaving her unwilling to force a split county vote without adjusting the timeline and engaging PACs.
disagreements.resolution: No committee vote was taken on the task force; Chair Jacobs agreed to circulate an email seeking a commissioner liaison to meet with Mayor Pro Tem Johnson and a school board representative to see if bylaw revisions could resolve the impasse.

meetings.title: August 10, 2020 BOCC Regular Session Virtual Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the August 10, 2020 virtual BOCC regular session (recorded offline due to a Biamp failure), opening with Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's tribute to Rep. John Lewis and Rev. C.T. Vivian, census mobilization remarks, and unanimous approval (5-0) of four sets of minutes. Commissioners adopted four memorial resolutions honoring Mary Ann Black, Andrea Lynette Harris, Kenneth William Edmonds, and Raymond Eurquhart, celebrated a NACo Achievement Award for DSS/IS&T predictive foster-care analytics, and approved the consent agenda 5-0—including the Longtime Homeowner Tax Deferral Program, Geer Street Cemetery archaeological grant support, and $95,000 for the Back on the Bull campaign after Howerton pressed for M/WBE vendor tracking. Following COVID-19 and Planning Commission updates, the board debated revised Joint Community Safety and Wellness Task Force bylaws, reaching a consensus impasse without a vote as Sheriff Clarence Birkhead, Commissioner Howerton, and Vice Chair James Hill opposed creating a new 24-month task force while Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Heidi Carter favored it (and Commissioner Reckhow raised alarm over emails opposing police in the room). After entering closed session (5-0), the board reconvened and voted unanimously (5-0) to remove and relocate the Confederate monument base to an undisclosed location for public safety and preservation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Census Update, Civil Rights Tribute, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff announced the meeting was being recorded for next-day upload due to a Biamp technical failure, after which Chair Jacobs led the Pledge of Allegiance and discussed mobilizing for the shortened September 30 census deadline (with Durham at 57.7% response). Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton read an A. Philip Randolph Institute tribute to John Lewis and Rev. C.T. Vivian, and the board voted 5-0 to approve four sets of May–June minutes.

agenda_items.title: Memorial Resolutions (Black, Harris, Edmonds, Eurquhart) and NACo Award Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners Reckhow, Howerton, Hill, and Carter read memorial resolutions honoring the lives and legacies of former BOCC Chair and Rep. Mary Ann Black, NCIMED founder Andrea Lynette Harris, Carolina Times publisher Kenneth William Edmonds, and activist/Soil & Water supervisor Raymond Eurquhart. At 00:41:39, DSS Director Ben Rose and IS&T staff were recognized for winning a 2020 NACo Achievement Award for predictive foster-care analytics.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Tax Deferral Program, Back on the Bull, and Geer Street Cemetery)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed the Longtime Homeowner Tax Deferral Program (Item 20-0397) with Tax Administrator Dwane Brinson—discussing financial counseling and a tax-bill check-off fund—and heard from Tom Miller regarding Item 20-0410 supporting Friends of Geer Cemetery's archaeological survey grant. After Commissioner Howerton objected that the $95,000 Back on the Bull media allocation lacked explicit M/WBE contract requirements, staff agreed to report contract vendor details and the board approved the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Health COVID-19 Update and Planning Commission Annual Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported active COVID-19 cases dropping below 400 (to 345, with 79 total deaths) while noting disproportionate Latinx construction-sector cases. Planning staff and Planning Commission representatives then presented the Planning Commission's annual report and attendance records.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Revised Bylaws
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed revised task force bylaws adding a Community Resource Panel of agency and law-enforcement heads and narrowing the county's five appointees to specific boards. Sheriff Clarence Birkhead, Commissioner Howerton, and Vice Chair Hill opposed forming another 24-month study during a spike in gun homicides, Commissioner Reckhow voiced concern over intense emails rejecting police even on the resource panel, and Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Carter defended the task force; the board reached a consensus impasse without a vote.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Action to Remove/Relocate Confederate Monument Base
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to adjourn into closed session under G.S. 143-318.11(a)(5) and (a)(3) for property/employment negotiations and attorney-client consultation. Reconvening at 02:45:10, commissioners voted unanimously (5-0) to remove and/or relocate the Confederate monument base to an undisclosed location to address public safety concerns and preserve the base until further action, before adjourning.

disagreements.meeting_title: August 10, 2020 BOCC Regular Session Virtual Meeting
disagreements.issue: M/WBE Contracting Commitment on $95,000 'Back on the Bull' Communications Budget Amendment
disagreements.summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton questioned the $264,195 project chart versus the $95,000 consent item and objected that no explicit M/WBE vendor participation requirement appeared in the agenda documentation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require documented M/WBE vendor participation commitments before approving communications funding.
side_a_arguments: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton argued the board committed to M/WBE participation across county contracts and saw no contractual language ensuring African American and minority vendors were hired.
disagreements.side_b_position: Approve the time-sensitive $95,000 budget amendment for Phases 2 and 3 media buys while directing staff to track and report M/WBE vendor contracting.
side_b_arguments: Chair Wendy Jacobs and General Manager Jodi Miller noted 57% of planned buys targeted Latinx media and that no vendor contracts were attached yet to the planning budget amendment.
Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow proposed approving the amendment while instructing staff to push for minority vendors and report back on actual contracts.
disagreements.resolution: Staff agreed to convey the board's M/WBE expectation and report back on actual media contracts, and the consent agenda passed 5-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: August 10, 2020 BOCC Regular Session Virtual Meeting
disagreements.issue: Impasse Over Revised Bylaws for the Joint Community Safety and Wellness Task Force
disagreements.summary: The board deadlocked without a vote on revised bylaws for the Joint Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, splitting over whether a 24-month body duplicated existing agencies during a homicide crisis and whether excluding law enforcement from voting seats—or even the resource room—undermined collaboration.
disagreements.side_a_position: Form the joint task force with the City and School Board using the revised bylaws and Community Resource Panel to engage residents on non-law-enforcement crisis and violence-prevention solutions.
side_a_arguments: Chair Wendy Jacobs argued residents amid the Black Lives Matter movement were clamoring for a community-led voice and suggested shortening the two-year timeline.

Commissioner Heidi Carter warned that county services (public health, CJRC, JCPC, EMS) were central to the work and expressed concern about the county sitting out while City Council and BOE moved ahead.
disagreements.side_b_position: Opposed creating a new 24-month task force that duplicates existing work, diverts exhausted staff, and faced community backlash over law enforcement involvement.
side_b_arguments: Sheriff Clarence Birkhead opposed the task force as a 'waste of time and a waste of resources' repeating prior reports while three homicides occurred in a single day, urging synergy with CJRC and existing community groups.

Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton refused to wait two years while Black and brown children were dying in the streets, argued the plan lacked broad community vetting and diverted 24/7 pandemic staff, and Vice Chair James Hill concurred.

Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow stated she had sought a 'big tent' compromise with the Community Resource Panel, but was sobered by an avalanche of community emails rejecting even police and sheriff participation in the room, concluding the board should not force a split vote.
disagreements.resolution: Chair Jacobs concluded the board had reached an impasse with no vote taken, deferring an update to the August 11 Joint City-County Committee meeting.

meetings.title: July 13, 2020 BOCC Regular Session Virtual Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the July 13, 2020 virtual regular session with all five commissioners present. The board unanimously approved its May 26, 2020 minutes (5-0), the consent agenda excluding pulled Item 20-0309 (5-0), and five land-use items: the South Miami Boulevard/Bruntland Road rezoning (20-0317, 5-0), Historic Properties Local Review Criteria updates (5-0), Neighborhood Protection Overlay revisions (20-0318, 5-0), Affordable Housing Dwelling Unit definition revisions (20-0319, 5-0), and UDO Omnibus 14 changes (20-0320, 5-0). On the Stormwater Utility Fee budget implementation item (20-0309) and the revised Stormwater Utility Ordinance, Chair Wendy Jacobs dissented over insufficient non-digital outreach and fees on 125 agricultural parcels, with both passing 4-1 (Ayes: Heidi Carter, James Hill, Ellen W. Reckhow, Brenda A. Howerton; Nay: Wendy Jacobs). Commissioners postponed action on the Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force bylaws to the August work session after Vice Chair James Hill demanded voting seats for the Sheriff and Police Chief and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton cited late receipt of revised drafts, while later voting 4-1 to extend the meeting past 11:00 p.m. (Ayes: Brenda A. Howerton, James Hill, Ellen W. Reckhow, Wendy Jacobs; Nay: Heidi Carter) before entering a closed session on opioid litigation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Public Comments, and Approval of May 26, 2020 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the virtual meeting, read the public charge, and shared announcements on nonprofit mask distribution (over 40,000 distributed and 60,000 more available), the 'I Voted' sticker contest, and the Get Back on the Bull campaign. Clerk Monica Toomer read submitted public comments urging redistribution of School Resource Officer funds and adoption of the Community Safety and Wellness Task Force bylaws without law enforcement members. The board unanimously approved the May 26, 2020 minutes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Pulled Item 20-0309)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs pulled Item 20-0309 (Stormwater Utility Fee) for discussion after the stormwater presentation and led review of consent items including the Durham Crisis Response Center / Family Justice Center lease (20-0308, building valued over $1.2 million), detention center window replacements for suicide prevention (20-0311), Vazquez/Elna Media translation and language-equity planning (20-0330), DDI (20-0331), and the Chamber of Commerce economic development contract (20-0332). Staff clarified safety rationale on the jail windows and committed to returning with a translation pilot proposal.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 20-0317 — Zoning Map Change (2622 S. Miami Blvd & 2120 Bruntland Rd)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Jamie Sunyak presented applicant Brian Harris's request to rezone approximately seven acres at 2622 South Miami Boulevard and 2120 Bruntland Road from Industrial Light, Commercial Neighborhood, and RS-20 to Industrial Light, noting the Planning Commission's 10-0 recommendation of consistency. With no public speakers signed up or on the line, the board unanimously adopted the consistency statement and zoning map amendment.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Historic Properties Local Review Criteria Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Item 20-0318 experienced audio feedback issues and was temporarily bypassed, Planner Carla Rosenberg presented two-year updates to the Historic Properties Local Review Criteria, noting City Council's June 15 approval reversing tree-removal allowances for solar installations while the Environmental Affairs Board conducts a one-year review. Commissioners unanimously adopted the revised criteria.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 20-0318 — UDO Text Amendment, Neighborhood Protection Overlay Revisions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Michael Stock (relayed by phone through Sarah Young) presented revisions to NPO procedures in Articles 2 and 4 reflecting new state law requiring property-owner or governing-body permission for downzoning, and gave an update on the Forest Hills NPO application. Following an unopposed public hearing, the board unanimously adopted the consistency statement and UDO amendment.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 20-0319 — UDO Text Amendment, Affordable Housing Dwelling Unit Definition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented UDO revisions to Article 17 updating the Affordable Housing Dwelling Unit definition and addressing Planning Commission member Tom Miller's feedback prior to City Council adoption. With no public comment, commissioners unanimously adopted the consistency statement and ordinance amendment.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 20-0320 — UDO Text Amendment, Omnibus Changes 14
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented Omnibus Changes 14 incorporating minor revisions across UDO Articles 1–10, 12, and 14–17. After closing the unopposed public hearing, the board unanimously approved the consistency statement and amending ordinance.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Public Health Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported 4,651 cumulative Durham COVID-19 cases (515 active, 4,063 inactive, 72 deaths) with a 7-day moving average declining to 64 and Latinx share of July cases dropping from 76.8% in June to roughly 50%, while zip code 27704 remained highest at 20.88 per 1,000 residents. He highlighted the new Duke/county testing site at Holton Recreation Center, state orders requiring negative-test reporting, and preparation for school reopening.

agenda_items.title: Update on County Food Security Coordinator Position and BOCC Directives
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt outlined plans to reclassify a vacant county FTE into a County Food Security Coordinator position, form a cross-departmental County Food Security Team, and develop a food policy network and food security plan. Chair Jacobs and Chief of Staff Drew Cummings also discussed SharePoint glitches affecting access to post-February BOCC directives.

agenda_items.title: Stormwater Utility Outreach Update, Pulled Item 20-0309, and Stormwater Utility Ordinance
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Stormwater Manager Ryan Eads, McKenzie Myers, and consultant Inga Kennedy presented virtual outreach results and the three-tier residential fee structure ($12/$24/$48 based on a 4,300-square-foot ERU) plus non-residential ERU billing for unincorporated properties to fund Falls Lake and Jordan Lake compliance. Chair Wendy Jacobs objected to taxing 125 non-residential agricultural parcels (~$40,000 total) before establishing BMP credits or conducting non-digital mail/in-person farm outreach and voted against both Pulled Item 20-0309 and the later Stormwater Utility Ordinance, which each passed 4-1.

agenda_items.title: Discussion on Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Bylaws
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Jodi Miller shared Criminal Justice Advisory Committee feedback, and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow presented compromise bylaws developed with Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson dedicating four county seats to representatives from existing health, sheriff advisory, CJAC, and JCPC boards while placing the Sheriff, Police Chief, DA, and Superintendent on a non-voting Community Resource Panel. Commissioner Heidi Carter urged immediate passage, but Vice Chair James Hill insisted the Sheriff and Police Chief be voting task force members and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton cited unreadiness due to late draft changes, leading the board to delay action to the August work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Deferred to August work session (no formal vote)

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Closed Session (AmerisourceBergen Litigation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler announced appointment results for the ABC Board, Board of Adjustment, CJAC, DSS Board, Durham Convention Center Authority, and Women's Commission. Following a request to add active litigation (Durham County v. AmerisourceBergen, 1:19-cv-00491) under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3), the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session and 4-1 (Carter opposed) to extend the meeting until 11:30 p.m., returning at 04:16:05 to adjourn.
