disagreements.meeting_title: July 13, 2020 BOCC Regular Session Virtual Meeting
disagreements.issue: Stormwater Utility Fee Non-Residential Agricultural Parcels and Pandemic Outreach
disagreements.summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs sought to delay adoption of the Stormwater Utility Ordinance and Pulled Item 20-0309 until August to address non-digital outreach and agricultural BMP credits for 125 non-residential farm parcels, while the remaining four commissioners voted 4-1 to enact the fee immediately.
disagreements.side_a_position: Delay implementation of the non-residential stormwater fee until August to conduct mail/non-virtual farmer outreach and offset the ~$40,000 impact on 125 agricultural parcels with BMP credits.
side_a_arguments: Many farmers do not use computers or Zoom and could not participate in virtual outreach while in-person Farm Bureau and Ruritan meetings were suspended due to COVID-19.
Charging agricultural properties that already implement water-quality BMPs contradicts county farmland preservation programs.
disagreements.side_b_position: Enact the Stormwater Utility Ordinance and accompanying budget item now while developing a future credit program and mailed tax-bill outreach.
side_b_arguments: Exempting one landowner class poses legal equity risks and shifts compliance costs onto residential ratepayers, while the fee is already baked into the adopted FY21 budget.
Staff noted 499 of 624 agricultural parcels already pay only residential rates (capped at $48/year) and the remaining 125 parcels have a median fee of $120/year.
disagreements.resolution: Both Pulled Item 20-0309 and the Stormwater Utility Ordinance passed 4-1, with staff directed to return with a credit structure proposal and continue mailed/direct outreach.

disagreements.meeting_title: July 13, 2020 BOCC Regular Session Virtual Meeting
disagreements.issue: Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Bylaws and Law Enforcement Membership
disagreements.summary: Commissioners split over whether to immediately adopt compromise bylaws placing the Sheriff and Police Chief on a non-voting Community Resource Panel or postpone action to resolve demands for voting law enforcement seats and late draft circulation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the revised bylaws immediately, keeping the task force strictly community-led with non-police solutions while engaging the Sheriff and Police Chief on the advisory Resource Panel.
side_a_arguments: Over 100 community residents urged prompt passage aligned with the Beyond Policing report and prior City Council and School Board approvals.
City Council would not approve voting seats for law enforcement on a community task force designed to evaluate alternatives to policing.
disagreements.side_b_position: Postpone approval to the August work session; add the Sheriff and Police Chief as voting members (Hill) or allow adequate time to review late bylaw revisions (Howerton).
side_b_arguments: Vice Chair James Hill stated excluding Durham's African American Sheriff and Police Chief from voting membership was unreasonable and said he would vote No unless they were added.

Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton stated she was unready to vote because revised drafts were emailed too close to the meeting, and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow agreed to pause two weeks rather than split along racial lines over the two African American members' objections.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; Chair Jacobs deferred the bylaws to the August work session.

meetings.title: Durham County Government BOCC Live
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the June 22, 2020 regular session (streamed/archived June 23, 2020) with all five commissioners present, and every formal vote passed unanimously 5-0. The board approved April 27 and May 11, 2020 minutes (5-0), adopted consent agenda items 20-0260 through 20-0299 (5-0) after reviewing pulled items on Wellpath jail healthcare and universal COVID-19 testing, the Sheriff's firing range architectural contract, tax refunds, and a $1.5 million health-benefit fund balance safeguard, and approved a $925,000 performance-based economic incentive for GRAIL, Inc. (5-0). Commissioners also voted 5-0 to commit $1,000,000 to join the City of Durham's Small Business Recovery Fund administered by Carolina Small Business Development Fund, approved a $60,000 match for a $300,000 federal EDA CARES Act grant for the Bulls Initiative Biowork expansion (5-0), adopted the revised FY 2021–2030 Capital Improvement Plan while urging the Museum of Life and Science to increase private fundraising (5-0), and authorized staff to negotiate homeless-housing RFP contracts ahead of the July 8 Marriott RTP expiration (5-0). Following brief discussion of the Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force bylaws—where Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and Sheriff Clarence Birkhead objected to excluding public safety voices and framing county programs negatively—the board deferred the task force item to July 13, approved CARES Act fair-share advocacy letters (5-0), announced 15 boards/commissions appointments, extended the meeting to 11:30 p.m. (5-0), and entered closed session (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment (Juneteenth), Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the virtual meeting, added a brief discussion on making Juneteenth a county employee holiday at Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's request, and shared announcements on gardening kits. Commissioners unanimously approved the April 27 and May 11, 2020 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Discussion and Approval (Items 20-0260 through 20-0299)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners pulled and examined Item 20-0271 (May 2020 tax releases/refunds district codes), Item 20-0272 (DSS/DFI scope revisions), Item 20-0273 (Wellpath jail medical contract, where Heidi Carter and Ellen W. Reckhow pressed for regular/universal COVID-19 testing in the Detention Center and staff were directed to bring back testing options by July 13), Item 20-0275 (firing range drainage/pre-design vs Northern Durham campus classrooms), and Item 20-0291 ($1.5M fund balance transfer safeguard for Cigna health claims). The board unanimously approved the consent agenda, also recognizing the GoTriangle appointment of Stephanie Williams following Reckhow's decades of transit service.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Paid Juneteenth Holiday for County Employees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton urged the board to consider making Juneteenth a paid holiday for Durham County employees starting in 2021. Chair Jacobs supported placing the item on the September work session agenda for staff and Racial Equity Officer Quillie Rashid-Henry to develop proposals.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Incentive for GRAIL, Inc.
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Officer Andy Miracle presented a $925,000 performance-based award over seven years for GRAIL, Inc. to establish a cancer-screening lab creating 739 jobs and $111 million in capital investment, supported by a state JDIG award. GRAIL representative Michael Myers and Greater Durham Chamber VP Joshua Gunn supported the project, and commissioners amended the motion to bind the briefing paper's workforce-pipeline commitments into the contract.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Public Health Update and County Reopening / Travel Guidelines
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported 3,267 cumulative Durham cases, 62 deaths, and 548 active cases, with 79.5% of June cases in the Latinx community and 16% under age 18, alongside an expected $1.296M DHHS grant and expanded testing at Holton Rec Center and El Centro Hispano. Staff then reviewed internal COVID-19 reopening protocols covering social distancing cohorts, mandatory face coverings, HVAC fresh-air optimization, sanitation, and temporary employee travel/high-risk activity guidelines.

agenda_items.title: Durham Small Business Recovery Fund ($1,000,000 Allocation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Andy Miracle and Carolina Small Business Development Fund CEO Kevin Dick compared partnering with the City/Duke Small Business Recovery Fund (3% interest, 10-year term, no personal guarantee/collateral, <=25 FTEs) against the NC Rural Center loan fund (5%, 5-year, personal guarantee). Despite legal/finance staff cautioning about unsecured loans, commissioners voted unanimously to join the unified City/Duke fund via CSBDF to maximize simplicity and equitable access.

agenda_items.title: Bulls Initiative Update and $60,000 EDA CARES Act Grant Match
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Andy Miracle and Casey Steinbacher presented an 80/20 federal EDA CARES Act grant opportunity for $300,000 in modular aseptic lab equipment to relocate and triple capacity of Durham Tech's Biowork certificate program from Northern Durham to a transit-accessible site. Commissioners unanimously approved the required $60,000 county match while urging increased private biotech sector contributions.

agenda_items.title: Revised FY 2021–2030 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Keith Lane and staff answered follow-up questions on Administration Building 1 HVAC/renovations (floors 2–3), Museum of Life and Science ($36 million in planned requests), Youth Home state partnership talks, and Alliance Behavioral Health space modifications. Commissioners unanimously approved the revised CIP with an added directive encouraging the Museum of Life and Science to step up private fundraising, and tabled Admin Building 1 Phases 3–5 pricing with Robert Sattel to a later date.

agenda_items.title: Homeless Housing Proposals During COVID-19 (Post-Marriott RTP Contract)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Drew Cummings reported that the Marriott RTP shelter contract expires July 8 and Urban Ministries can only reoccupy at half capacity, prompting an RFP that drew three bids: a flexible short-term hotel option and two community-based organization proposals offering permanent homeless-system capacity and potential COVID-positive quarantine beds. The board unanimously authorized staff to negotiate with the bidders and return by July 13 or an earlier special meeting.

agenda_items.title: Discussion on Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners briefly discussed the proposed task force bylaws ahead of a fuller July 13 debate. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow criticized the lack of prior Joint City-County Committee vetting and the bylaws' narrow focus on shortcomings rather than Durham's nationally recognized Stepping Up, CJRC, and specialty court programs, while Sheriff Clarence Birkhead objected that public safety had no representation on the task force.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments, CARES Act Letters, Meeting Extension, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Attorney Lowell Siler announced appointments across 15 boards and commissions (with one Women's Commission seat and CJAC business slot needing re-advertisement/follow-up). The board unanimously approved CARES Act fair-share advocacy letters drafted by Deborah Craig-Ray, voted 5-0 to extend the meeting to 11:30 p.m., and entered closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(3) before adjourning at 04:53:10.

votes.item_title: Approval of April 27 and May 11, 2020 Regular Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes of both spring regular sessions after confirming Commissioner Howerton's aye by phone.

votes.item_title: Approval of $925,000 Economic Development Incentive Agreement with GRAIL, Inc.
votes.discussion_detail: Amended motion by Reckhow (originally seconded before amendment; amended motion seconded by Hill) authorizing a $925,000 seven-year incentive tied to $111M investment and 739 jobs, incorporating briefing-sheet workforce commitments.

votes.item_title: Approval of $1,000,000 County Participation in City/Duke Small Business Recovery Fund

disagreements.issue: Joint Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Bylaws and Representation
disagreements.summary: During preliminary review ahead of the July 13 vote, commissioners and Sheriff Clarence Birkhead diverged over whether the City-drafted bylaws fairly involved county leadership, acknowledged existing county criminal justice programs, and included public safety officials.
disagreements.side_a_position: Advance the community-led task force promptly in alignment with City Council and School Board expectations, keeping elected officials and department heads off the voting body.
side_a_arguments: Commissioners Heidi Carter and Wendy Jacobs cited strong public demand and noted the task force was modeled like the Pre-K task force to comprise community representatives rather than elected or department leaders.
Chair Jacobs noted Mayor Pro Tem Jillian Johnson welcomed county bylaw revisions and proposed a joint briefing on existing county programs.
disagreements.side_b_position: Revise the bylaws before approval to ensure equal county partnership, reflect existing county criminal justice successes, and give public safety officials a voice.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow objected that the City bypassed the Joint City-County Committee and wrote bylaws focusing on perceived gaps while ignoring Durham's CJRC, Stepping Up initiative, mental health court, and reduced jail population.
Sheriff Clarence Birkhead objected that a public safety task force excluded public safety representation.
disagreements.resolution: Continued to the July 13, 2020 meeting for bylaw revisions and fuller debate.

meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the June 8, 2020 regular session (streamed/archived June 9, 2020) with all five commissioners participating. The board unanimously approved its March 2, 2020 work session minutes (5-0), proclaimed World Sickle Cell Awareness Day, adopted/presented the Resolution Declaring Racism as a Public Health Crisis brought by Dr. Wanda Boone, recognized a $50,000 RTP Foundation donation to the EOC, and passed the consent agenda (5-0). On the FY 2020–2021 budget, Commissioner Heidi Carter's motion (seconded by Chair Wendy Jacobs) to pull $3.8 million from reserves/fund balance to immediately fund a $15/hour minimum wage for all Durham Public Schools classified staff failed 2-3 (Ayes: Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs; Nays: James Hill, Ellen W. Reckhow, Brenda A. Howerton); after unanimously adding $42,714 for a state-matched Cooperative Extension agricultural agent (5-0), the board passed the amended FY 2020–2021 budget ordinance 3-2 (Ayes: Brenda A. Howerton, Ellen W. Reckhow, James Hill; Nays: Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs). Commissioners also unanimously approved the $5.48 million Durham County Coronavirus Relief Fund (CRF) plan for submission to NC PRO (5-0), reviewed the revised FY 2021–2030 Capital Improvement Plan ahead of a June 22 vote, and received a COVID-19 public health update.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of March 2, 2020 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the virtual meeting and shared announcements regarding COVID-19 volunteer opportunities (Feed Durham, Durham FEAST), free tax preparation at Northgate Mall, and Census response (55.5%). The board unanimously approved the March 2, 2020 work session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: 11th Anniversary of World Sickle Cell Awareness Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill read the proclamation designating June 19, 2020 as World Sickle Cell Awareness Day, and Duke Sickle Cell Program educator Tiffany Bell discussed the disproportionate impact of COVID-19 and healthcare disparities on Black men and sickle cell patients.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Declaring Racism as a Public Health Crisis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read the resolution authored with Dr. Wanda Boone (Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People), Racial Equity Officer Quillie Rashid-Henry, and Public Health Director Rod Jenkins declaring racism a public health crisis and committing to eight anti-racism policy, training, and reporting actions. Commissioners, Dr. Boone, Rashid-Henry, and Jenkins spoke strongly in support; Chair Jacobs also read letters from the Confederate Monuments Commission co-chairs and Mayor Steve Schewel urging action on the remaining Confederate monument base, prompting Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton to object to raising the monument when the County Attorney advised holding off.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of $50,000 RTP Foundation Donation and Consent Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board recognized the Research Triangle Foundation for contributing $50,000 and coordinating $17,000 in lunches for Emergency Operations Center frontline workers. Commissioners then unanimously approved the consent agenda without pulling any items.

agenda_items.title: Adoption of FY 2020–2021 Budget Ordinance (DPS $15/hr Classified Staff Amendment & Cooperative Extension Position)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter moved (seconded by Chair Wendy Jacobs) to appropriate $3.8 million from fund balance/COVID reserves to fully implement a $15/hour minimum wage for all DPS classified staff in FY21; the motion failed 2-3 after Reckhow, Howerton, and Hill argued the board already added ~$1.9M–$2M by trimming Sheriff positions/vehicles and could not further deplete reserves amid severe pandemic revenue uncertainty and a $2.5M sales-tax split loss. The board unanimously added $42,714 (matched 40% by NC State) for a Cooperative Extension agricultural position (5-0), debated legal limits on countywide property tax relief under the Machinery Act, and adopted the amended FY 2020–2021 Budget Ordinance by a 3-2 vote (Carter and Jacobs opposed).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Amendment Failed 2-3; Extension Position Passed 5-0; Budget Ordinance Passed 3-2

agenda_items.title: Durham County Coronavirus Relief Fund (CRF) Plan ($5.48 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Jodi Miller presented the county's $5.48 million CARES Act CRF spending plan due to NC PRO by June 15, 2020, structured under updated state guidance to pursue 75%/25% FEMA/state reimbursement first while applying CRF funds to testing/Panther lab upgrades ($60k), direct public health expenses ($1.43M), public safety base/hazard payroll, and homeless/senior wraparound support ($2.17M). agenda_items.discussion_summary: Budget Director Keith Lane presented major CIP revisions including a $162.5M increase for Durham Public Schools (projected to require a 2-cent tax increase in FY 2022–23), deferring half the Public Safety Complex, Youth Home bed-count expansion, Snow Hill pump station escalation ($13M to $19.6M), Admin Building 1 renovations ($11M vs $8M scaled back), and $36M in Museum of Life and Science requests. votes.discussion_detail: Allocated $42,714 from General Fund fund balance to fund 60% of a permanent Cooperative Extension agricultural agent supporting small/emerging farmers and hemp growers, matched 40% by NC State.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved submission of the $5.48M CRF spending plan to NC PRO ahead of the June 15, 2020 deadline.

disagreements.issue: Full Immediate Funding ($3.8M) for DPS Classified Staff $15/Hour Minimum Wage and FY 2020–2021 Budget Adoption
disagreements.summary: The board split 2-3 on appropriating $3.8 million from reserves to immediately pay all DPS classified staff $15/hour, and subsequently split 3-2 on adopting the final FY 2020–2021 budget ordinance.
disagreements.side_a_position: Fully fund the $15/hour living wage for all DPS classified staff in FY 2020–2021 now using fund balance/COVID reserves, and reject a budget that leaves those workers below $15/hour.
side_a_arguments: DPS bus drivers, custodians, and cafeteria workers—overwhelmingly Black and brown essential workers—were the only remaining county/city public employees below $15/hour.

With $3.5M remaining in the COVID set-aside, $4.6M in economic uncertainty reserves, and expected FEMA/CARES reimbursements for the $3.67M fund balance spend, the county could fund the $3.8M gap immediately.
disagreements.side_b_position: Limit DPS classified wage increases to the ~$1.9M down payment in the FY21 budget, preserve reserves against pandemic uncertainty, and revisit full funding in January 2021.
side_b_arguments: Commissioners already redirected ~$2M (including $1.25M from Sheriff detention vacancies and vehicles) on top of the manager's $5M DPS increase after DPS's estimate jumped from $1.7M–$1.8M to $3.8M.

County Manager Wendell Davis warned COVID costs already exceeded $7M and DHHS was demanding 10x testing expansion, while the city's sales-tax split change cost the county ~$2.5M and DPS held an $8M fund balance.
disagreements.resolution: Carter's $3.8M amendment failed 2-3, and the amended FY 2020–2021 budget ordinance passed 3-2 with Carter and Jacobs dissenting.

disagreements.issue: Design and City Cost-Sharing of Countywide Property Tax Assistance Program
disagreements.summary: Ahead of the budget vote, commissioners differed over whether the July 13 property tax relief proposal should focus strictly on long-term low-income homeowners alongside a binding City match, or explore broader legally permissible COVID-19 options.
disagreements.side_a_position: Bring forward a model countywide tax assistance program targeting long-term low-income homeowners in time for FY21 tax bills, meeting directly with advocacy groups.
side_a_arguments: Commissioner Heidi Carter emphasized helping long-term low-income homeowners stay in their homes and partnering with the City of Durham.
Chair Wendy Jacobs supported consulting community affordable-housing advocates while also addressing COVID-related mortgage/tax hardship.
disagreements.side_b_position: Restrict options to what is legal under the NC Machinery Act, avoid non-needy recipients, and secure a firm 50%+ financial commitment from the City.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow warned the County Attorney advised outright grant programs could expose commissioners to personal liability, and Vice Chair James Hill cautioned against broad relief echoing federal PPP abuses.
Reckhow and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton noted the Mayor's letter lacked an explicit 50% funding commitment even though the City benefited from $2.5M in reallocated sales tax.
disagreements.resolution: Staff was directed to meet with community groups and present legally viable options on July 13, 2020.

disagreements.issue: Raising Confederate Monument Base Removal During Racism Resolution Discussion
disagreements.summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs read letters calling for removal of the remaining Confederate monument base as a public health hazard, while Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton objected to bringing it up when the County Attorney advised waiting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Connect the Racism as a Public Health Crisis resolution to declaring the Confederate monument base a public health and safety hazard for removal.
side_a_arguments: Confederate Monuments Commission co-chairs and Mayor Steve Schewel wrote urging BOCC to act because white supremacist symbols inflict measurable stress and harm on Black residents.
disagreements.side_b_position: Do not force the monument onto the evening's agenda against the County Attorney's advice when the urgent focus is preventing Black and brown people from being killed.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Howerton noted the board had already agreed to hold the monument off the agenda for staff legal research and urged keeping focus on immediate threats to life.
disagreements.resolution: Chair Jacobs clarified no action on the monument was on the June 8/9 agenda and moved to the next agenda item.

meetings.title: Durham County Government BOCC Live
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the May 26, 2020 virtual regular session (archived/dated May 27, 2020) with all five commissioners present, and all formal votes passed unanimously (5-0). The board approved its April 13, 2020 regular session minutes (5-0), introduced Durham County's inaugural Racial Equity Officer Quillie Rashid-Henry and Early Childhood Coordinator Kate Elander, and issued proclamations for Older Americans Month and Children's Mental Health Awareness Month. Commissioners reviewed every consent item individually—including over $5 million in post-malware IT and cybersecurity contracts, an Orange County glass-recycling interlocal agreement, and $21,525 in pooled commissioner funds for 50,000 masks—before passing the consent agenda 5-0. The board then held two public hearings under SB 704 rules (leaving comments open 24 hours without voting): one on the FY 2020–2021 County Manager's Recommended Budget featuring 29 written comments largely advocating $15/hour DPS classified wages, school interpreters, and Sheriff budget reallocations, and a second on up to $75 million in Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2020C/2020D) for the 300 E. Main St. parking deck, Snow Hill pump station, Club RTP, DTCC land, and DPS schools; following COVID-19 and malware/SAP recovery updates and board appointments, the board entered closed session (5-0) and adjourned.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of April 13, 2020 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the virtual meeting, noted absentee ballot resources at dcovote.com, and congratulated Clerk Macio Carlton on detailed April 13, 2020 minutes. The board unanimously approved the minutes.

agenda_items.title: Introductions of Racial Equity Officer and Early Childhood Coordinator; Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Joanne Pierce introduced Durham County's first Racial Equity Officer, Quillie Rashid-Henry, and Cooperative Extension Director Donna Rewalt introduced Early Childhood Coordinator Kate Elander, both board-created positions. Chair Jacobs also read proclamations for Older Americans Month (with DSS's Janine Gordon) and Children's Mental Health Awareness Month (noting Alliance Health's Tika Demson).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Item-by-Item Review and Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis walked through each consent item, including IT/cybersecurity contracts (Items 174, 179, 180, 185, 186, 225) following the March 6 malware attack, March and April tax refund reports (191, 192), City-County and Orange County recycling agreements (198, 218 — allowing curbside fee to stay flat if glass is separated at convenience sites), $52,000 for Food Security Task Force contracts (207), and $21,525 in pooled commissioner funds for 50,000 masks via Cover Durham and the Community Health Coalition (242). Commissioners unanimously approved the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2020–2021 County Manager's Recommended Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Toomer read 29 submitted public comments (with duplicates grouped and Spanish-language submissions translated), overwhelmingly from Durham Association of Educators members, teachers, parents, and People's Alliance members urging at least $8.5 million in new DPS funding, a $15/hour minimum wage for DPS classified workers, additional school interpreters, eviction diversion, property tax relief, and reallocating $1.5M for Sheriff vehicles and unspent jail mental-health pod funds. Per SB 704, the hearing remained open for written comments for 24 hours.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Not to Exceed $75 Million Limited Obligation Bonds (Series 2020C & 2020D)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance Director Susan Tezai and Budget Director Keith Lane presented the $75M short-term LOBs resolution covering $15M taxable financing for the 300 E. Main St. parking deck plus tax-exempt financing for Snow Hill pump station, $20M for Club RTP, $2.9M for a central Durham Tech land/building purchase (freeing $2.9M in pay-go reserves for COVID/economic uncertainty), and $18.5M for DPS school projects. Chair Jacobs officially opened the public hearing for 24 hours under SB 704 ahead of a June 1 vote and June 2 LGC review.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Public Health Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public Health Director Rod Jenkins reported Day 70 of EOC posture with 1,352 Durham cases, 45 deaths, and 408 active cases, highlighting a surge to 48–54% of recent cases in the Latinx community (particularly construction workers), a 1,000+-view Spanish Facebook Live event with ISLA, radio ads on La Ley and Radio One, and delays in receiving total negative-test denominators from NCDHHS.

agenda_items.title: Malware Attack Recovery and SAP Payroll Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CIO Greg Marrow reported completing P0 core IT, P1 citizen-facing, and P2 enterprise/SAP infrastructure restoration 80+ days after the March 6 malware attack, while continuing work on P3 departmental software. Finance Director Susan Tezai detailed manual processing of 2,150 handwritten AP checks, reopening SAP financials countywide, creating COVID disaster pay codes, and truing up payroll for election and part-time workers.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler announced selections for the ABC Board, Animal Welfare Advisory Committee, Board of Health, Durham Cultural Advisory Committee, Farmland Preservation Advisory Board, Industrial Facilities Authority, and Nursing Home CAC, while deferring a Women's Commission seat with only two votes. The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(5) regarding property acquisition/employment terms and returned at 03:41:46 to adjourn.

votes.discussion_detail: Unanimously approved April 13, 2020 regular session minutes.

disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the full consent agenda to fund urgent COVID-19 operations, shelter/PPE procurement, school land acquisition, and parking deck pre-construction.

disagreements.resolution: Consent agenda passed 4-1.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC February 24, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the February 24, 2020 regular session with all five commissioners present, dominated by an added public comment period and closed session regarding County Manager Wendell Davis's letter alleging racial bias and demeaning remarks by Commissioner Heidi Carter. After voting unanimously to add both a public comment period and a closed session (5-0 each), the board heard emotional testimony from community leaders—including Joshua Gunn, Omar Beasley, Edward Bell, Jackie Wagstaff, Jarvis Martin, Brian Calloway, and Dr. Lavonia Allison—demanding an independent external investigation, while Carter defended her equity and public-school advocacy. Following a 30-minute closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6) (5-0), Chair Jacobs announced the board unanimously directed the clerk to contact the NC Association of County Commissioners (NCACC), UNC School of Government, and ICMA to recommend outside legal counsel and facilitate a broad independent investigation. In the remainder of the meeting, commissioners memorialized former Commissioner Joe Bowser, honored retiring Interim EMS Director Kevin Underhill, approved December 2, 2019 minutes (5-0), reviewed property tax relief programs, approved the consent agenda (5-0) and pulled items 20-0079 and 20-0087 (5-0), and made board and commission appointments.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Agenda Adjustments (Adding Public Comment & Closed Session)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order and moved to add a closed session to the agenda, while Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton moved to add a public comment period and place it prior to the closed session so waiting citizens could address the board. Both adjustments passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Emergency Public Comment on County Manager Wendell Davis's Allegations Against Commissioner Heidi Carter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Multiple community members and leaders—including Joshua Gunn, Omar Beasley (Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People), Edward Bell, Jackie Wagstaff, Andrea 'Muffin' Hudson, Jarvis Martin, Brian Calloway, and Dr. Lavonia Allison—spoke in support of County Manager Wendell Davis following media reports of his letter alleging racial bias and mistreatment by Commissioner Heidi Carter, calling for an external objective investigation. Commissioner Carter closed the period by rejecting claims of racism, stating she would not apologize for advocating for DPS, pre-K, affordable housing, healthcare, food security, and transit alongside leaders of color.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Personnel Matter (NCGS 143-318.11(a)(6)) and Investigation Directive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session to address the confidential personnel/grievance matter. Upon returning at 01:40:49, Chair Jacobs announced the board unanimously directed the clerk to contact NCACC for outside counsel recommendations and consult UNC School of Government and ICMA regarding a broad investigation, adding that she felt badly Manager Davis was hurt while believing Carter did not intend racist statements.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Tribute to Former Commissioner Joe Bowser, and Resolution for Kevin Underhill
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs paid tribute to former Commissioner Joe Bowser (who passed away February 14, 2020), shared March 3 primary voting and Braggtown Library reopening announcements, and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow recognized Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton and Durham organizations for Think Babies NC awards. The board also presented a retirement resolution honoring Interim EMS Director Kevin Underhill's 26 years of service, including pioneering pre-hospital STEMI ECG protocols and community paramedicine.

agenda_items.title: Approval of December 2, 2019 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After briefly revisiting the skipped minutes item, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow requested a status report on directives from the December 2, 2019 work session at next week's work session and moved approval of the minutes, which passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Tax Relief Program Overview, Consent Agenda, and Pulled Items 20-0079 and 20-0087
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Tax Administrator Dwayne Brinson outlined payment coupons, delinquent payment plans, the online Property Tax Assistance Evaluator, and North Carolina's three primary relief programs (Homestead, Circuit Breaker, Disabled Veteran). The board approved consent items 20-0070 through 20-0081 (excluding 20-0079 and 20-0087) 5-0, heard public comments from Dr. Lavonia Allison and Mr. Leonard on Register of Deeds excise tax refund statute GS 105-228.37, tax revaluations, and Board of Elections voting-site statutes, and then approved items 20-0079 and 20-0087 unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Commuter Rail Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler announced appointment votes for the Board of Health (Roger McDougal, James Miller, Robert Rosenstein, Victoria Orto), Boxing and Wrestling Commission (Maya Bass), and Durham County Women's Commission (Laura Myers). Chair Jacobs noted staff would circulate a summary of strong public turnout at the weekend commuter rail open house before adjourning.

disagreements.issue: County Manager Wendell Davis's Racial Bias Allegations Against Commissioner Heidi Carter and Scope of Investigation
disagreements.summary: Public speakers, Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, and Commissioner Heidi Carter clashed over County Manager Wendell Davis's letter accusing Carter of racial bias and demeaning remarks, though all five commissioners ultimately agreed in closed session to seek an independent outside investigation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Validate the County Manager's complaint of racial bias and mistreatment by Commissioner Carter and launch a swift, impartial external investigation.
side_a_arguments: Community speakers (including Joshua Gunn, Omar Beasley, Jackie Wagstaff, and Dr. Lavonia Allison) cited Davis's seven-year exemplary audit record and accused Carter of racial insensitivity and disrespectful remarks ('you work for the board; grin and bear it').
Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton insisted on holding the public comment session before closed session so community voices would be heard.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject allegations of racist intent while agreeing to an independent outside review to address all underlying issues fairly.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Heidi Carter stated she would not apologize for advocating for DPS, pre-K, affordable housing, and transit alongside leaders of color, and joined the vote to enter closed session.
Chair Wendy Jacobs apologized that Davis's feelings were hurt while stating she did not believe Carter intended racist remarks and supporting outside counsel.
disagreements.resolution: After a 30-minute closed session, the board unanimously directed the clerk to contact NCACC for outside counsel recommendations and consult UNC School of Government and ICMA regarding a broad investigation.

meetings.title: BOCC Feb 10 2020 ENTIRE meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the February 10, 2020 regular session with all five commissioners present. The board unanimously approved its January 27, 2020 minutes (5-0) and consent agenda items 20-0032 through 20-0067 (5-0)—including $76,700 in Open Space and Trails matching grants, $2 million+ for bus stops, a revised Economic Development Incentives Policy with community benefits, a Sports Commission interlocal agreement, and $3 million in school capital reallocations. Following a public hearing, commissioners voted 5-0 to approve a $2,550,000 seven-year economic development incentive for Eli Lilly and Company's $440 million, 462-job biopharmaceutical manufacturing facility. During BOCC directives review, commissioners sparred over whether to evaluate paid employee parking in county decks as part of Transportation Demand Management, with Ellen W. Reckhow and Wendy Jacobs urging options while James Hill and Brenda A. Howerton opposed charging county workers. On the Triangle Trails Initiative resolution, the board voted 4-1 to endorse multi-county trail planning (Ayes: Heidi Carter, Ellen W. Reckhow, Wendy Jacobs, James Hill; Nay: Brenda A. Howerton, who cited unclear accountability), before entering closed session (5-0) and granting Vice Chair Hill an excused absence for March 2 (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of January 27, 2020 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting (noting building construction disrupted video livestreaming, leaving audio active), shared March 3 primary early-voting and same-day registration information, and announced a $701,101 JCPC funding RFP and Golden Leaf Award nominations. Commissioners unanimously approved the January 27, 2020 minutes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Approval (Items 20-0032 through 20-0067)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners highlighted key consent items including $76,700 in Open Space & Trails matching grants, Youth Home comprehensive center planning, expanded Veterans outreach, over $2 million for bus stop amenities, and the revised Economic Development Incentives Policy incorporating community benefits. Staff also clarified $352,000+ in annual Urban Ministries support after public comment from Mr. Chavis, reviewed the new Sports Commission interlocal agreement, and confirmed reallocating $3M from Northern High School 2016 GO bond funds would not delay Northern High or Elementary School C before approving the consent agenda 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Item 20-0065 — $2,550,000 Economic Development Incentive for Eli Lilly and Company
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Officer Andy Miracle presented a $2.55M seven-year incentive for Eli Lilly's $440 million facility creating 462 jobs (half accessible with associate/vocational degrees starting around $50,000+) and generating $5.3M in new property tax revenue over five years, plus childcare, TDM, MWBE, and second-chance hiring commitments under the new policy. Chamber representative Brian Foxx supported the grant, while CJ Broderick urged upfront anti-displacement planning; commissioners approved the incentive 5-0.

agenda_items.title: BOCC Directives Follow-Up (TDM/Paid Parking, Planning Split, Sheriff Jail Data, Sales Tax ILA)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed outstanding directives, sparking debate over Transportation Demand Management and paid employee deck parking ahead of 300/500 E. Main St. agreements, with Reckhow and Jacobs seeking options and Hill and Howerton opposing employee parking fees. Commissioners also queried Engaged Durham consultant spending, DPS pre-K Title I data, unspent Sheriff female mental health pod funds and jail data, the 70/30 city-county planning workload vs 50/50 cost split, DSS building DFI plans, the sales-tax ILA, and the 100% clean energy RFQ.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting the Triangle Trails Initiative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow presented a resolution endorsing multi-county regional greenway planning led by Chuck Flink (Greenways Inc.) using privately raised funds at no cost to Durham County, incorporating Chair Jacobs's added 'whereas' clause on commuting access and climate/carbon reduction and Heidi Carter's request for equitable engagement. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton opposed the resolution, citing insufficient background on who holds accountability, resulting in a 4-1 passage.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Excused Absence for Vice Chair James Hill
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under NCGS 143-318.11(a)(4) on economic development incentives, returned at 02:08:22, unanimously granted Vice Chair James Hill an excused absence for the March 2 work session to attend the NACo conference, and adjourned.

votes.item_title: Approval of January 27, 2020 Regular Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Unanimously approved January 27, 2020 regular session minutes.

votes.item_title: Item 20-0065 — Approval of $2,550,000 Economic Development Incentive Agreement with Eli Lilly and Company
votes.discussion_detail: Authorized manager to execute $2.55M performance-based incentive agreement with Eli Lilly tied to $440M investment and 462 jobs.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Resolution Supporting the Triangle Trails Initiative (as Amended)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted resolution supporting multi-county greenway planning led by Greenways Inc./Triangle Trails Initiative with added language on transportation equity and carbon reduction; Commissioner Howerton initially expressed indifference and then recorded a No vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn into Closed Session (NCGS 143-318.11(a)(4) — Economic Development)
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session to discuss industry expansion and economic development incentives.

votes.item_title: Excused Absence for Vice Chair James Hill from March 2, 2020 Work Session
votes.discussion_detail: Excused Vice Chair Hill from the March 2, 2020 work session to attend the NACo legislative conference.

disagreements.issue: Triangle Trails Initiative Resolution Governance and Accountability
disagreements.summary: Four commissioners supported endorsing the privately funded multi-county Triangle Trails Initiative with added climate and commuting-equity language, while Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton voted No due to unclear organizational accountability.
disagreements.side_a_position: Endorse the Triangle Trails Initiative resolution to establish regional greenway connections for commuting, health, economic development, and climate benefits at no cost to Durham County.
side_a_arguments: Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow, Wendy Jacobs, and Heidi Carter noted the initiative required no county funds, leveraged private philanthropy through a regional foundation, and supported transportation equity and carbon reduction.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose the resolution until leadership, organizational governance, and county responsibility are clearly explained.
side_b_arguments: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton stated the agenda packet lacked sufficient background on the proposed foundation and which entity would be accountable, saying she 'didn't get the essence of it.'
disagreements.resolution: Resolution passed 4-1, with Reckhow tasked with following up on equitable community engagement and governance questions.

disagreements.issue: Transportation Demand Management and Charging County Employees for Deck Parking
disagreements.summary: During directives review, commissioners clashed over whether staff should evaluate charging county employees to park in county decks ahead of the 300 and 500 East Main Street parking decisions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Bring forward TDM options including potential employee parking fees to manage parking demand and right-size downtown parking decks.
side_a_arguments: Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Wendy Jacobs noted City of Durham employees pay tiered parking rates and the Environmental Affairs Board urged cutting parking supply in the 300/500 block projects.
disagreements.side_b_position: Protect free employee parking as a matter of workforce fairness and economic equity.
side_b_arguments: Vice Chair James Hill argued charging county workers—many single mothers—for parking when Durham transit cannot reliably get parents from schools to downtown work is regressive.
Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton called taking back hard-won competitive employee compensation through parking fees 'inhumane.'
disagreements.resolution: No vote taken; County Manager Wendell Davis agreed to present TDM options and updates at the March work session.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC January 27, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the January 27, 2020 regular session with all five commissioners present, passing every formal vote unanimously (5-0). The board approved its November 4, 2019 work session and January 13, 2020 regular session minutes (5-0), welcomed new Public Health Director Rodney Jenkins and a deploying 91st Civil Affairs Battalion delegation from Fort Bragg, and approved consent items 20-0019 through 20-0039 (5-0) after reviewing a NACo early-childhood policy resolution tied to the Pritzker grant. Following a public hearing on UDO Text Amendment TC19-0002—a privately initiated request on behalf of Topgolf at Page Road and I-40 allowing extended outdoor recreational lighting hours (up to 3:00 a.m. Sun–Thu and 5:00 a.m. Fri–Sat) in industrial zoning districts via a quasi-judicial Minor Special Use Permit—commissioners questioned lighting glare, neighborhood notice, public interest, and service-worker wages before adopting both the consistency statement (5-0) and the ordinance amendment (5-0). The meeting concluded with appointments across six boards and commissions and a brief manager update awaiting Durham Public Schools' revised capital cash-flow plan.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting, announced the Youth Listening Project, new GoDurham high-frequency/night routes, March 3 primary election rules (no photo ID required), and county tax payment plans. Commissioners unanimously approved the November 4, 2019 work session and January 13, 2020 regular session minutes and noted directives follow-up for the February work session.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Welcomes: Public Health Director Rodney Jenkins and 91st Civil Affairs Battalion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board formally welcomed new Public Health Director Rodney Jenkins, who expressed pride in joining Durham County's 250+ public health professionals, and hosted Captain Juan Cruz and soldiers from Fort Bragg's 91st Civil Affairs Battalion studying local governance ahead of their deployment to West Africa.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 20-0019 through 20-0039)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's request, Marcia and Linda explained Item 20-0039, a resolution submitting Durham's birth-to-three and early-childhood workforce priorities to NACo's national policy agenda in alignment with the Pritzker grant ahead of a January 29 deadline. Commissioners unanimously approved consent items 20-0019 through 20-0039.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC19-0002 — Outdoor Lighting Applicability
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Pat Young and Senior Planner Carl Kolosna presented privately initiated text amendment TC19-0002 enabling recreational venues in Industrial, Industrial Light, and Industrial Park districts to operate outdoor lighting until 3:00 a.m. (Sun–Thu) and 5:00 a.m. (Fri–Sat) if granted a quasi-judicial Minor Special Use Permit by the Board of Adjustment with 600-foot neighbor notice. Applicant attorney Keith Burns confirmed the site is a proposed Topgolf facility at Page Road and I-40 requiring late-night outfield maintenance lighting; after Commissioners Carter and Howerton pressed Burns on paying $15/hour living wages and commissioners praised Planning Commission feedback, the board unanimously adopted the consistency statement and ordinance amendment.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and DPS Capital Cash-Flow Inquiry
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board appointed members to the Board of Health (Eric Ireland), Boxing and Wrestling Commission (Jonathan Leach), City-County Appearance Commission (Bettina/Latina Rogers), DOST (William Aiken and Reynolds Smith), Farmland Protection Advisory Board (Talmadge Layton), and Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (DeWarren Langley). Before adjourning, Manager Wendell Davis responded to a commissioner inquiry that staff was still awaiting Durham Public Schools' workable cash-flow version of its long-term facility master plan.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 4, 2019 Work Session and January 13, 2020 Regular Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Unanimously approved November 4, 2019 work session and January 13, 2020 regular session minutes.

votes.item_title: TC19-0002 Statement of Consistency (NCGS 153A-341) — Outdoor Lighting Applicability
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted statutory consistency statement for UDO text amendment TC19-0002.

votes.item_title: Adoption of UDO Text Amendment TC19-0002 — Article 7 Design Standards (Outdoor Lighting)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted UDO Article 7 revisions permitting extended late-hour recreational lighting in industrial districts subject to Board of Adjustment Minor Special Use Permit approval.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC December 9, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the December 9, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, with all five commissioners present. The board unanimously approved the October 28 and November 12, 2019 minutes (5-0), honored Southern High School football players for organizing the 'Guns Down, Lives Up' anti-gun-violence rally, and heard a presentation from the Eno River Association's new executive director. After pulling consent item 19-0608 ($1.9 million to design a 780-space downtown parking deck) due to a resident's climate-related objection, the board unanimously approved both the remainder of the consent agenda (5-0) and item 19-0608 (5-0), emphasizing the deck's mixed-use integration with affordable housing, commercial space, and a daycare facility. Following a public hearing, the board also unanimously approved a $950,000 economic development incentive for Q2 Solutions (5-0), expected to create 749 jobs and $84.2 million in investment, before adjourning to a closed session on pending litigation (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and North Carolina Solar Schools Initiative
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Announcements covered the DCHC MPO regional plan to reduce single-occupancy vehicles, the Hub Pop-Up youth resource event, the Durham Holiday Parade, open enrollment at healthcare.gov, and the launch of the North Carolina Solar Schools Initiative by 34 elected officials partnering with Duke Energy to install no-cost solar on public schools.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 28, 2019 and November 12, 2019 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval of the October 28 and November 12, 2019 meeting minutes and commended the clerk's office on the improved formatting. Commissioner Heidi Carter seconded the commendation and motion, which passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Eno River Association Calendar, 'Guns Down, Lives Up' Resolution, and Youth Safety
agenda_items.discussion_summary: New Eno River Association Executive Director Jessica Sheffield presented the organization's annual calendar. Vice Chair James Hill read a resolution honoring Southern High School football team members and Durham Athletes United Against Gun Violence for organizing the November 'Guns Down, Lives Up' rally, followed by discussion of Durham youth violence/bullying statistics and a request for Congress to revoke the Medicaid Inmate Exclusion Policy.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 19-0560 through 19-0618, excluding 19-0608)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed a $1.2 million pay-as-you-go interfund reimbursement resolution, state 'Raise the Age' juvenile crime prevention allocations ($4.2 million in FY 2019-20 and $6.6 million in FY 2020-21), and two conservation easements. The board unanimously approved items 19-0560 through 19-0618 with item 19-0608 pulled for public comment.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC November 25, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the November 25, 2019 regular session, with Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton excused absent (4-0) and four commissioners present. The board approved the October 7 work session minutes (4-0) and adopted a consent agenda (4-0) that included $6.5 million in limited obligation bonds capital funding for Durham Public Schools deferred maintenance and a $145 million installment financing and refunding package yielding roughly $5 million in net present value savings. During the public hearing on UDO Text Amendment TC190001 (Omnibus Changes 13), neighbors raised urgent complaints about non-compliant fill sites, concrete debris, and DOT diamond-grinding dumping near Falls Lake. An initial combined motion by Ellen W. Reckhow (seconded by Heidi Carter) to approve the proposed regulations along with monitoring and enforcement recommendations passed 3-1, with Ellen W. Reckhow and Heidi Carter voting aye and one of the remaining two present commissioners (Wendy Jacobs or James Hill, not identified by name in the audio transcript) voting nay; the board then unanimously passed the required statutory consistency statement (4-0) and adopted the UDO text amendment with a task force directive to the Environmental Affairs Board and Soil and Water Conservation Board (4-0) before entering closed session (4-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excused Absence for Commissioner Howerton, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting, read the public charge, and removed closed session adjustments before the board voted 4-0 to excuse Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's absence. Announcements highlighted the Durham Homicide and Victims of Violent Death Memorial Quilt, a Durham Local Reentry Council simulation, community anti-violence collaboration (Project Build and Bull City United), and public comment on single-occupancy vehicle reduction.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 7, 2019 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval of the October 7, 2019 work session minutes and praised staff for thorough documentation of a long, complex session. Vice Chair James Hill seconded, and the motion passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: National Radon Action Month and Refugee Welcome Letters
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board proclaimed National Radon Action Month 2019 with state program director Phillip Gibson, highlighting EPA grant participation and radon's role as a leading cause of lung cancer in non-smokers. Commissioners also discussed letters affirming Durham County as a welcoming community for refugees alongside the City of Durham.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 19-0535 through 19-0574): DPS Capital Funding & $145M Financing/Refunding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter questioned item 19-0535 ($6.5 million in limited obligation bonds for Durham Public Schools deferred maintenance) and item 19-0574 (authorizing a $145 million installment financing amendment including $10.029 million for Administration One renovations, EMS Station 1 draw takeout, and a taxable refunding projected to save $5 million net present value). Staff confirmed the low-interest timing and shovel-ready contract status before the board approved the consent agenda 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC190001 (Omnibus Changes 13) & Fill-Site Sedimentation Enforcement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented TC190001 covering comprehensive plan evaluation, limited agricultural permits/chickens, solar installations, sidewalks, and sedimentation/erosion control regulations. Residents near Falls Lake testified about rill erosion, concrete debris on Betty Ross Road, and $1.9 million DOT diamond-grinding dumping contracts, urging stronger compliance and removal of the 30-foot stockpile language; after an initial combined motion passed 3-1, the board unanimously adopted the statutory consistency statement (4-0) and the UDO ordinance with a task force directive to the Soil and Water Conservation Board and Environmental Affairs Board (4-0).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Economic Development Incentives)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 4-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss economic development incentives and industry expansion. Upon reconvening at 02:59:17, Chair Jacobs stated direction was given to staff and the board adjourned.

votes.discussion_detail: Granted an excused absence to Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton for the November 25, 2019 regular session.

votes.item_title: Approval of October 7, 2019 Work Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the October 7, 2019 work session minutes with commendation to staff.

Staff subsequently prompted separate statutory motions for the consistency statement and ordinance.

votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) on economic development incentives.

disagreements.issue: TC190001 Sedimentation/Erosion Control Regulations and Fill-Site Enforcement
disagreements.summary: Following resident testimony detailing non-compliant fill sites, concrete debris on Betty Ross Road, and DOT diamond-grinding dumping near Falls Lake, commissioners debated whether to adopt the City-approved Omnibus Changes 13 text amendment immediately alongside a task force review or hold/modify provisions such as the 30-foot stockpile rule and compliance enforcement.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the pending TC190001 regulations now (matching the City) while commissioning a task force with the Soil and Water Conservation Board, Environmental Affairs Board, and NC State to bring back enforcement and legislative amendments.
side_a_arguments: The City of Durham had already approved the omnibus ordinance.
Staff committed to convening a task force for monitoring, enforcement, and near-term amendments in the new year.
disagreements.side_b_position: One present commissioner (either Wendy Jacobs or James Hill, not named in the audio transcript) voted against the initial combined approval motion at 02:21:58 amid concerns raised about the 30-foot stockpile provision and unresolved compliance enforcement.
side_b_arguments: Residents warned that current fill-site enforcement and the 30-foot stockpile language failed to protect Falls Lake watershed residents.
disagreements.resolution: The preliminary combined motion passed 3-1 (with Ellen W. Reckhow and Heidi Carter moving/seconding in favor, and one unidentified present member between Wendy Jacobs and James Hill opposed); when prompted for formal statutory votes, the board unanimously approved both the consistency statement (4-0) and the ordinance with the task force directive (4-0).

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC November 12, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the Tuesday, November 12, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, shifted from Monday due to Veterans Day, with all five commissioners present. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow took a point of personal privilege to reflect on her 31 years of service on the board, and Commissioner Heidi Carter introduced a joint local-official letter urging Duke Energy to deploy no-upfront-cost solar plus battery storage on North Carolina public schools. The board received a $10,000 Duke Energy donation for City-County Emergency Management, accepted the second installment of a $1.2 million contribution from the Durham Library Foundation for the new main library, and adopted resolutions supporting Durham becoming a Medicaid Healthy Opportunities Community and urging the General Assembly to end the FY 2019-2020 state budget impasse with a 5% public school employee raise and Medicaid expansion. Formally, the board unanimously approved the October 14 minutes (5-0), the consent agenda items 19-0488 through 19-0556 including the library item (5-0), and closed session entry under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)-(4) (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Ellen W. Reckhow 31-Year Service Reflection
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the Tuesday session (rescheduled for Veterans Day) and shared announcements on the 300/500 East Main Street developer open house and a vaping/smoking public health forum. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow took a point of personal privilege reflecting on 31 years on the board and thanking voters across 24 primary and general elections, and Commissioner Heidi Carter circulated a clean-energy letter urging Duke Energy to partner on no-upfront-cost solar plus battery storage at public schools.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Duke Energy Donation, National Adoption Month, Healthy Opportunities, and State Budget Impasse Resolutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board recognized a $10,000 Duke Energy donation to Emergency Management and proclaimed November 2019 as National Adoption Awareness Month (noting 166 adoptions since January 2014). Commissioners also presented a resolution supporting Durham's six-county Medicaid Healthy Opportunities social determinants of health RFP and a resolution urging the North Carolina General Assembly to resolve the 2019-2020 budget impasse, enact a 5% raise for public school employees and retirees, and expand Medicaid.

agenda_items.title: Durham Library Foundation $1.2 Million Contribution Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Library Foundation President Annie Cravar presented the second installment of contributions totaling $1.2 million ($800,000 committed in June plus $400,000 raised over the past year) for enhancements to the new main library. Commissioners expressed gratitude and incorporated the library business item into the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 14, 2019 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs noted the minutes had been briefly overlooked after ceremonial items. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved approval of the October 14, 2019 regular session minutes, seconded by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton, and the motion passed 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 19-0488 through 19-0556, plus Library Item 19-0529)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board added library item 19-0529 to consent items 19-0488 through 19-0556 and unanimously approved the package (5-0). Chair Jacobs highlighted a conservation easement on a minority-owned farm, an added full-time nutrition educator for the DINE program in Durham Public Schools, and funding for the Formerly Incarcerated Transitions (FIT) health program.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Economic Development & Attorney-Client Privilege)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) for economic development incentive negotiations and N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) for attorney-client privilege. Upon reconvening at 02:30:41, Chair Jacobs acknowledged a staff binder on the DPS MOU data and the board adjourned.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved the October 14, 2019 regular session minutes.

votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(3).

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC October 28, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the October 28, 2019 regular session, with Vice Chair James Hill excused absent (4-0) and four commissioners present. After approving the September 23 minutes (4-0), recognizing Bull City United outreach worker Keisha Gray and the Made in Durham work-based learning campaign, and passing single-item consent agenda 19-0500 (4-0), the board conducted four consecutive land-use public hearings. Commissioners unanimously approved zoning map change Z1900020 for Leesville Road Boat and RV Storage with a proffered Section 9.7 screening standard (4-0 across consistency and ordinance votes) and adopted UDO Text Amendment TC190003 updating FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Maps (4-0 across both votes). Following extensive discussion of stormwater and environmental impacts on the county's previously referred Expanding Housing Choices text amendment (TC180007), the board unanimously adopted the consistency statement (4-0), the UDO amendment (4-0), and a county substitute monitoring resolution requiring a three-year review (4-0), and likewise approved Tree Coverage and Landscaping UDO amendment TC180005 (4-0 across both votes) before making advisory board appointments.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Minutes, and Excused Absence for Vice Chair Hill
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting, announced the Durham County Recycles app, the Homicide Memorial Quilt display at Human Services, and Healthcare.gov open enrollment. The board approved the September 23, 2019 regular session minutes (4-0), granted an excused absence to Vice Chair James Hill (4-0), and confirmed with the County Manager that the employee compensation study implementation would be retroactive.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: Bull City United Award and Made in Durham Work-Based Learning Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board honored Bull City United violence interruption worker Keisha Gray for winning the 2019 Willis Young Memorial Award and reviewed a video and resolution supporting the Made in Durham work-based learning collaborative campaign.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Item 19-0500
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the single-item consent agenda (19-0500) on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and second by Commissioner Heidi Carter.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change Z1900020 (Leesville Road Boat & RV Storage)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff presented applicant Warren Mitchell's request to rezone nearly 14 acres at 4615 Leesville Road from Rural Residential (RR) to Commercial General with a text-only development plan (CG-D) limited to boat and RV storage. After Commissioner Reckhow requested enforceable screening guarantees, the applicant proffered compliance with UDO Section 9.7 perimeter screening, and the board unanimously approved the consistency statement and rezoning ordinance (4-0 each).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC190003 (FEMA FIRM Updates)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock and Ryan Eaves presented TC190003 to incorporate outstanding FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map panels resolved after neighboring-county challenges prior to the December 6, 2019 deadline required for National Flood Insurance Program eligibility. Commissioners discussed 1% future-conditions floodplain mapping and watershed education before unanimously adopting the consistency statement and ordinance (4-0 each).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC180007 (Expanding Housing Choices, County Jurisdiction)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning Director Pat Young reintroduced Expanding Housing Choices (TC180007) for the county jurisdiction following the board's September 23 referral back to staff. Commissioners examined how stormwater/environmental impacts from accessory dwelling units and small-lot infill would be tracked alongside tree planting, ribbon driveways, and the upcoming affordable housing bond, then unanimously adopted the consistency statement (4-0), ordinance (4-0), and a substitute metrics and three-year review resolution (4-0).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC180005 (Tree Coverage and Landscaping)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michael Stock presented TC180005 to prioritize preservation of existing trees over replacement, widen buffers where mass grading is used, and increase urban-tier tree coverage, while deferring broad suburban right-of-way street tree mandates pending a joint pilot with TreesDurham. Commissioners expressed disappointment over the deferred right-of-way street tree rules and urged equitable tree planting in low-income communities before unanimously approving the consistency statement and ordinance (4-0 each).

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The clerk announced board appointment results for the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee, Board of Adjustment, Community Child Protection/Child Fatality Prevention Team, Discover Durham Tourism Development Authority, Industrial Facilities and Pollution Control Financing Authority, and Workforce Development Board before adjournment.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC August 26, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the August 26, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners with all five commissioners present. Following emotional remarks and a Project Build update addressing recent gun violence—including the fatal shooting of a nine-year-old boy—the board approved prior minutes (5-0) and proclaimed National Recovery Month 2019. Commissioners unanimously approved the unpulled consent agenda (5-0) and then approved pulled consent items 0396 ($12.6 million Snow Hill capital project amendment and $2.1 million design-build phase), 0406 (Chamber of Commerce contract), and 0407 (Downtown Durham Inc. contract) (5-0) after discussing gap tax billing, local workforce pipelines, MWBE participation, and downtown panhandling outreach. After a public hearing on item 19-0395, the board unanimously adopted the Compact Suburban Design District UDO text amendment, consistency statement, and future street network resolution for Patterson Place (5-0 across all three votes), heard a reproductive rights presentation from the Durham County Women's Commission, made board appointments, and entered closed session (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Gun Violence Remarks, and Project Build Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting and addressed recent shootings in Durham, including the fatal shooting of a nine-year-old boy and wounding of an eight-year-old child. Project Build staff described newly funded outreach workers, a six-week Phoenix conflict-resolution curriculum at Lakeview School, trauma support, and the Fatherhood of Durham initiative.

agenda_items.title: Approval of June 24, July 11, and August 5, 2019 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the June 24, July 11, and August 5, 2019 work session and regular session minutes on a motion by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and second by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Item: National Recovery Month 2019 Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Representatives from the Criminal Justice Resource Center (CJRC) and Durham's recovery community received a National Recovery Month 2019 proclamation highlighting fentanyl-driven overdose deaths, suicide rates, mental health treatment gaps, and stigma reduction.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Pulled Items 19-0396, 19-0400, 19-0406, and 19-0407
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved consent items 19-0382 through 19-0407 minus four pulled items (5-0), then reviewed the pulled items: the $12.6 million Snow Hill capital project ($2.1 million initial design-build contract), tax settlement report showing gap-billing impacts (0400), the Greater Durham Chamber contract (0406, focusing on Treyburn transit and local hiring pipelines), and the Downtown Durham Inc. contract (0407, noting a panhandling best-practices study). Commissioners then unanimously approved items 0396, 0406, and 0407 (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Compact Suburban Design District Text Amendment & Patterson Place (Item 19-0395)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Lisa Miller presented the form-based Compact Suburban Design District text amendment and Patterson Place future street network, incorporating affordable housing density bonuses, prohibited payday lending, New Hope Creek environmental buffers, and suspended sidewalks. Following discussion of transit frequency without light rail, Go Triangle height comments, and school/sewer capacity (Gethin lift station), the board unanimously approved the consistency statement, text amendment ordinance, and future street network resolution (5-0 each).

agenda_items.title: Durham County Women's Commission Presentation on Reproductive Healthcare & Maternal Mortality
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Women's Commission representatives Vivian Slade, Sarah Bausch, and Patty Black urged the board to pass a resolution affirming reproductive healthcare access and supporting federal legislation (the Women's Health Protection Act and EACH Act). Commissioners requested a draft resolution incorporating Black maternal mortality, volunteer doula access (MAAME), and county public health programs.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The clerk announced board appointments to the Adult Care Home Community Advisory Committee, Board of Adjustment, Appearance Commission, and Durham-Wake Research and Production Service District. The board then voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)-(4), returning at 03:45:14 to adjourn.
