meetings.title: Durham County BOCC August 12, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the August 12, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners with all five commissioners present. The board opened with a joint statement condemning recent mass shootings in Gilroy, El Paso, and Dayton as well as large-scale ICE raids, approved May and June meeting minutes (5-0), and signed onto the Paris Declaration on Fast-Track Cities to End the AIDS Epidemic alongside IAPAC leader Dr. Jose Zuniga and Ace Robinson. Commissioners also adopted a Purple Heart resolution, endorsed a resolution opposing proposed USDA restrictions on SNAP broad-based categorical eligibility, recognized Durham County IT's second-place national ranking in the 2019 Digital Counties Survey, and unanimously approved consent agenda items 19-0214 through 19-0368 (5-0). Following a public hearing, the board unanimously approved a $3 million economic development incentive for Merck's $650 million Durham plant expansion creating 391 new jobs (5-0) before adjourning to closed session (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Statement on Mass Shootings and ICE Raids, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting and delivered a board statement condemning mass shootings in Gilroy, El Paso, and Dayton and large-scale federal ICE arrests, followed by comments from commissioners on federal inaction and gun violence. The board also added a closed session to the agenda and shared announcements including City Hall Selfie Day and a local history exhibit at the Health Department.

agenda_items.title: Approval of May 21, May 29, and June 10, 2019 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter moved approval of the May 21 and May 29 budget work session minutes and June 10 regular session minutes, noting their detailed directives. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton seconded, and the motion passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Fast-Track Cities Paris Declaration, Purple Heart, SNAP Eligibility Resolution, and Digital Counties Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County signed the Paris Declaration on Fast-Track Cities to End the AIDS Epidemic with Dr. Jose Zuniga and Ace Robinson, adopted a Purple Heart recognition resolution, and endorsed a resolution presented with DSS Director Ben Rose opposing federal USDA restrictions on SNAP broad-based categorical eligibility that threaten child nutrition. The board also introduced newly promoted staff and recognized IT Director Greg Marrow for tying for second place nationwide in the 2019 Digital Counties Survey.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 19-0214 through 19-0368)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a brief question on item 19-0365, the board unanimously approved consent items 19-0214 through 19-0368. Chair Jacobs highlighted a grant for a sensory-inclusive space at the main library and doubling county electric-vehicle charging stations.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: $3 Million Economic Development Incentive for Merck
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Director Andy Miracle presented a $3 million incentive for Merck's $650 million expansion of its Durham vaccine manufacturing plant, adding 391 new jobs averaging roughly $73,000 (including operations and support jobs starting at $61,000-$80,000 without advanced degree requirements). Following public hearing testimony from Greater Durham Chamber VP Brian Fox and commissioner inquiries regarding net job growth after 150 prior positions and workforce pipeline access for Durham residents, the board unanimously approved the $3 million award.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (Attorney-Client Privilege and Criminal Investigation Reports)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(7) for attorney-client consultation and reports concerning investigations of alleged criminal misconduct. Upon returning at 02:35:52, Chair Jacobs reported direction was given to staff and the meeting adjourned.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved the May 21 and May 29 budget work session minutes and June 10, 2019 regular session minutes.

votes.notes: Mover was not identified by name in the audio transcript; seconded by Vice Chair James Hill.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC July 8, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the July 8, 2019 regular session following an initial closed session, with all five commissioners present. Immediately upon reconvening, the board voted 4-1 on a motion by Ellen W. Reckhow and second by James Hill to set the County Manager's salary at $226,011—with Ellen W. Reckhow, James Hill, and two of the other three commissioners (Wendy Jacobs, Brenda A. Howerton, and Heidi Carter) voting aye, and one of those three commissioners casting the lone nay (whose name was garbled/unidentified in the audio transcript). Commissioners then unanimously approved the June 3 work session minutes (5-0) and the consent agenda (5-0), including funding for main library and cooperative extension after-hours security. In other business, the board received an update from the UNC School of Government's Development Finance Initiative (DFI) on selecting Laurel Street for 305 affordable housing units at 300 and 500 East Main Street, endorsed staff's post-light-rail transit planning framework with GoTriangle (including Commissioner Howerton's call for representative board diversity), approved ABC Board language (5-0), made advisory board appointments, and entered closed session (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Post-Closed Session Action: County Manager Salary Adjustment ($226,011)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Reconvening from a pre-meeting closed session, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved and Vice Chair James Hill seconded setting the County Manager's salary at $226,011. The motion passed 4-1 with one unidentified commissioner voting nay.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, Minutes, and Consent Agenda (Item 19-0337)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs shared announcements on Durham Neighborhood College, Engaged Durham, Innovate Durham, and the Eno-Haw Regional Hazard Mitigation Plan. The board unanimously approved the June 3, 2019 work session minutes (5-0) and the consent agenda (5-0) after clarifying that item 19-0337 transfers funds for after-hours security at Cooperative Extension and additional security at the new main library.

agenda_items.title: Update on 300 and 500 East Main Street Development Partner Selection (305 Affordable Units)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Marcia Perritt of UNC's Development Finance Initiative (DFI) updated the board on selecting Laurel Street's proposal for 300 and 500 East Main Street, which exceeds the solicitation's 277-unit target by providing 305 affordable units at 80% AMI and below alongside community meet-the-developer sessions. Commissioners praised the county's milestone entry into affordable housing development and discussed shared parking and street-level design over a six-to-nine-month predevelopment period.

agenda_items.title: Post-Light-Rail Durham County Transit Plan Update & Framework Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning and GoTriangle staff outlined a 12-month process to update the 2017 Durham County Transit Plan following cancellation of the Durham-Orange Light Rail project, including an FY 2020 pipeline assessment and budget reconciliation by November 1. Commissioners discussed bus and commuter-rail priorities, multi-directional commuter patterns, and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's demand for greater racial diversity on the GoTriangle Board of Directors; staff confirmed no formal resolution was needed to endorse the process.

agenda_items.title: ABC Board Language Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a brief introduction with the county attorney regarding proposed language for the ABC Board, the board approved the motion by unanimous voice vote.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The clerk announced selections for the Board of Adjustment (one of two vacancies filled) and other advisory posts including Natalia Rice. meetings.title: Durham County BOCC June 24, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the June 24, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners with all five commissioners present. After approving May minutes (5-0), celebrating the J. Robert Havlick Innovation Award, and passing consent items 19-0108 through 19-0331 minus pulled item 19-0236 (5-0), the board unanimously adopted the FY 2019-2020 Budget Ordinance (5-0). The adopted budget set a 71.22-cent tax rate (2.3 cents above revenue-neutral), boosted Durham Public Schools funding by $7.25 million (adding $250,000 above the manager's $7 million recommendation, bringing DPS operating funds near $146 million), funded Durham Pre-K at $5.1 million, invested $4.8 million in justice diversion/reentry programs, and allocated $3.1 million for employee compensation equity. The board also unanimously approved the continued Rougemont Commercial rezoning Z1800037 (5-0 across both votes), endorsed the City-County Response Policy Regarding Encampments on Public Property (5-0), updated the Northern Durham convenience site plan, adopted the Downtown County-Owned Property Evaluation Framework with equity and transit-oriented language (5-0), and voted 5-0 on anniversary-date salary increases for five appointed/elected officials.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs announced salaries following an early closed session for the Sheriff, Register of Deeds, Acting Tax Administrator, Clerk to the Board, and County Attorney, and shared announcements on summer meals, the USATF Youth Outdoor Championship, and 2020 Census jobs. The board unanimously approved the May 13, May 28, and May 18, 2019 minutes (5-0) and recognized the J. Robert Havlick Innovation Award.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed Urban Ministries items (19-0291 and 19-0317) and requested a future briefing on computer stations before pulling item 19-0236 (the FY 2019-2020 budget ordinance). The remainder of the consent agenda passed unanimously (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 19-0236: FY 2019-2020 Budget Ordinance ($7.25M DPS Increase & 71.22-Cent Tax Rate)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter introduced the updated budget ordinance adding $250,000 above the manager's $7 million recommendation for Durham Public Schools—providing a $7.25 million increase (nearly $146 million total)—alongside $5.1 million for Durham Pre-K, $1.4 million in Durham Tech scholarships, $4.8 million for Bull City United/FIT/Project Build/reentry, doubled eviction diversion funding, $3.1 million for employee pay equity, and a 71.22-cent property tax rate. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton noted a procedural concern that the $250,000 addition arose after the last work session, while all five commissioners voted aye to adopt the budget (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Continued Public Hearing: Zoning Map Change Z1800037 (Rougemont Commercial)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Emily Struthers presented supplemental analysis on the 2014 Village of Rougemont Plan and rural pedestrian connectivity for continued rezoning case Z1800037. Commissioners noted that Rougemont residents had previously prioritized local commercial retail access over restrictive design guidelines and unanimously approved the consistency statement and rezoning ordinance (5-0 each).

agenda_items.title: City-County Response Policy Regarding Encampments on Public Property
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Homeless Project Manager Analia Hoberman presented the formalized City-County encampment response policy developed with homeless service providers after visible encampments along Highway 147, establishing public health, safety, and mobility assessments alongside outreach. Commissioners asked about Homeless Services Advisory Committee progress reporting and unanimously endorsed the policy (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Northern Durham Convenience Site Project Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Services and Solid Waste staff presented plans to replace the gravel Bahama/Northern Durham convenience site (over 100,000 annual visitors) with a four-bay paved layout, cardboard compactors, shared fire-station driveway access, and a multi-purpose two-story building incorporating Sheriff observation/substation access and youth environmental education.

agenda_items.title: Downtown County-Owned Property Evaluation Tool / Framework
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the revised downtown property evaluation tool incorporating acquisition history, current tenants, opportunity costs, human capital, affordable housing, and partners such as DHA and DPS, while awaiting a joint city-county consultant study on additional parcels including 315 Holland Street. At Chair Jacobs's request, the motion to adopt the framework (5-0) directed staff to incorporate explicit equity and transit-oriented development language.

agenda_items.title: Official Salary Adjustments Vote and Boards & Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Recognizing that the closed-session salary adjustments required a formal open-session vote, the board unanimously approved anniversary-date salary adjustments for the Sheriff ($144,654 as read in the motion; $150,602 noted earlier), Register of Deeds ($105,541), Interim Tax Administrator ($107,054), Clerk to the Board ($85,000), and County Attorney ($209,931) (5-0). The clerk then read board appointment results for 12 advisory bodies before adjournment.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 13, May 28, and May 18, 2019 Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the May 13 regular session, May 28 regular session, and May 18 minutes.

votes.item_title: FY 2019-2020 Budget Ordinance Adoption (Item 19-0236)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the FY 2019-2020 budget ordinance at a 71.22-cent property tax rate, including a $7.25M funding increase for Durham Public Schools (adding $250,000 above the manager's recommendation), $5.1M for Durham Pre-K, and $3.1M for employee pay equity.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change Z1800037 (Rougemont Commercial) Consistency Statement
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the statutory consistency statement for Rougemont Commercial rezoning Z1800037 pursuant to N.C.G.S. 153A-341.

votes.item_title: Zoning Map Change Z1800037 (Rougemont Commercial) Ordinance Adoption
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the UDO rezoning ordinance for Rougemont Commercial (Z1800037) in the Little River District B watershed overlay.

votes.item_title: Endorse City-County Response Policy Regarding Encampments on Public Property
votes.discussion_detail: Endorsed the joint City-County response policy for assessing and addressing encampments on public property with outreach and mitigation protocols.

votes.item_title: Adopt Downtown County-Owned Property Evaluation Framework (with Equity and Transit-Oriented Language)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the downtown county-owned property evaluation framework while directing staff to add explicit equity/inclusiveness and transit-oriented development wording.

votes.item_title: Official Salary Adjustments for Sheriff, Register of Deeds, Interim Tax Administrator, Clerk, and County Attorney
votes.discussion_detail: Approved anniversary-date salary adjustments for the Sheriff ($144,654 stated in motion; $150,602 read earlier), Register of Deeds ($105,541), Interim Tax Administrator ($107,054), Clerk to the Board ($85,000), and County Attorney ($209,931).

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC June 10, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the June 10, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, adjusting the agenda to recognize the Friends of the Library Foundation for furnishing the Main Library and proclaiming June 19, 2019 as the 10th Anniversary of World Sickle Cell Awareness Day. The board unanimously approved meeting minutes (5-0), excused upcoming September 9 absences for Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow (5-0), and adopted the consent agenda (5-0), which included conveying five county surplus properties—including a 3.5-acre parcel—to the City of Durham for $10 each for affordable housing and accepting NC Biotech and NIH grants. Following a public hearing on $120,500 in economic development incentives for ParExcel International Corporation (to add 264 jobs and establish a second U.S. headquarters) and community budget remarks, the board held a public hearing and voted 5-0 to approve merging Durham County ACCESS paratransit operations with the City of Durham. Commissioners also heard from DSS Director Ben Rose regarding a proposed federal Office of Management and Budget rule change shifting poverty guidelines to Chained CPI and discussed submitting a comment letter opposing the change before holding a unanimous closed session on three pending litigation matters (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment, and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order following a closed session, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. She adjusted the agenda to move Item 19-0284 to the start of ceremonial items and announced the Durham County Summer Reading Program, Board of Elections voter photo ID sessions, and the County Manager's Durham This Week newsletter.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes and Excused Absences for September 9, 2019 Meeting
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs noted a pending excused absence request with Clerk Monica Toomer for the September 9 meeting. The board voted unanimously (5-0) to approve the minutes and then voted unanimously (5-0) to excuse Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow from the September 9 regular meeting.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: Friends of the Library Foundation (Item 19-0284) and World Sickle Cell Awareness Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board recognized Friends of the Library Foundation Board Chair Lou and foundation representatives for fundraising and furnishing the Main Library's communal space. Chair Jacobs then read a proclamation recognizing Wednesday, June 19, 2019 as the 10th anniversary of World Sickle Cell Awareness Day with Tiffany Bell and community partners.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 19-0185 through 19-0305)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved consent items 19-0185 through 19-0305 (5-0). Chair Jacobs highlighted Item 19-0280 conveying five county surplus parcels—including a 3.5-acre site—to the City of Durham at $10 each for affordable housing, and Economic Development's Andy Miracle highlighted NC Biotech-funded awards with community benefits and an NIH library health programming grant.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Economic Development Incentives for ParExcel International Corporation and Budget Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Andy Miracle presented a proposal to allocate $120,500 in economic development funds to ParExcel International Corporation to support a $1.7 million investment, 264 new jobs, retention of over 600 North Carolina employees, and a second U.S. headquarters in Durham County. Later in the session, commissioners thanked the large community audience for attending and weighing in on upcoming budget decisions.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Approval of Durham County ACCESS Merger with City of Durham
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation staff member Linda Wallace Thomas presented the interlocal merger transferring administrative functions of Durham County ACCESS demand-response paratransit to the City of Durham to achieve cost and operational efficiencies while maintaining FY18-19 funding and service levels under First Transit management. Chair Jacobs asked staff to pursue continuing the Transportation Heroes recognition ceremonies, and after closing the public hearing with no speakers, the board approved the merger 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of Proposed Federal OMB Poverty Guidelines Rule Change
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS Director Ben Rose briefed the board on the federal Office of Management and Budget proposal to calculate poverty guidelines using the Chained Consumer Price Index rather than the traditional CPI, warning it would lower thresholds over time and reduce SNAP and social services eligibility. Commissioners discussed having the County Manager send a comment letter supporting continued use of CPI with copies to the congressional delegation.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Litigation Matters (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session to consult with legal counsel regarding Marquita Welton v. Durham County et al. (17-CV-258), Julia Graves v. Durham County et al. (19-CV-316), and Durham County v. AmerisourceBergen Drug Corporation et al. (1:19-CV-0041). Upon returning to open session, Chair Jacobs reported that staff was given direction and the board adjourned.

votes.item_title: Approval of Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: ASR transcribed Commissioner Reckhow as 'Rec out' and Commissioner Howerton as 'Howardton'.
votes.discussion_detail: Unanimous approval of the minutes presented by Clerk Monica Toomer.

votes.item_title: Motion to Excuse Absences of Chair Jacobs and Commissioner Reckhow for September 9, 2019 Meeting
votes.discussion_detail: Approved excused absences for Chair Wendy Jacobs and Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow for the September 9, 2019 regular meeting.

votes.item_title: Approval of Durham County ACCESS Paratransit Merger with City of Durham
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the interlocal merger of Durham County ACCESS with the City of Durham following a public hearing with no opposition.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session to consult with legal counsel regarding Welton v. Durham County, Graves v. Durham County, and Durham County v. AmerisourceBergen Drug Corporation.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC May 28, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 28, 2019 regular session, Chair Wendy Jacobs and the Durham County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved prior meeting minutes (5-0) and consent agenda items 19-0239 through 19-0273 (5-0). Ceremonial items included an Older Americans Month proclamation presented with DSS Director Ben Rose and a special recognition honoring Amia Mitchell for using Stop the Bleed training to save gunshot victim Aria Hackney's life. During a public hearing on the Rougemont Commercial text-only rezoning (Item 19-0257), commissioners questioned staff on prohibited uses such as tobacco shops, sidewalk requirements, water utilities, and Rougemont Rural Village Plan consistency, while a resident expressed opposition to a rumored Dollar General; the board voted unanimously (5-0) to continue the hearing to June 24, 2019 for a supplemental staff report. The board also announced appointments to the Dangerous Dog Appeal Board and Workforce Development Board, welcomed summer Strategic Initiatives interns Sabrina Davis and Kelly Warren, and voted 5-0 to enter closed session on economic development incentives.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. She announced Board of Elections voter ID seminars (including Spanish-language sessions), the June 1 property tax relief deadline for seniors and disabled veterans, the FY19-20 budget portal and June 10 public hearing, Alert Durham, and the Community Health Coalition's 30th anniversary.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes (PAC 4 Feb 9, PAC 2 April 8, Regular Sessions April 8 and April 22, 2019)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved minutes from the February 9 PAC 4 meeting, April 8 PAC 2 meeting, April 8 regular session, and April 22 regular session.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Older Americans Month Proclamation and Recognition of Amia Mitchell
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill read the Older Americans Month proclamation alongside DSS Director Ben Rose, who noted Durham County's 65-and-older population is projected to rise from roughly 32,000 to nearly 90,000 by 2037. Chair Jacobs then presented a recognition to Amia Mitchell for using Stop the Bleed training to save Aria Hackney after a gunshot wound.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 19-0239 through 19-0273)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no items pulled for separate discussion, the board unanimously approved consent agenda items 19-0239 through 19-0273.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Rougemont Commercial Text-Only Rezoning (Item 19-0257)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planner Emily Struthers presented a text-only development plan rezoning to Commercial Neighborhood (CN) prohibiting drive-throughs, dry cleaning, payday lenders, taxi dispatch, and animal kennels, which the Planning Commission recommended 8-3. Commissioners raised questions about tobacco shops, malt beverage sales, UDO restrictions on proffering sidewalks in text-only plans, utilities, and Rougemont transit, and after public comment opposing a rumored Dollar General, voted 5-0 to continue the hearing to June 24, 2019 for a supplemental report on the Rougemont Rural Village Plan.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board conducted ballots and announced appointments to county advisory bodies, including Michelle Bixby to the Dangerous Dog Appeal Board and Anthony Nelson to the Workforce Development Board.

agenda_items.title: Introduction of Summer Interns and Closed Session on Economic Development (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session regarding business location and economic development incentives under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4), after which Chair Jacobs introduced Strategic Initiatives summer interns Sabrina Davis (Duke MPP) and Kelly Warren (NC State MPA). Upon returning from closed session, Chair Jacobs announced direction had been given to staff and the meeting adjourned.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (PAC 4, PAC 2, April 8 and April 22, 2019 Regular Sessions)
votes.discussion_detail: Unanimous approval of four sets of prior work/PAC and regular session minutes.

votes.item_title: Continue Rougemont Commercial Rezoning (Item 19-0257) to June 24, 2019 with Public Hearing Open
votes.notes: Motion deferred final action to June 24, 2019.
votes.discussion_detail: Continued the Rougemont Commercial text-only rezoning public hearing to June 24, 2019 so planning staff can prepare a supplemental report addressing the Rougemont Rural Village Plan and commissioner questions.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4))
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session to discuss economic development incentives and business location negotiations.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC May 13, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: During the May 13, 2019 regular session, the Durham County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved April 1, 2019 work session minutes (5-0) and issued ceremonial proclamations for National Drug Treatment Court Month, EMS Week (honoring responders to the April 10 downtown Durham incident), and Foster Care Month alongside DSS Director Ben Rose. The board also presented a resolution supporting North Carolina's working families—advocating for paid family leave, a $15 state employee minimum wage, Medicaid expansion, and public-sector collective bargaining rights. Following the County Manager's FY19-20 recommended budget presentation, public speakers Brian Calloway and Carl Kenney urged competitive pay and a $15 minimum wage across Durham Public Schools and Durham County, and the board unanimously adopted consent agenda items 19-0168 through 19-0248 (5-0), including a milestone ground-floor restaurant lease at Admin II. After a unanimous personnel closed session (5-0), the board voted 5-0 to appoint Monica Toomer as Clerk to the Board ($85,000 salary) and Timothy Dwayne Brinson as Tax Administrator ($165,000 salary).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of April 1, 2019 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order, read the public charge, and shared announcements covering Board of Elections voter ID seminars, FY2020 transit work plans public comment through May 20, the Foster Care Fair, Aging Well in Durham, and the FY19-20 budget portal. The board then unanimously approved the April 1, 2019 work session minutes (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: National Drug Treatment Court Month, EMS Week, and Foster Care Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter read the National Drug Treatment Court Month proclamation, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow read the EMS Week proclamation with Sheriff Clarence Burkhead honoring April 10 first responders, and the board recognized Foster Care Month (313 children in care and 104 licensed foster homes). DSS Director Ben Rose and commissioners discussed flat state foster reimbursement rates, $800,000 in mid-year local foster funding ($3.8 million total), and shifting toward prevention and Durham Pre-K.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting North Carolina's Working People and Their Families
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read a board resolution urging the North Carolina legislative delegation to support paid family leave, a higher minimum wage and $15/hour for all state employees, Medicaid expansion, and repealing 'right to work' restrictions to allow public-sector collective bargaining. Commissioners noted Durham County already provides a $15/hour minimum wage and 12 weeks of paid family leave.

agenda_items.title: FY19-20 Recommended Budget Remarks and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the County Manager's FY19-20 budget presentation (which noted five upcoming budget work sessions totaling 26 hours and honored retiring staff member Gail), two public speakers addressed compensation and capital planning. Brian Calloway criticized the DPS budget for omitting a $15 minimum wage while raising administrator salaries and commended the manager's bond approach to DPS capital requests, while Carl Kenney urged market-competitive pay for county workers.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 19-0168 through 19-0248)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs highlighted Item 19-0216, a milestone ground-floor retail lease in the Admin II building for Neighbors restaurant incorporating board-requested community benefits. The board voted unanimously (5-0) to approve consent items 19-0168 through 19-0248.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Personnel (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to consider public officer appointments and employment conditions.

agenda_items.title: Appointments of Clerk to the Board (Monica Toomer) and Tax Administrator (Timothy Dwayne Brinson)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After returning from closed session, the board voted 5-0 to appoint interim clerk Monica Toomer as Clerk to the Board effective May 14, 2019 at an annual salary of $85,000. The board then voted 5-0 to appoint Orange County Tax Administrator Timothy Dwayne Brinson as Durham County Tax Administrator effective July 1, 2019 (succeeding retired Kimberly Simpson) at a salary of $165,000, approving his appointment, salary, and contract.

votes.item_title: Approval of April 1, 2019 Work Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Unanimous approval of the April 1, 2019 work session minutes.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session to consider qualifications, conditions of appointment, and employment for public officers.

votes.item_title: Appointment of Monica Toomer as Clerk to the Board ($85,000 Salary)
votes.discussion_detail: Appointed Monica Toomer (serving as interim clerk since December) as Clerk to the Board effective May 14, 2019 at a salary of $85,000.

votes.item_title: Appointment of Timothy Dwayne Brinson as Tax Administrator ($165,000 Salary and Contract)
votes.discussion_detail: Appointed Timothy Dwayne Brinson as Durham County Tax Administrator effective July 1, 2019 at a salary of $165,000, succeeding retired Tax Administrator Kimberly Simpson, and approved his contract.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC April 22, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: On April 22, 2019, the Durham County Board of Commissioners approved work session and March 25 regular session minutes (5-0) after clarifying that prior work-session discussion on participating in a post-light-rail transit feasibility study reflected informal consensus rather than formal action. Ceremonially, Commissioner Heidi Carter read a Children's Mental Health Awareness Month proclamation and Chair Wendy Jacobs read a resolution supporting the May 1, 2019 Day of Action for North Carolina Public Schools, calling for state-funded support staff, a $15 school minimum wage, 5% employee and retiree raises, Medicaid expansion, and reinstated retiree health benefits. The board unanimously passed consent items 19-0179 through 19-0195 (5-0), received a report from the Adult Services Advisory Committee regarding volunteer retention and training, and announced appointments to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission, Child Protection/Fatality Prevention Team, Criminal Justice Advisory Committee, City-County Appearance Commission, and Durham County Hospital Corporation Board of Trustees. Commissioners then entered a closed session on personnel and attorney-client matters (5-0) before giving staff direction and adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The meeting opened with the public charge, Pledge of Allegiance, and announcements including a non-medication pain management workshop at the Durham Center for Senior Life, GoTriangle Get On Board Day free passes (April 22–26), and an Expanding Housing Choices community conversation on April 27 at Walltown Park Recreation Center.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Work Session and March 25, 2019 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Responding to Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton's concern about whether work-session consensus on joining a transit feasibility study (evaluating options instead of light rail if four partner entities participated) constituted formal action, commissioners clarified no motion or rule suspension occurred at the work session. The board then voted 5-0 to approve both the work session and March 25 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Children's Mental Health Awareness Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter, the board's representative to Alliance Behavioral Healthcare, read the proclamation for Children's Mental Health Awareness Month and presented it to Tika Dempson, who provided a brief update on local System of Care initiatives.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting May 1st Day of Action for North Carolina Public Schools
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs read a resolution signed by all five commissioners backing Durham Public Schools educators ahead of the May 1, 2019 rally. The resolution urged the General Assembly to fund national ratios for school nurses, social workers, psychologists, counselors, and media coordinators, enact a $15 minimum wage and 5% raises/retiree COLA, expand Medicaid, and restore state retiree health benefits; staff was directed to send copies to the school board, superintendent, governor, and legislative delegation.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 19-0179 through 19-0195)

agenda_items.title: Adult Services Advisory Committee Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Adult Services Advisory Committee Chair Sue Roth, Earl Kirby, and Jeff Austin delivered the committee's annual report. Commissioners discussed board orientation, training, and member retention challenges.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After correcting a ballot typo noting four selections (two citizen, two health system) for the Durham County Hospital Corporation Board of Trustees, the board announced appointments across five advisory bodies including Trisha Smart (BPAC), Keith Helmer (Child Protection/Fatality Prevention), Andrew Jennings (CJAC), three Appearance Commission appointees, and four Hospital Corporation Trustees.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Personnel and Attorney-Client Privilege (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session to discuss personnel matters and consult with the county attorney. Upon returning in open session, Chair Jacobs announced staff had been given direction and the board adjourned.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved both the work session minutes and March 25, 2019 regular session minutes after clarifying that work-session consensus on a transit feasibility study was not a formal vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) and (a)(6))

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC April 8, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 8, 2019 meeting, the Durham County Board of Commissioners approved the February 11 and March 11 regular session minutes (5-0) and presented seven ceremonial proclamations and resolutions, including Week of the Young Child, Child Abuse Prevention Awareness Month, Reentry Week, and a 2020 Census resolution targeting an 82% or higher county response rate. Following discussion of the 1% public art allocation process across capital projects, the board held a major deliberation on the termination of the Durham-Orange Light Rail cost-sharing agreement, citing North Carolina General Assembly funding cuts from 25% to 7.7% (which required $57.6 million in extra county transit funds), rigid legislative deadlines, the federal shutdown, and unexpected environmental assessment requirements. Commissioners voted unanimously (5-0) to approve disbanding the light rail cost-sharing agreement while committing to a 12-to-15-month Durham Transit Plan update, evaluating how to repurpose corridor investments, advancing commuter rail planning ($800,000 committed), and expanding public transit budget transparency online. The board concluded with a unanimous closed session on pending litigation (18-CVS-312) before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Community Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order at 7:01 PM, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Announcements included a Tax Administration Homestead exemption seminar for seniors, the FY19-20 online budget comment portal, the Kids Voting Durham youth survey, Microsoft Man Code Camp at NCCU, and board/commission vacancies.

agenda_items.title: Approval of February 11, 2019 and March 11, 2019 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the minutes of the February 11, 2019 and March 11, 2019 regular sessions.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations and Resolutions (Early Childhood, Child Abuse Prevention, Reentry Week, and 2020 Census)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented proclamations for Week of the Young Child (with Durham Partnership for Children and Durham Tech), Child Abuse Prevention Awareness Month (with DSS Director Ben Rose), and Reentry Week (read by Vice Chair James Hill). Chair Jacobs also read a resolution supporting the 2020 Census with Deborah Craig-Ray, setting an 82% response goal (up from 75% in 2010) and launching a Complete Count Committee for hard-to-count communities.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of 1% Public Art Allocation Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed how the 1% public art policy is applied across county capital projects. Vice Chair James Hill asked for clarification on project-by-project eligibility and noted that artistic selection should remain with arts professionals rather than becoming politicized.

agenda_items.title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Cost-Sharing Disbanding and Transit Plan Next Steps
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners reviewed why the Durham-Orange Light Rail project could no longer move forward under statutory deadlines after General Assembly funding cuts reduced state participation from 25% to 10% and then 7.7%—requiring $57.6 million in additional county transit funds—compounded by the six-week federal shutdown and an unexpected environmental assessment. The board voted 5-0 to approve disbanding the cost-sharing agreement, while committing to evaluate repurposing corridor investments, conduct a 12–15 month Durham Transit Plan update, publish transit spending data online, and advance regional commuter rail planning ($800,000 committed).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Litigation (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3) to consult with legal counsel regarding Francisco Rivera-Rodriguez v. Michael Andrews, Paul Aiken, Durham County, and Travelers Casualty and Surety Company (18-CVS-312). The board returned from closed session and adjourned.

votes.item_title: Approval of February 11, 2019 and March 11, 2019 Regular Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Unanimous approval of the February 11 and March 11, 2019 regular session minutes.

votes.item_title: Approval of Durham-Orange Light Rail Cost-Sharing Disbanding and Transit Plan Recommendation
votes.discussion_detail: Approved disbanding the Durham-Orange Light Rail cost-sharing interlocal agreement drafted with County Attorney Willie Darby while committing to repurpose corridor investments, update the Durham Transit Plan over 12–15 months, and advance commuter rail planning.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3))
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session under attorney-client privilege regarding 18-CVS-312.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC March 25, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 25, 2019 meeting, Chair Wendy Jacobs delivered the 2019 State of the County Address, highlighting county investments exceeding $150 million (over one-third of the budget) in public education, Durham Pre-K, Durham Tech College Promise, and upcoming capital needs for Northern High School and a new South Durham elementary school. Her address also reviewed the ACEs task force, AARP Age-Friendly Community certification, Youth Home and Detention Center facility planning, surplus property transfers for affordable housing, a 2050 100% renewable energy goal, the Data DCoNC dashboard, and a record 99.8% tax collection rate. Ceremonial recognitions honored National Service Recognition Day (AmeriCorps), County Government Month, and Women in Public Office Day. The board unanimously approved the consent agenda (Item 19-0113, February 2019 property tax releases and refunds, 5-0), approved the $50,000 Aetna-funded Durham Pre-K mini-grant program (5-0), heard budget comments from resident Michael Harris, and made appointments to four boards and commissions including the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority and Library Board of Trustees.

agenda_items.title: 2019 State of the County Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs delivered the 2019 State of the County Address after postponing a technical intro video. She emphasized shared prosperity across affordable housing, transit, and job training; over $150 million in education funding and upcoming CIP needs for Northern High School and a South Durham elementary school; the ACEs task force and AARP Age-Friendly certification; Youth Home and Detention Center upgrades; affordable housing surplus land transfers; the 2050 renewable energy resolution; and a 99.8% tax collection rate.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: National Service Recognition Day, County Government Month, and Women in Public Office Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board proclaimed National Service Recognition Day 2019 with Conservation Trust for North Carolina AmeriCorps representatives (noting six local AmeriCorps members and over $700,000 in federal funding), recognized County Government Month and the NACo 'Connecting the Unconnected' initiative, and proclaimed Women in Public Office Day 2019 with Vice Chair James Hill honoring women's leadership on the suffrage centennial.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Item 19-0113: Property Tax Releases and Refunds)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the single consent agenda item, Item 19-0113 covering property tax releases and refunds for February 2019.

agenda_items.title: Durham Pre-K Mini-Grant Program ($50,000 Aetna Grant)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the Durham Pre-K mini-grant program utilizing a $50,000 grant from Aetna alongside capacity-building and outcome indicator requirements for local organizations. Commissioners noted the agenda text should explicitly clarify the Aetna grant source rather than general fund dollars, then voted unanimously (5-0) to approve the funding item.

agenda_items.title: Supplemental Public Comment on Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Michael Harris addressed the board regarding taxpayer funding and urged commissioners to exercise frugality in county spending. Chair Jacobs thanked him for waiting to speak and explained that the regular budget public hearing had taken place earlier in the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After circulating the AARP Age-Friendly Community certification, the board announced appointments including Edward Rezuto (Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission), Camilla Mique (Library Board of Trustees), Edwin Bryson Jr. (Memorial Stadium Authority), and Patrick Hannah and David Morgan (Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority).

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC March 11, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 11, 2019 regular session, the Durham County Board of Commissioners postponed Item 19-0115 (My Brother's Keeper mini-grant program) to March 25 and unanimously approved the corrected January 28 regular session minutes (5-0) and February 4 work session minutes (5-0). Ceremonially, Vice Chair James Hill sponsored a Colorectal Cancer Awareness Month proclamation highlighting screening at age 45, and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton presented a resolution supporting Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (JCPC) allocation expansion to address nine years of flat base funding and the December 1, 2019 Raise the Age implementation, which staff was directed to send to NCACC, the Durham legislative delegation, and Public Safety Secretary Hooks. Staff also demonstrated the interactive Data DCoNC and Power BI Strategic Plan and Budget dashboards, including 10-year longitudinal NCACC peer-county tax and school spending comparisons. Following a unanimous closed session under attorney-client privilege (5-0), the board voted 5-0 to approve a Memorandum of Agreement with the State of North Carolina and voted 5-0 to authorize Chair Wendy Jacobs to execute the agreement.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment (Item 19-0115 Postponed), and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order, postponed Item 19-0115 (My Brother's Keeper mini-grant program) to March 25, and shared community announcements including Sheriff's Office $10 rabies clinics, safe internet exchange zones at the courthouse parking lot, LIEAP energy assistance through March 31, National Track & Field Championship registration, Alert Durham, and 43 county advisory boards.

agenda_items.title: Approval of January 28, 2019 Regular Session and February 4, 2019 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the January 28, 2019 regular session minutes with a minor correction (5-0) and subsequently approved the February 4, 2019 work session minutes (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Colorectal Cancer Awareness Month 2019
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill read the Colorectal Cancer Awareness Month proclamation emphasizing early screening starting at age 45, noting colorectal cancer is the second leading cause of cancer death for men and women combined. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow shared her family history and urged residents to get screened.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Supporting Juvenile Crime Prevention Council (JCPC) Allocation Expansion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton read a resolution urging the state to expand JCPC funding—unchanged for nine years—to support early intervention programs and the December 1, 2019 Raise the Age Juvenile Justice Reinvestment Act expansion to 16- and 17-year-olds. The board directed staff to transmit the resolution to NCACC's Kevin Leonard, the Durham legislative delegation, and NC Department of Public Safety Secretary Hooks.

agenda_items.title: Presentation: Data DCoNC Power BI Strategic Plan, Budget, and NCACC Comparison Dashboards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff demonstrated interactive Power BI visualizations embedded on the county budget page, including the Strategic Plan Dashboard across five goal areas, real-time adopted general fund expenditures (66% spent at 69.5% of the year across $228 million operating and $138 million personnel), and 10-year longitudinal NCACC Budget & Tax Survey comparisons of per-pupil school spending and tax rates across peer counties. Staff committed to emailing direct dashboard links to commissioners and improving homepage visibility.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3)) and Memorandum of Agreement with the State of North Carolina
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the request of County Attorney Lowell Siler, the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session for attorney-client consultation under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3). Returning to open session at 02:38:44, the board voted 5-0 to approve a Memorandum of Agreement with the State of North Carolina and voted 5-0 to authorize Chair Jacobs to execute the agreement.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC February 11, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 11, 2019 regular session, Chair Wendy Jacobs read a formal board statement condemning recent ICE enforcement actions in Durham affecting at least six families and affirming support for Sheriff Clarence F. Birkhead's policy refusing to honor ICE detainers or facilitate immigration apprehensions. The board unanimously approved the January 14, 2019 meeting minutes (5-0), presented the Resolution to Protect Food and Nutrition Services (SNAP) from Impact of Federal Government Shutdowns alongside DSS staff Rhonda Stevens, and fielded a pre-consent inquiry on Item 19-0079 (Durham Crisis Response Center grant extension and the Lethality Assessment Program). Later in the meeting, commissioners discussed partnering on state RAD advocacy and county land availability—while cautioning against cash commitments—for a $566 million public housing redevelopment effort addressing 60% unemployment among work-able public housing adults. Staff also briefed the board on Durham Pre-K expansion ($1,250/child/month reimbursement, 18 quality-improvement 'pipeline' classrooms, and 5 new classrooms starting in March) and the 2019 property reappraisal (showing 19.5% value growth excluding 3.5% natural growth and explaining the statutory revenue-neutral rate calculation in response to taxpayer concerns).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the meeting and read a board statement condemning recent ICE enforcement actions affecting at least six Durham families, noting they undermine trust in local law enforcement, and affirming the board's support for Sheriff Clarence F. Birkhead's policy not to honor ICE detainers. Announcements covered the Feb 12 DPS Town Hall at Neal Middle School, the Hayti Heritage Film Festival, the Durham YouthWork goal of 300+ paid summer internships, and recognition of Durham employers on a regional workplace list.

agenda_items.title: Approval of January 14, 2019 Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously (5-0) to approve the minutes of the January 14, 2019 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Resolution to Protect FNS/SNAP from Impact of Federal Government Shutdowns
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DSS staff member Rhonda Stevens spoke on behalf of Director Ben Rose, and Chair Jacobs read the resolution signed by all five commissioners urging federal lawmakers (Senators Burr and Tillis and Representatives Butterfield and Price) to classify SNAP as an essential service exempt from federal shutdowns, citing over 36,000 Durham County recipients and $4.5 million in monthly food and nutrition benefits.

disagreements.issue: Scope of Proposed Comprehensive Plan Policy Evaluating Affordable Housing Impacts of NPOs and Local Historic Districts
disagreements.summary: During consideration of the 2017 Evaluation and Assessment Report, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow objected to singling out only Neighborhood Protection Overlays (NPOs) and local historic districts for housing affordability impact evaluations and asked to sever or broaden the wording, whereas Commissioner Heidi Carter and Chair Wendy Jacobs argued the targeted policy was an appropriate informational step prompted by City Council's Old West Durham NPO debate.
disagreements.side_a_position: Sever the policy back to the Joint City-County Planning Committee (JCCPC) or broaden its wording to evaluate housing affordability impacts across all major land-use changes, not just NPOs and historic districts.
side_a_arguments: Citing Planning Commissioner Tom Miller's comments and National Trust/CityLab research, older smaller buildings in historic districts and NPOs often preserve naturally occurring affordable housing and prevent teardowns.
Targeting only NPOs and historic districts casts an unfair cloud over neighborhood preservation while ignoring rezonings (such as residential-to-commercial) that also affect housing affordability.
The proposed policy had not been discussed at JCCPC and lacked context in the report.
disagreements.side_b_position: Retain and approve the policy as drafted so planning staff evaluates the net impact of proposed NPOs and local historic districts on housing affordability and supply.
side_b_arguments: The policy grew directly out of City Council's Old West Durham NPO deliberations, where restrictions on accessory dwelling units and duplexes raised long-term housing supply concerns.
Planning staff already removed the earlier directive requiring staff to recommend denial, leaving only a neutral informational analysis that could also show positive affordability impacts.
Overlay districts impose broad area-wide restrictions distinct from individual parcel rezonings, and Durham City Council had already approved the report 7-0.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved by compromise without a split vote: planning staff agreed to consider proposing broadened policy language covering other land-use categories when returning to JCCPC with the evaluation methodology, after which Commissioner Reckhow moved adoption of the 2017 EAR resolution and it passed unanimously 5-0.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC January 14, 2019
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the January 14, 2019 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, opening with remarks by Jacobs and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton mourning recent gun and domestic violence—including the fatal shooting of a 22-year-old mother and her 10-month-old infant—alongside ceremonial proclamations for National Mentoring Month and Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. The board unanimously approved the December 20, 2018 minutes (5-0), reordered business items after public hearings (5-0), approved Consent Agenda items 18-1133 through 19-0030 (5-0), and approved pulled Item 18-1191 as amended (5-0) to rename the 'Durham-Orange fund' reference to 'Durham Transit Fund'. In three public hearings, the board unanimously approved UDO Text Amendment TC1800002 (Omnibus Changes 12, 5-0 on consistency and 5-0 on the ordinance), UDO Text Amendment TC1800008 (Text-Only Development Plans, 5-0 on consistency and 5-0 on the ordinance), and a $750,000 economic development incentive allocation for gene-therapy company AveXis (Project Bengal, 5-0) tied to a $60 million investment and 200 jobs. The board also reviewed a clean FY2018 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) audit from Cherry Bekaert, debated neighborhood-character versus aggressive housing-supply trade-offs during an Expanding Housing Choices briefing, outlined 2019 General Assembly legislative priorities, and entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) (5-0) before adjourning.

Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton shared a personal connection to the victims' family and urged the community to confront violence, after which Chair Jacobs announced the Jan. 15 MLK observance, Jan. 21 holiday closures, LEAP heating assistance, Golden Leaf Awards, Durham YouthWorks internships, Durham's 150th anniversary, and Alert Durham.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: On motion by Commissioner Heidi Carter and second by Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow, the board unanimously approved the minutes from its December 20, 2018 meeting.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs read a proclamation declaring January 2019 as National Mentoring Month in Durham County, noting a minor text correction from 'more likely' to 'less likely' regarding school truancy statistics. Charles Hamilton Houston Foundation Executive Director Dewarren Langley and representatives from more than a dozen local mentoring, school, workforce, and violence-interruption organizations gave brief remarks on coordinating youth mentorship, with Commissioners Ellen W. Reckhow and Brenda A. Howerton linking the work to the county's ACEs Task Force.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow moved to adjust the agenda to place the three regular business items (18-1198, 19-0002, and 19-0033) after the three public hearings, recommending that order as standard practice going forward. MLK Steering Committee Chair Reverend Lucas and committee members thanked commissioners for funding 12 student scholarships and outlined the week's commemorative schedule including the wreath-laying, prayer breakfast, unity march, Book Harvest Day of Service, Jubilee Home workday, and religious service.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 18-1133 through 19-0030) and Pulled Item 18-1191 (Transit Cost-Share Amendment)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Before voting, commissioners highlighted Bull City 150 sponsorship, a housing-rehab grant study (Item 0022) showing half of Durham households are housing- and transit-cost burdened, the updated firearm discharge ordinance (Item 19-0029), federal shutdown impacts on DSS food-assistance funding (secured through February), and continuation funding for the Durham Integrated Violence Response System grant (Item 0006). The board unanimously approved Consent Agenda items 18-1133 through 19-0030 excluding pulled Item 18-1191 (5-0), then unanimously approved Item 18-1191 as amended (5-0) to replace a reference to the 'Durham-Orange fund' with 'Durham Transit Fund' on page 1 of the contractor-change amendment.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Adoption: UDO Text Amendment TC1800002 (Omnibus Changes 12)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Michael Stock presented UDO Text Amendment TC1800002 containing technical corrections and minor policy updates—including removing parking minimums on very narrow infill lots and expanding the affordable housing density bonus from 1:1 to 2:1—noting that Neighborhood Protection Overlay process changes (Section 8) were removed by Planning Commission and referred back to staff. After brief questions and a public hearing with no speakers, the board unanimously adopted both the Statement of Consistency (5-0) and the ordinance amendment (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Adoption: UDO Text Amendment TC1800008 (Text-Only Development Plans)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Michael Stock presented UDO Text Amendment TC1800008 establishing a limited text-only development plan option for zoning map change requests to allow proffers limiting permitted uses under Article 5, previously recommended 12-0 by the Planning Commission. Chair Wendy Jacobs praised the streamlined option as user-friendly and less costly for applicants, and following a public hearing with no speakers, the board unanimously adopted the N.C.G.S. 153A-341 Statement of Consistency (5-0) and the ordinance amendment (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing and Approval: $750,000 Economic Development Incentive for AveXis (Project Bengal)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Director Andy Miracle presented a $750,000 economic development investment allocation for gene-therapy firm AveXis (Project Bengal), contingent on a minimum $60 million investment and 200 new jobs averaging ~$76,000 in annual wages alongside workforce partnerships with Durham Public Schools CTE, Durham Tech, and NCWorks and MWBE purchasing commitments. Greater Durham Chamber of Commerce representative Jeff Durham spoke in support during the public hearing, commissioners commended the binding community-benefit and living-wage provisions while confirming the final contract will return to the board, and the board voted 5-0 to approve the allocation.

agenda_items.title: Presentation: FY2018 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) and External Audit
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Susan Tezai introduced Cherry Bekaert engagement partner Scott Duda, who reported unmodified ('clean') financial statement and Yellow Book audit opinions for FY2018, no management letter or material weaknesses, four internal control significant deficiencies across grant compliance testing (including one repeat finding from 2017), and timely Local Government Commission submission with zero LGC comments. Commissioners questioned retiree health benefit increases under GASB 75, >10% budget underspending variances in General Administration and Economic/Physical Development, and a $16 million DSS general fund amendment reduction, requesting dedicated CAFR review time at the upcoming budget retreat.

agenda_items.title: Presentation and Discussion: Expanding Housing Choices (Missing Middle UDO Proposals)

Commissioners debated the trade-offs extensively: Ellen W. Reckhow raised concerns about overriding Neighborhood Protection Overlays and small-lot rows tearing neighborhood fabric; Heidi Carter urged aggressive supply expansion over preserving neighborhood fabric; James Hill warned against absentee investors accelerating gentrification in lower-income areas; and Chair Wendy Jacobs highlighted ADU design/financing pilots, transit access, and revisiting the three-unrelated-occupant cap.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: County legislative staff briefed commissioners ahead of the January 22 legislative breakfast with Durham's General Assembly delegation—noting newly seated Representatives Zack Hawkins and Robert Reives II and the end of the legislative supermajority—and outlined initial priorities across criminal justice, education, human services, and transportation. Commissioners requested adding or emphasizing funding for Raise the Age youth detention/home facilities, drug and mental health treatment courts, additional Assistant District Attorneys, City-backed expungement legislation, K-3 class-size flexibility, a $1.3B statewide K-12 school construction bond, authority to convey school property for teacher housing, Medicaid expansion, opioid funding, tenant eviction reform, and increasing state transit funding above 4%.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) to discuss economic development incentives and the location or expansion of industries or businesses. disagreements.issue: Neighborhood Character Protection vs. Aggressive Missing-Middle Housing Supply in Expanding Housing Choices
disagreements.summary: During the Expanding Housing Choices briefing, commissioners diverged on how aggressively to loosen urban-tier zoning rules: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow and Vice Chair James Hill emphasized neighborhood fabric, Neighborhood Protection Overlays (NPOs), and gentrification/absentee-investor risks, while Commissioner Heidi Carter urged prioritizing maximum housing supply and future affordability over existing neighborhood preservation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Prioritize protecting existing neighborhood fabric, honoring Neighborhood Protection Overlays, and guarding against speculative investor conversions and displacement in lower-income neighborhoods.
side_a_arguments: Overriding NPO provisions undermines extensive community work put into overlays like Old West Durham and Tuscaloosa-Lakewood.
Dividing a block face into six small lots in a row would create a tear in the fabric of established neighborhoods; clustered cottage courts or zero-lot-line designs would be more context-sensitive.
Without owner-occupancy rules, outside investors in less affluent neighborhoods could buy properties solely to maximize units without caring about neighborhood character, compounding gentrification.
disagreements.side_b_position: Pursue missing-middle housing supply and urban-tier density as aggressively as possible to address Durham's affordability crisis for future and current residents.
side_b_arguments: Expanding housing options and missing-middle supply should be the board's primary driver rather than preserving existing neighborhood fabric through overlays.
With 160,000 new residents projected over 25–30 years, failing to expand in-town supply will drive worse unaffordability, sprawl, and climate/infrastructure costs.
Suburban neighborhoods should also be examined for duplex and townhome opportunities where covenants do not prohibit them.
disagreements.resolution: Informational work-session discussion with no formal vote; Planning Director Patrick Young committed to refining context-sensitive standards with neighborhood groups ahead of the February 12, 2019 Planning Commission public hearing and April/May 2019 board vote.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Dec 20 Live
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the December 20, 2018 Durham County Board of Commissioners regular meeting, held at 2:00 p.m. after Monday's session was rescheduled due to a snowstorm. The board unanimously approved adding an Eno River Association presentation (5-0), approved the November 26, 2018 minutes (5-0), and passed all consent agenda items except Item 18-1124 (5-0), highlighting eight grant-funded items across departments including the Sheriff's Office and Public Health. After amending the 2019 board calendar (Item 18-1124) to correct NCACC Legislative Goals Conference dates, reschedule a June 13 budget work session, and add an August 13 joint city-county meeting, the board approved the calendar (5-0) and authorized moving forward with a $35,000 Age-Friendly Durham Master Aging Plan following an update from the Durham Center for Senior Life (5-0). Following commissioner comments on surplus property marketing and delinquent tax foreclosure policies, Open Space and Trails Commission appointments, and a closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6), the four remaining commissioners unanimously appointed Teresa Harrison as Interim Tax Administrator (4-0; Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton had departed prior to closed session).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Public Charge, Pledge of Allegiance, Agenda Adjustments, and Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the rescheduled December 20, 2018 meeting to order at 2:00 p.m., read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The board voted 5-0 to add an Eno River Association presentation to ceremonial items, followed by announcements on FEMA disaster rental assistance, the Welcome Baby coat drive, and LIEAP energy bill assistance.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 26, 2018 Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered the minutes from the November 26, 2018 meeting. Commissioner James Hill moved approval, Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow seconded, and the motion passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Presentations: Eno River Association and Transportation Champions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Eno River Association Executive Director Robin Jacobs and Milo Pyne addressed the board during the annual ceremonial presentation. Chair Jacobs also recognized Durham County ACCESS transit users and transportation champions for providing critical mobility to work and medical care.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 18-1124)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners pulled Item 18-1124 (the 2019 board calendar) for separate edits and highlighted Item 18-1180 and eight grant-funded consent items benefiting departments including the Sheriff's Office and Public Health, as well as a private-sector Credit Suisse grant. The board unanimously approved all remaining consent agenda items through 18-119D.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 18-1124: 2019 Board Calendar and Excused Absence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners corrected the 2019 calendar dates for the NCACC Legislative Goals Conference (January 10-11), removed the June 13 six-hour budget work session for rescheduling due to Commissioner Reckhow's absence, fixed the Monday August 12 regular session label, and added an August 13 joint city-county meeting. The board approved the amended calendar 5-0 and granted Commissioner Reckhow an excused absence for a January 9 joint meeting 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Durham Center for Senior Life Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Judy Kinney presented an update on the Durham Center for Senior Life, detailing its downtown center, adult day program, and congregate meal sites on Fayetteville Street, JFK Towers, North Roxboro, and Little River. She noted an annual budget just under $1,650,000, with 70% derived from government contracts and relatively flat funding over the prior four years.

agenda_items.title: Age-Friendly Durham Master Aging Plan Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented plans to develop an Age-Friendly Durham Master Aging Plan following the prior livability assessment, outlining a $35,000 project budget largely for contractor facilitation of roughly 25 meetings and steering committee coordination with Partnership for Seniors. The board voted unanimously to approve moving forward with the plan.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Comments, Boards and Commissions Appointments, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Reckhow raised accelerating surplus property marketing with Joint City-County Planning and DFI and asked for a report on tax foreclosure policy for properties delinquent more than a year. The board announced the selection of Dave Connolly and Tisha Wymore to the Open Space and Trails Commission, after which Commissioner Howerton stated she was leaving and would not stay for closed session; the board then entered closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6).

agenda_items.title: Appointment of Interim Tax Administrator
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon returning from closed session and reporting that staff had been given direction, Chair Jacobs entertained a motion to appoint Teresa Harrison as Interim Tax Administrator. The four remaining commissioners approved the appointment unanimously before adjourning.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Work Session Dec 3 LIve
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 3, 2018 organizational work session, County Attorney Lowell Siler presided over receipt of Soil and Water Conservation District Supervisor election certificates for Natalie Murdock and David Harris and the unanimous re-election of Chair Wendy Jacobs (5-0), after which Chair Jacobs presided and Vice Chair James Hill was unanimously re-elected (5-0). The board approved public official bonds (5-0), witnessed the swearing-in of Murdock and Harris by District Court Judge Jaretta Walker, and voted unanimously to suspend the rules (5-0) and set the salary of the incoming sheriff (5-0). During work session review, commissioners disagreed over the proposed 2019 meeting calendar—Commissioner Heidi Carter declined to approve past June and proposed adding a second monthly work session on Thursday afternoons, whereas Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton urged approving at least through August for advance scheduling—leaving the calendar deferred to January. Commissioners also questioned capital cost overruns on Item 1130 ($2.7M over budget note), Item 1156 (over $4M total for Admin II 7th floor upfit), and Item 1158 (Detention Center HVAC grille and bunk bed safety modifications), directed the County Attorney to bring back the updated firearms ordinance, and entered closed session (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Organizational Business: Election Certificates, Selection of Chair and Vice Chair, Public Official Bonds, and Oaths
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Attorney Lowell Siler presided for the annual receipt of election certificates for Soil and Water Conservation District Supervisors Natalie Murdock and David Harris and conducted the election of Wendy Jacobs as Chair (5-0). Chair Jacobs then presided over the election of James Hill as Vice Chair (5-0), approval of public official bonds (5-0), and oaths administered by Judge Jaretta Walker.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident John Tarantino of 515 North Hyde Park spoke regarding traffic congestion and difficulties navigating NC-147 construction.

agenda_items.title: Suspend Rules and Set Salary of Incoming Sheriff
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs entertained a request to suspend the rules and act immediately on setting the salary of the incoming sheriff. The board voted 5-0 to suspend the rules and then voted 5-0 to approve and set the incoming sheriff's salary.

agenda_items.title: Discussion of 2019 Board Meeting Calendar and Second Monthly Work Session Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners debated the draft 2019 meeting schedule, with Commissioner Heidi Carter declining to vote past June and renewing her proposal to move work sessions to the Thursday afternoons following Monday regular meetings and add a second monthly work session. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton asked to approve at least through August so commissioners could plan ahead, and the board deferred action until January.

agenda_items.title: Review of Capital Budget Overruns, Admin II 7th Floor Upfit, and Detention Center Safety Upgrades
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners questioned Item 1130 ($65,000 addition and a $2.7 million over-budget reference), Item 1156 (Admin II 7th floor LOBs-funded upfit pushing total project cost over $4 million), and Item 1158 (Detention Center HVAC grilles, bunk bed safety modifications, and pod staff desks with C2 Wilson targeted for October 2019 completion). Commissioner Reckhow pressed staff to avoid letting surplus property sales languish so one-time revenues could help offset capital overruns.

agenda_items.title: Directives Follow-Up (Firearms Ordinance) and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners asked the County Attorney to bring back clarifications to the firearms ordinance—citing a Rougemont complaint dating back to early 2017 and preempted provisions—for the next regular meeting. Rather than recessing until 2:00 p.m., the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) and (a)(3).

side_b_arguments: Commissioners need confirmed dates through at least August to organize personal and professional calendars without shifting meeting dates.
disagreements.resolution: No vote was taken; Chair Wendy Jacobs and staff agreed to return at a January meeting with revised calendar options and printed schedule comparisons.
