meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Nov 26 Live
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the November 26, 2018 regular meeting of the Durham County Board of Commissioners. The board unanimously moved the ACEs Task Force resolution from regular business to ceremonial items (5-0), approved the October 22, November 5, and November 13, 2018 meeting minutes (5-0) while requesting future minutes record adjournment times, and honored the late Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong ('Coach Doc') and Captain Aleem for rescuing a mother and two children on I-85. Later in the session, the board unanimously approved submitting two amended NCACC legislative goals—on resiliency and volunteer firefighters—along with previously passed SNAP farm bill language (5-0), declining to draft a new Medicaid expansion goal due to the end-of-month deadline. Commissioners also received the County Manager's updated Power BI quarterly management report under the Managing for Results framework, clarified advisory board attendance rules, and appointed members to four boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the November 26, 2018 meeting, read the public charge, and led the Pledge of Allegiance. The board voted 5-0 to move the ACEs Task Force resolution to ceremonial items, shared community announcements including the November 30 light rail draft EIS comment deadline, and approved the October 22, November 5, and November 13 minutes 5-0 while requesting that future minutes include adjournment times.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolution Honoring Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong and Recognition of Captain Aleem
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented a resolution honoring the life and legacy of Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong ('Coach Doc'), a pioneering Duke pediatric cardiologist and 37-year Durham Striders coach and team physician who passed away on October 7, 2018, accepted by Durham Striders Director Frank Davis. Commissioners also recognized Captain Aleem for rescuing two children and their mother from an overturned vehicle on I-85.

agenda_items.title: NCACC Legislative Goals Submission (Resiliency, Volunteer Firefighters, and SNAP Farm Bill Resolution)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following discussion of NCACC legislative goal submissions before the end-of-November deadline, Commissioner Heidi Carter suggested adding SNAP benefits and Medicaid expansion. Because time did not permit drafting a new Medicaid expansion proposal, the board voted 5-0 to submit the two amended goals on resiliency and volunteer firefighters together with previously adopted SNAP farm bill language.

agenda_items.title: Quarterly Management Report (Managing for Results / Power BI Rollout)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The County Manager presented the second evolution of the quarterly management report powered by Power BI under the Managing for Results strategy. The dashboard enables drill-downs into five-year expenditure and revenue trends, adopted budgets, departmental FTEs, and strategic plan performance metrics.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Comments and Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners offered brief remarks on a recent D.C. trip and transit/zoning articles and clarified with County Attorney Lowell Siler that advisory board removal thresholds require exceeding 50% absences, three consecutive unexcused absences, or five total absences. The board appointed Deidre Thornlow (Nursing Home CAC), David Morgan (Planning Commission), Hannah Horn, Fred Mayak, and Natalie Murdock (Transportation Advisory Board), and Elizabeth Morel (Women's Commission).

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Nov 13 Live
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the November 13, 2018 regular meeting of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, shifted to Tuesday due to the Veterans Day holiday. The board unanimously approved five sets of September and October 2018 minutes (5-0), proclaimed the Durham NC Chapter of The Links, Incorporated Day, and adopted a solemn resolution honoring Lewis McCallen, a founding member of the Bull City United violence prevention program who died October 28, 2018. Commissioners unanimously approved Consent Agenda items 18-1025 through 18-1113 (5-0)—highlighting the affordable housing policy, surplus property, and a renewable energy resolution—and received briefings on comprehensive OB clinic ACEs screenings and Durham Pre-K integration into NC Pre-K ahead of its winter 2019 launch. Concluding a public hearing with no speakers, the board voted unanimously to adopt a statement of consistency (5-0) and an ordinance approving Unified Development Ordinance text amendment TC1800006 allowing private streets in cross-county developments (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of September-October 2018 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the November 13, 2018 meeting, noted announcements including the November 19 Veterans celebration at HHS and the light rail feedback deadline, and called for approval of the September 4, September 11, September 24, October 1, and October 8 minutes. Commissioners unanimously approved the minutes 5-0 while asking the clerk to follow up on outstanding September directives to the sustainability manager.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: Durham Chapter of The Links and Resolution Honoring Lewis McCallen
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board proclaimed Durham NC Chapter of The Links, Incorporated Day recognizing over 60 years of community service. Commissioners then read a resolution honoring Lewis McCallen, a founding member of Bull City United who worked to mediate violent conflicts from October 2016 until his sudden death at age 39 on October 28, 2018, with family and Bull City United staff present.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 18-1025 through 18-1113)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: No items were pulled from the consent agenda, and the board voted 5-0 to approve Items 18-1025 through 18-1113. Chair Jacobs highlighted key items on the consent agenda including the affordable housing policy, surplus property, a renewable energy resolution, and grant awards.

agenda_items.title: Health Quality, ACEs Screening, and Durham Pre-K Implementation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners discussed healthcare provider quality and the ACEs Task Force pilot integrating emotional and mental health assessments in the OB clinic. Staff also presented an overview of Durham Pre-K integration with NC Pre-K (583 state-funded spaces across community programs, DPS, and Head Start, plus 191 Head Start slots and Dolly Parton's Imagination Library) ahead of new Durham Pre-K seats opening in winter 2019.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC1800006 (Private Streets)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pat Young of the Planning Department presented TC1800006, a privately initiated text amendment by Mitch Craig of CE Group to allow private streets in Durham County developments that cross a county line from an adjacent jurisdiction where private streets already exist, narrowed after Planning Commission review to include engineering certification and 20-25 year durability criteria. meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Oct 22 Live
meetings.executive_summary: Vice Chair James Hill presided over the October 22, 2018 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners while Chair Wendy Jacobs had an excused absence to attend the Rail-Volution conference. The four present commissioners unanimously approved seven sets of May through August 2018 meeting minutes (4-0) and approved the consent agenda (4-0) after discussing contract phase structures and work session scheduling. Ceremonial items included proclaiming November 11, 2018 as Bells Across Durham Day for the World War I centennial—accepted by former City Council member Eddie Davis—and honoring the late Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong. The board held a public hearing with no speakers on the 2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values (no action required until November), heard a 2020 Census Complete Count Committee briefing in which County Manager Wendell Davis pledged a marketing budget amendment, and made appointments to six advisory boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of May-August 2018 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair James Hill called the October 22, 2018 meeting to order at 7:02 p.m., read the public charge, led announcements including encouraging citizens to vote, and presided over approval of seven sets of minutes (May 22, May 24, May 31, June 4, and June 14 budget work sessions; July 23 regular session; and August 6 work session). The board passed the minutes unanimously 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Bells Across Durham Day Proclamation and Tribute to Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow read a proclamation designating November 11, 2018 as Bells Across Durham Day to mark the 100th anniversary of the World War I Armistice, with former City Council member Eddie Davis speaking on the simultaneous bell-ringing initiative. The board also presented a tribute honoring Duke pediatric cardiologist and Durham Striders co-leader Dr. Brenda Estelle Armstrong following her passing on October 7, 2018.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners questioned why a contract listed eight service phases while the county was paying for a smaller portion and reiterated support for adding a second work session so consent items can be vetted in advance. The board then voted 4-0 to approve the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: 2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Hill opened and closed the public hearing on the 2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values with no speakers signed up or rising to comment. Staff noted two citizen emails had been received and answered and stated that no board vote was required until adoption in November.

agenda_items.title: 2020 Census Complete Count Committee and Recruitment Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: U.S. Census Bureau representatives Laura McCready and regional recruitment staff requested county participation in a Complete Count Committee with liaison Ms. Hines, marketing funds, and outreach to count underserved and homeless populations ahead of opening a local census office in Durham needing at least 348 applicants. County Manager Wendell Davis committed to returning with a budget amendment for census outreach.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff announced the board's voting results appointing Tamario Alston and Vicky Winters to the Adult Care Home CAC, Charles Douglas to the City-County Appearance Commission, Jessica Uba to the Dangerous Dog Appeal Board, Amanda Wire and Eric Zog to the Nursing Home CAC, Milton Gilder to the Transportation Advisory Board, and Michelle Laws to the Women's Commission.

votes.item_title: Approval of May-August 2018 Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Chair Wendy Jacobs had an excused absence (approved Oct 8, 2018) to attend the Rail-Volution conference. Mover and seconder were not named in the audio transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved minutes from May 22, May 24, May 31, June 4, and June 14 budget work sessions, July 23 regular session, and August 6 work session.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Oct 8 Live
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the October 8, 2018 regular meeting of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, opening after a closed session with an apology to guests for the 15-minute delay. The board adjusted the agenda to move pulled consent items after regular business (5-0) and postponed Item 18-1021 (the 2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values public hearing) to October 22 (5-0), approved March 2018 minutes while asking the clerk for a catch-up plan (5-0), honored the Bouncing Bulldogs world-champion jump rope team, and paid tribute to the late Dr. Brenda Armstrong. After receiving an update on Durham-Orange Light Rail operations and maintenance facility rezoning and public workshops, commissioners unanimously adopted Item 18-1063 establishing an Enterprise Fund Capital Reserve Fund for sewer System Development Fees in compliance with state law (5-0). At the County Manager's request to ensure clarity following pulled items, the board re-affirmed all consent agenda items including $6.5 million for multiple capital projects (5-0) and granted Chair Jacobs an excused absence for October 22 (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustments, Announcements, and Approval of March 2018 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning from closed session, Chair Jacobs apologized for the delay, led the Pledge of Allegiance, and presided over unanimous votes to move pulled consent items after regular business (5-0) and delay Item 18-1021 (2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values public hearing) to October 22 (5-0). Following announcements including free GoDurham/GoTriangle Youth GoPasses, the board approved March 2018 minutes 5-0 and asked Clerk Monica Toomer for a plan to catch up on remaining old minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolution Honoring the Bouncing Bulldogs and Tribute to Dr. Brenda Armstrong
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow presented a resolution honoring the Bouncing Bulldogs jump rope team and founder Ray Frederick Jr., celebrating their 2018 Double Dutch Contest World first-place victory in Tokyo in the 12-and-under Fusion category. Vice Chair James Hill and commissioners also paid tribute to Dr. Brenda Armstrong following her passing and requested a formal memorial resolution.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review (Late Additions and DPS Laptop/Chromebook Item)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter flagged multiple late consent items not reviewed in advance, including a Durham Public Schools request regarding laptops and Chromebooks that lacked lease amounts and quantities in the amendment backup. The remaining consent items were subsequently confirmed later in the meeting.

agenda_items.title: Durham-Orange Light Rail Project Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff provided an update on GoTriangle's rail operations and maintenance facility site acquisition, Planning Commission and City Council rezoning/annexation steps for water service, workforce development alignment, and public design workshops scheduled for November 3, 5, and 8. Commissioner Howerton also flagged transit stop conditions at Phoenix Square and Fayetteville Street.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Item 18-1063: Enterprise Fund Capital Reserve Fund for System Development Fees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff explained that following 2017 legislation (N.C.G.S. 162A Article 8), a W.R. Martin fee study, and UNC School of Government guidance, the county must establish a Capital Reserve Fund within the Sewer Enterprise Fund before collecting and expending System Development Fees adopted in the FY2019 budget. The board voted 5-0 to adopt the resolution along with the Capital Improvement Plan and supplemental materials.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence, Agenda Order Discussion, and Re-affirmation of Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 5-0 to excuse Chair Jacobs from the October 22 meeting to attend the Rail-Volution conference in Pittsburgh and discussed keeping pulled consent items earlier in future agendas while Commissioner Carter advocated adding a second work session. At County Manager Wendell Davis's request to ensure clarity on Item 091 ($6.5 million for capital projects), the board voted 5-0 to re-affirm approval of all consent agenda items.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved Commissioner Heidi Carter's suggestion to place pulled consent items after regular business items.

votes.notes: Mover transcribed as 'Commissioner Howard' and seconder as 'Commissioner Recco' in ASR.
votes.discussion_detail: At the County Attorney's request, removed Item 18-1021 from the October 8 agenda and rescheduled the public hearing for October 22, 2018.

votes.notes: Mover transcribed as 'commissioner. Rec house'; seconder name was cut off in transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved backlog March 2018 minutes and directed the clerk to present a catch-up plan for older minutes.

votes.notes: Mover transcribed as 'commissioner Rekow' and seconder as 'commissioner Howard' in ASR.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC Sept 24 LIve
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs presided over the September 24, 2018 regular session of the Durham County Board of Commissioners after returning from closed session. The board thanked first responders and emergency staff for Hurricane Florence preparedness, approved the August 27, 2018 minutes as amended (5-0), and issued proclamations for Minority Enterprise Development Week, National Community Planning Month (marking the 30th anniversary of the merged City-County Planning Department), and domestic/care workers. After pulling Item 18-0995 to reconcile a 75% advisory board attendance requirement, the board approved Consent Agenda items 18-1036 through 18-1049 (5-0) and heard Tax Administrator Kim Simpson introduce the 2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values. Following a public hearing with no speakers on UDO Text Amendment TC1800003—updating FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) panels effective October 19, 2018 to preserve National Flood Insurance Program eligibility—the board unanimously adopted the statement of consistency (5-0) and the UDO Article 8 ordinance (5-0), and appointed residents to five advisory boards and commissions.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Emergency Preparedness Announcements, and Approval of August 27, 2018 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After adjourning from closed session, Chair Wendy Jacobs opened the September 24, 2018 meeting, praised county first responders and emergency management for Hurricane Florence response during National Preparedness Month, and shared announcements including the Inter-Faith Food Shuttle Child Food Hub opening and Alert Durham. The board approved the August 27, 2018 minutes as amended 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: MED Week, National Community Planning Month, and Domestic Workers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board proclaimed October 1-5, 2018 as Minority Enterprise Development Week (highlighting the county's MWBE ordinance), October 2018 as National Community Planning Month (celebrating the 30th anniversary of the merged City-County Planning Department), and honored domestic and care workers in the legacy of Dorothy Bolden.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Excluding Item 18-0995) and 2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 18-0995 was pulled for wording clarification on an advisory board's 75% attendance requirement, and the board voted 5-0 to approve Consent Agenda items 18-1036 through 18-1049. Tax Administrator Kim Simpson then briefed the board and public on the 2019 Reappraisal Schedule of Values and offered community outreach to civic groups.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: UDO Text Amendment TC1800003 (FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map Updates)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff and County Engineer Ryan Eaves presented TC1800003, adopting revised FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) panels effective October 19, 2018 so Durham County maintains National Flood Insurance Program eligibility; the maps added over 300 acres to the Special Flood Hazard Area while removing 271 buildings and adding 146. After opening and closing the public hearing with no speakers, the board voted 5-0 to adopt the statement of consistency and 5-0 to adopt the UDO Article 8 ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Boards and Commissions Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff announced the board's appointment results: Margery Frazier and Shelby Agree (Adult Care Home CAC), Nicole McCoy (Audit Oversight Committee), David Atwater (Dangerous Dog Appeal Board), Matt Bouchard, Katie Hamilton, and David DeBerry (Historic Preservation Commission), and Sarah Bosch (Women's Commission).

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC July 23, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At the July 23, 2018 regular session presided over by Chair Wendy Jacobs, the Durham County Board of Commissioners approved the March 8 work session and June 11 and June 25 regular session minutes (5-0), adopted consent agenda items 18-0897 through 18-0916 after deferring item 18-0887 to the August work session (5-0), and recognized community matriarchs Mrs. Peggy Johnson Tapp (posthumously) and Mrs. Cora Jones Boothe McCloy on her 100th birthday. Following joint public hearings with Economic Development Director Andy Miracle and Greater Durham Chamber of Commerce CEO Geoff Durham, the board unanimously approved (5-0) local match allocations for Job Development Investment Grant awards to AveXis, Inc. ($175,000 match donated by Clarion Partners), LabCorp ($220,000 match donated by Karlin Real Estate), and Sensus USA ($50,000 match), along with a completion-date amendment to January 1, 2019 for Austin Lawrence Partners East LLC. After making appointments to eight advisory boards and committees and returning from closed session, the board approved a motion moved by Ellen W. Reckhow and seconded by Heidi Carter setting the County Attorney's salary at $204,811 effective on his anniversary date by a 4-1 voice vote (Ayes: Ellen W. Reckhow, Heidi Carter, and two other commissioners; Nay: one unidentified commissioner not named in the audio record).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Adjustment, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order at 7:05 p.m. following a closed-session recess, noted the board would return to closed session later in the evening, and shared announcements on the Complete Streets workshop, East Main Street 300/500 parking lot mixed-use/affordable housing input sessions, Durham Neighborhood College, summer reading, and the City-County Planning zoning survey. The board unanimously approved the March 8, 2018 work session minutes and the June 11 and June 25, 2018 regular session minutes, while flagging follow-up on the Park Center agreement.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comment Period: ABC Board Reappointment Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citizen Jackie Wagstaff addressed the board requesting reappointment to a second term on the Durham Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Board, noting that reappointment was necessary for her to remain in line to sit on the state ABC Board of Directors.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Resolutions: Mrs. Peggy Johnson Tapp and Mrs. Cora Jones Boothe McCloy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board presented a resolution honoring the late Mrs. Peggy Johnson Tapp, co-operator of the Chicken Hut restaurant and community gathering place, followed by Vice Chair James Hill reading a resolution celebrating the 100th birthday of longtime Durham resident and entrepreneur Mrs. Cora Jones Boothe McCloy.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 18-0897 through 18-0916; Item 18-0887 Deferred)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs removed item 18-0887 from the agenda for consideration at the August work session. The board then unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0897 through 18-0916.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearings: Economic Development Local Match Grants (18-0909, 18-0910, 18-0911) and Austin Lawrence Partners East Amendment (18-0914)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Economic Development Director Andy Miracle and Chamber of Commerce CEO Geoff Durham presented four items: JDIG local match recognitions for AveXis, Inc. ($175,000 Clarion Partners donation; $55 million investment and 100 jobs), LabCorp at Parmer RTP ($220,000 Karlin Real Estate donation; $30 million investment and 422 jobs), and Sensus USA at Keystone Park ($50,000 match; $4 million investment and 301 jobs), plus a contract amendment extending Austin Lawrence Partners East LLC's completion date from July 1, 2018 to January 1, 2019 due to a mechanical contractor failure. Commissioners questioned job qualifications and inclusive local workforce outreach through Durham Tech before unanimously approving all four items in separate motions.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Prior to announcing ballot results, a commissioner raised concern about low Durham residency among primary and secondary recommendations for an advisory body. Results were announced for appointments to the ABC Board, Convention Center Authority, Criminal Justice Advisory Committee, Dangerous Dog Appeal Board, Durham-Wake Counties Research and Production Service District, Environmental Affairs Board, Library Board of Trustees, and Sports Commission.

agenda_items.title: Post-Closed Session Action: County Attorney Salary Adjustment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a closed-session recess beginning at 01:16:54, the board returned to open session and considered setting the County Attorney's salary at $204,811 effective on his anniversary date. The motion carried on a 4-1 voice vote, with one unidentified commissioner voting in opposition.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC June 25, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: With Commissioner Heidi Carter absent on an excused absence previously approved on June 11, the four attending members of the Durham County Board of Commissioners unanimously adopted the FY 2018-19 Budget Ordinance (4-0) after reducing the County Manager's proposed property tax increase from 1.9 cents to 1 cent. Before voting on the budget, Chair Wendy Jacobs, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Brenda A. Howerton delivered an extensive board statement responding to June 11 public hearing testimony on Detention Center safety and suicide prevention, detailing 16 years of CIP and operating allocations ($137,000 for HVAC security vents, $90,000 for window fixes, $1.5 million for Durham Youth Home expansion, and over $3.5 million annually for inmate physical and mental healthcare). The board also unanimously (4-0) approved consent items 18-0848 through 18-0892 (including the southern Durham fire consolidation ILA with the City and a Durham Pre-K expansion contract), installment financing and reimbursement resolutions under G.S. 160A-20 (refinancing $43.5 million for Admin II and funding jail, emergency communications, and fire district capital projects), and post-closed-session salaries for Tax Collector/Administrator Kim Simpson ($145,306) and Register of Deeds Sharon Davis ($100,515).

agenda_items.title: Adjournment from Pre-Meeting Closed Session, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 4-0 to adjourn from closed session, read the public charge, and shared announcements covering the 15-501 corridor study, JCPC community conversation, HIV testing, summer reading, Durham Neighborhood College, and the zoning choices survey. Commissioner Howerton raised an NC AFL-CIO petition regarding Kroger's closure of 14 Triangle stores (4 not converting to Harris Teeter or Food Lion), and the board approved April 2 work session and May 29 regular session minutes 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognition: Durham County EMS AHA Mission: Lifeline Gold Plus Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim EMS Director Kevin Underhill and staff were recognized for receiving the American Heart Association Mission: Lifeline Gold Plus award, the highest EMS recognition level. Underhill highlighted 256 STEMI transports out of 1,700+ acute coronary syndrome dispatches in 2017 and a 17% cardiac arrest survival rate compared to the 10.4% national average.

agenda_items.title: Board Statement on Durham County Detention Center Safety, Suicide Prevention, and Youth Home Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Jacobs delivered a detailed statement on behalf of the board addressing June 11 public hearing concerns over inmate safety in the Detention Center. Staff's review back to 2002 found that $40,000 window and $1.23 million air vent grille proposals in the 2004–2013 CIP were never brought forward as capital project amendments, while the county subsequently funded $137,000 for HVAC security vents (80+ cells completed by March 2017), $90,000 for completed cell window fixes, $87,600 and $1.5 million toward expanding the Durham Youth Home to 24 beds ahead of Raise the Age, $544,542 for jail mental health services, and over $3 million for inmate physical health care; Commissioners Reckhow and Howerton expressed regret for not responding directly to the mother at the June 11 hearing.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Review and Approval (Items 18-0848 through 18-0892, Excluding Pulled Item 18-0881)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Reckhow highlighted the fire service consolidation ILA with the City of Durham (18-0848), the Child Care Services Association Pre-K expansion contract (18-0866; 13 new and 25 enhanced classrooms), and requested follow-up on Greater Durham Chamber of Commerce workforce readiness resources (18-0877); Chair Jacobs highlighted the Student U MOU for W.G. Pearson School. Commissioner Howerton pulled item 18-0881 (FY 2018-19 budget ordinance) for citizen comment, and the remaining consent items passed 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Installment Financing Agreement (G.S. 160A-20) and CFO Reimbursement Authority Resolutions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Jay Gibson and CFO Susan Tezai presented two resolutions to refinance $43.5 million for Administration Building II renovations and finance detention center pod renovations, a portion of Admin II, the emergency communications center in the new police headquarters, emergency radio equipment, detention center elevators, and three Durham County Fire and Rescue vehicles, while authorizing the CFO to handle reimbursement actions under IRS/Treasury rules. No citizens spoke during the public hearing, and both resolutions passed 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 18-0881: FY 2018-19 Budget Ordinance Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Ricky Hart questioned confusing language in the recommended budget displaying $2.5 million for 27 school resource officers and $300,000 transitional SRO funds on the DPS page; Budget Director Keith Lane and commissioners clarified the SROs are in the Sheriff's budget, the $300,000 request was rescinded, and the adopted budget text would be clarified. Bull City Community Schools executive director Nicholas Graber-Grace thanked the board, and commissioners highlighted full DPS funding ($138M+), two community schools coordinator positions, $2.15 million for Pre-K, $300,000+ for eviction diversion and supportive housing, law enforcement pay raises, a female mental health jail pod, expanded community paramedicine, and cutting the property tax increase from 1.9 cents to 1 cent before adopting the budget 4-0.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments and Motion to Enter Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The four present commissioners made appointments to 13 advisory boards and commissions, deferring a tied Sports Commission vote until July when all five members would be present. The board then voted 4-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(6).

agenda_items.title: Post-Closed Session Salary Adjustments for Tax Collector and Register of Deeds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Upon returning from closed session, the board voted 4-0 to set Tax Collector/Administrator Kim Simpson's salary at $145,306 and Register of Deeds Sharon Davis's salary at $100,515, effective on their anniversary dates.

votes.item_title: Motion to Adjourn from Pre-Meeting Closed Session
votes.notes: Heidi Carter absent on an excused absence approved June 11, 2018 (confirmed at 01:47:02 by note to wait until July 'when we have five').
votes.discussion_detail: Motion to return to open session at the start of the regular meeting.

votes.item_title: Approval of Minutes (April 2, 2018 Work Session and May 29, 2018 Regular Session)
votes.discussion_detail: Commissioners reminded staff to communicate directives contained in the April 2 work session minutes.

votes.item_title: Consent Agenda (Items 18-0848 through 18-0892, Excluding Pulled Item 18-0881)
votes.discussion_detail: Included southern Durham fire consolidation ILA (18-0848), Pre-K expansion contract (18-0866), Chamber contract (18-0877), and Student U W.G. Pearson MOU; item 18-0881 was pulled for public comment.

votes.item_title: Installment Financing Agreement (G.S. 160A-20) and CFO Reimbursement Authority Resolutions
votes.discussion_detail: Authorizes installment financing to refinance Admin II ($43.5M) and fund detention center pods/elevators, emergency communications center/radios, and fire/rescue vehicles, plus CFO reimbursement authority.

votes.item_title: Item 18-0881: Adoption of FY 2018-19 Budget Ordinance
votes.discussion_detail: Adopts the FY 2018-19 Durham County budget ordinance with a 1-cent property tax increase (reduced from 1.9 cents), full DPS request ($138M+), two community schools coordinator positions, $2.15M Durham Pre-K expansion, eviction diversion/supportive housing, law enforcement pay raises, and a female jail mental health pod.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(4) and (a)(6))
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session to continue economic development negotiations and conduct individual personnel matters.

votes.item_title: Post-Closed Session Salary Adjustments for Tax Collector Kim Simpson ($145,306) and Register of Deeds Sharon Davis ($100,515)
votes.discussion_detail: Sets new salaries effective on each official's anniversary date.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC June 11, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 11, 2018 meeting, the Durham County Board of Commissioners approved the May 14 minutes (5-0), recognized awards for Best Workplace for Commuters and the Sedimentation & Erosion Control program, approved consent agenda items 18-0743 through 18-0851 (5-0), and held an extensive public hearing on the FY 2018-19 recommended budget. Dozens of speakers addressed Detention Center safety and the 2017 suicide of 17-year-old Niecy Fennell, Inmate Welfare Fund commissary/phone fees and money bail, funding five Community Schools coordinator positions, custodial living wages, eviction diversion rental assistance, and Durham Tech accountability. Following a closed-session personnel evaluation, the board split 4-1 to set County Manager Wendell Davis's FY 2018-19 salary at $221,579 (Ayes: Wendy Jacobs, James Hill, Ellen W. Reckhow, Heidi Carter; Nay: Brenda A. Howerton), with Howerton objecting that the 2% increase was unfair compared to peer counties and the board's own 3% adjustment and protesting same-day distribution of evaluation materials.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of May 14, 2018 Regular Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order and announced the June 25 budget adoption date, the online budget comment portal, a June 16 Dolly Parton's Imagination Library enrollment event, and the relaunch of Durham Neighborhood College. The board unanimously approved the May 14, 2018 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: Best Workplace for Commuters and Sedimentation & Erosion Control Award
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sustainability Officer Tobin Freid presented the Best Workplace for Commuters recognition highlighting employee GoPasses, vanpool subsidies, bike lockers, flex schedules, and GoTriangle's Emergency Ride Home program. State officials also presented an award recognizing Durham County's Sedimentation & Erosion Control program for rebounding from 2016 probation and enacting UDO alignment updates.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Scheduling Objection and Approval of Consent Agenda (Items 18-0743 through 18-0851)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton objected to taking up a closed-session personnel item whose packet materials were circulated at 6:00 p.m. that evening and asked to postpone it to June 25; Chair Jacobs noted other commissioners wished to hold the closed session that night while offering an additional session if needed. The board then unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0743 through 18-0851.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on FY 2018-19 County Manager's Recommended Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Under a two-minute per speaker limit, residents and advocates testified on four major budget themes: (1) jail safety, federal PREA sight-and-sound separation for minors, inmate mental healthcare, ending money bail, and removing detainee phone/commissary fees from the Inmate Welfare Fund (including attorneys Ian Mance and Whitley Carpenter representing Julia Graves, mother of Niecy Fennell); (2) funding five Community Schools coordinator positions, custodial living wages, universal Pre-K, and Durham Tech outcome tracking (opposed on tax/outcomes grounds by Antonio Jones and Friends of Durham chair Dick Ford); (3) adding $200,000 in county emergency rental assistance and a coordinator for eviction diversion plus renewing Durham Habitat's $40,000 repair grant; and (4) funding a Memorial Stadium hammer throw cage for the 2019 USATF National Youth Outdoor Championships.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session on Personnel Evaluation (G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the public hearing, the board voted 5-0 to enter closed session pursuant to N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6) to conduct an individual public officer evaluation.

agenda_items.title: Post-Closed Session Vote and Debate on County Manager FY 2018-19 Salary ($221,579)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Returning from closed session, the board voted 4-1 to set County Manager Wendell Davis's FY 2018-19 salary at $221,579. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton opposed the figure and read a formal dissent citing the manager's achievements and arguing he deserved a 3%–6% raise, while Commissioners James Hill, Wendy Jacobs, Ellen W. Reckhow, and Heidi Carter defended the ~2% increase as consistent with a 'meets expectations' rating under the board's mutually adopted evaluation instrument and placing Davis third in base pay and second in total compensation ($324,968.07) among peer NC counties.

agenda_items.title: Commissioner Heidi Carter Excused Absence Request for June 25, 2018
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter requested and received unanimous approval for an excused absence from the June 25, 2018 budget adoption meeting to accompany her husband on an award trip to Hawaii.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 14, 2018 Regular Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Routine approval of the May 14, 2018 regular session minutes.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session (N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(6))
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for individual public officer evaluation.

disagreements.issue: County Manager Wendell Davis FY 2018-19 Salary Increase and Evaluation Process
disagreements.summary: The board divided 4-1 over setting County Manager Wendell Davis's FY 2018-19 salary at $221,579 (an increase of over $4,000, or roughly 2%), as well as over holding the vote the same night evaluation materials were circulated at 6:00 p.m.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve a 2% salary increase to $221,579 based on the board's mutually adopted evaluation instrument and peer county benchmarks.
side_a_arguments: James Hill noted that peer county managers received 0% to 2% raises (contradicting claims of a 3%–6% floor) and that 48% of county employees received the same 2% 'meets expectations' increase.

Wendy Jacobs cited benchmark data showing $221,579 ranked third highest in base pay behind only Mecklenburg and Wake counties and second highest statewide in total compensation ($324,968.07 including benefits).
Ellen W. Reckhow and Heidi Carter emphasized that the manager co-drafted and agreed to the evaluation instrument, which the entire board—including Howerton—had unanimously adopted the prior year.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject limiting the County Manager's increase to ~$4,000 (~2%) and defer the vote to June 25 to allow proper review of same-day materials.
side_b_arguments: Brenda A. Howerton argued the manager exceeded expectations—citing the AAA bond rating, clean audit, 15+ awards, Managing for Results, Pre-K, gun violence reduction, and southern fire consolidation—and deserved 3%–6% rather than less than the board's own 3% budget adjustment.
Howerton protested voting on information distributed at 6:00 p.m. the same evening instead of postponing action until the June 25 meeting.
disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 4-1, setting the County Manager's FY 2018-19 salary at $221,579.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC May 14, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 14, 2018 regular session, County Manager Wendell Davis presented his FY 2018-19 Recommended Budget totaling $644.5 million (+1.8%, including a $435.5 million general fund) and proposing a 1.9-cent countywide property tax increase plus a 2-cent Durham County Fire and Rescue Service District tax increase to support southern Durham fire consolidation with the City. Key budget recommendations included $137 million in operating funding for Durham Public Schools (+$3 million), $5.2 million total for Pre-K expansion ($3.7 million as a challenge grant), 20 new Sheriff's Office positions (5 school resource officers replacing city-funded SROs, 2 domestic violence deputies, and 13 detention officers for a female mental health unit), $3 million to begin implementing the compensation and classification study, and transitioning 53 county fire positions to the City of Durham. The board also issued proclamations for Foster Care Awareness Month, National Drug Court Month, and Older Americans Month, approved the April 21 minutes (5-0), and unanimously adopted consent agenda items 18-0673 through 18-0810 (5-0).

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order and announced the third annual Aging Well in Durham Summit on May 19, the June 9 Summer Reading kickoff at Northgate Mall, and a May 17 maintenance closure at a county solid waste convenience site. The board unanimously approved the April 21, 2018 meeting minutes.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board read proclamations for Foster Care Awareness Month (with DSS Director Ben Rose and Sharon Flatt highlighting the need for more locally licensed foster homes), National Drug Court Month (with Judge Brad Battaglia and CJRC's Roshana Parker noting restorative justice outcomes), and Older Americans Month (with commissioner remarks on pedestrian fatalities and waitlists for Meals on Wheels and in-home care).

agenda_items.title: County Manager's Recommended FY 2018-19 Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Wendell Davis presented the recommended $644.5 million FY 2018-19 budget ($435.5 million general fund), proposing a 1.9-cent property tax rate increase and a 2-cent fire district tax increase to fund southern fire consolidation (transferring 53 positions to the City). Major priorities included $137 million for DPS (+$3M; $3,400 per pupil), $5.2 million for Pre-K expansion, $7.5 million for Durham Tech, 20 new Sheriff/Detention positions (5 SROs, 2 DV deputies, 13 detention officers for a female mental health pod), EMS training and 5 replacement ambulances, $3 million to begin implementing the compensation/classification study, and a 2%–4% pay-for-performance range; commissioners confirmed the May–June budget work session schedule and asked to review the resident survey on May 22.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC April 23, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 23, 2018 regular session, the Durham County Board of Commissioners surprised retiring Clerk to the Board Michelle Parker-Evans with a resolution honoring her 31 years of local government service and issued proclamations for Durham Reentry Week, National Correctional Officers and Employees Week, and Children's Mental Health Awareness Month. The board unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0745 through 18-0782 (5-0), including a Triangle Wastewater Treatment Plant contract achieving 100% minority- and women-owned business participation, a letter supporting state legislation for Durham Public Schools teacher housing with CASA and SECU, and a resolution advocating a 2018 statewide North Carolina School Construction Bond. Following a public hearing with no speakers, the board unanimously adopted Unified Development Ordinance Text Amendment TC17-007 allowing alternative streetscape designs in Downtown and Compact Design districts (5-0), and after a closed session covering litigation (*Milton v. Durham County*) and personnel, unanimously appointed Terry Huggy (transcribed) as Clerk to the Board effective May 7, 2018 at an $85,000 salary (5-0).

Howerton circulated an NEA alert urging opposition to SNAP cuts in the federal Agriculture and Nutrition Act. The board unanimously approved the April 9 regular session and April 14 PAC 4 meeting minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Items: Clerk Michelle Parker-Evans Retirement and Reentry, Correctional Officers, and Children's Mental Health Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board surprised Clerk to the Board Michelle Parker-Evans with a resolution celebrating her 31-year career in local government ahead of her May 1 retirement. Commissioners also presented proclamations for Durham Reentry Week (April 23–27), National Correctional Officers and Employees Week (with Sheriff Mike Andrews), and Children's Mental Health Awareness Month.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 18-0745 through 18-0782) and NC School Construction Bond Resolution

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC April 9 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 9, 2018 regular session, the Durham County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved minutes for three prior meetings (5-0), honored retiring Soil and Water Conservation Director Eddie Culberson, and issued proclamations for Child Abuse Prevention Month and National County Government Month. IT Director Greg Marrow, Criminal Justice Resource Center Director Gudrun Parmer, and Dr. Shannon Tufts of the UNC School of Government recognized item 18-0647—Durham County's Local Government Federal Credit Union innovation award for its open-source court date text reminder system (`courtreminders.dconc.gov`) that sharply curtailed failure-to-appear jailings. The board unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0647 through 18-0753 (5-0), including a landmark Resolution to Support Women's Health (read aloud by Heidi Carter) calling for repeal of the federal Hyde Amendment and comprehensive reproductive healthcare and abortion insurance coverage, and unanimously approved an excused absence request for May 23–29, 2018 (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs called the meeting to order and announced the April 17 Kids Voting Durham youth candidate forum, April 16 NC 98 corridor study open house, Pre-K/Head Start enrollment, an April 23 NCDOT roundabout meeting, NCACC school construction bond advocacy (noted by Brenda A. Howerton), and Veterans Services limited hours. The board unanimously approved minutes for the February 8 work session, March 26 regular session, and March 16 legislative breakfast.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: Eddie Culberson, Child Abuse Prevention Month, and National County Government Month
agenda_items.discussion_summary: General Manager Jay Gibson introduced a surprise recognition honoring Eddie Culberson for his water quality, stream restoration, and stormwater work in Soil and Water Conservation. The board also presented proclamations for Child Abuse Prevention Month (with DSS Director Ben Rose and Prevent Child Abuse NC's Sharon Hirsch) and National County Government Month.

agenda_items.title: Recognition of Item 18-0647: UNC School of Government Award for Court Date Reminder System
agenda_items.discussion_summary: IT Director Greg Marrow, CJRC Director Gudrun Parmer, and UNC School of Government's Dr. Shannon Tufts presented the Local Government Federal Credit Union innovation award for Durham County's open-source court date text reminder system (`courtreminders.dconc.gov`). Officials noted that over 2,000 residents had signed up and only two recipients missed court out of several thousand reminders sent over a recent 20-day period, helping reduce failure-to-appear incarcerations, fines, and fees.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 18-0647 through 18-0753) and Resolution to Support Women's Health
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0647 through 18-0753. Commissioner Heidi Carter then read aloud the adopted Resolution to Support Women's Health—calling for repeal of the federal Hyde Amendment and urging President Trump and Governor Cooper to protect reproductive healthcare and abortion insurance coverage—which Chair Jacobs noted made Durham the 14th locality nationally and first in North Carolina to pass such a resolution.

agenda_items.title: Excused Absence Request (May 23–29) and Grant Acknowledgements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved an excused absence for meetings from May 23 to May 29, 2018. Chair Jacobs also highlighted numerous grants and community donations included on the consent agenda (Aetna, UNC FIT, Shift NC, Watts Street Baptist Church, Wake EMC, and an anonymous CJRC donation), with Vice Chair James Hill emphasizing that the board's gratitude applied on behalf of all five commissioners.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC March 26
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 26, 2018 regular session (indexed under March 27, 2018), Chair Wendy Jacobs delivered the 2018 State of the County Address highlighting Durham's 27.9% job growth, cradle-to-career and early childhood priorities, opioid response, court-reminder and reentry initiatives, Durham-Orange Light Rail and Durham-Wake Commuter Rail progress, and 3.54% property tax base growth tempered by slowing sales tax revenues. Following budget public comments, approval of the February 26 minutes (5-0), and recognitions for National Service Recognition Day, EMS Corporal Chris Langdon, and IS&T analyst Bert White, the board unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0687 through 18-0741 (5-0), including resolutions opposing offshore oil/gas drilling and seismic blasting (18-0722) and supporting youth-led advocacy for gun violence prevention legislation (18-0741). After a public hearing with no opposition, the board unanimously approved the Future Land Use Map amendment (Office to Industrial), consistency statement, and Industrial Light rezoning for the 2.187-acre Long Beverage expansion along Page Road (5-0 each) and appointed three members to the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and 2018 State of the County Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs delivered the 2018 State of the County Address, citing 3.8% unemployment and 27.9% job growth alongside a 17.4% poverty rate and only 38% kindergarten readiness as drivers for a cradle-to-career system. She also highlighted law enforcement Narcan deployment, the court reminder and Local Reentry Council programs, Durham-Orange Light Rail ($1.25 billion federal funding eligibility) and Durham-Wake Commuter Rail progress, interim affordable housing density bonuses, and 3.54% tax base growth offset by slowing sales tax collections.

agenda_items.title: Budget Public Comment, Announcements, NCACC Report, and Approval of February 26 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Carolina Arbors residents commented on the upcoming May opening of co-located Fire Station 17, neighborhood speeding, and prioritizing education funding, while staff publicized the online FY 2018-19 budget comment portal. Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton reported on her NCACC '100 Counties Helping All Children Thrive' summit, and the board unanimously approved the February 26, 2018 regular session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions: National Service Recognition Day, EMS Corporal Chris Langdon, and IS&T Analyst Bert White
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board proclaimed April 3, 2018 as National Service Recognition Day with NCCU Eagle Corps director Colleen Herbert and Durham Tech RSVP coordinator Paula Rife. Commissioners then witnessed EMS Operations Chief Rodney Medlin present the Meritorious Intervention Commendation to Paramedic Corporal Chris Langdon for saving a crash victim's life off-duty with a tourniquet, and recognized IS&T's Bert White as HDI IT Analyst of the Year for the Triangle/Eastern NC region.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 18-0687 through 18-0741), Offshore Drilling Opposition (18-0722), and Youth Gun Violence Resolution (18-0741)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0687 through 18-0741. Commissioner Ellen W. Reckhow then read Resolution 18-0722 opposing offshore oil/gas drilling and seismic airgun blasting off North Carolina's coast, and Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton read Resolution 18-0741 supporting youth-led advocacy for universal background checks, waiting periods, an assault weapons ban, and extreme risk protective orders while rejecting arming teachers.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Long Beverage Expansion Plan Amendment and Rezoning (A1700015 / Z1700037)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Senior Planner Jamie Sunyak and Planning Director Sara Young presented Patrick Byker's application to amend the Future Land Use Map from Office to Industrial and rezone four parcels (2.187 acres along Page Road) from Rural Residential to Industrial Light (IL) for future Long Beverage expansion, noting a 13-0 Planning Commission recommendation. After the applicant testified that employee shifts occur outside peak hours and no opponents spoke, the board unanimously approved the plan amendment resolution, consistency statement, and IL rezoning ordinance.

agenda_items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted by ballot to appoint Sylvia Alston, Northy Justice, and Brenda Bram (as transcribed) to the Nursing Home Community Advisory Committee before adjourning.

meetings.title: Durham County BOCC March 12
meetings.executive_summary: At the March 12, 2018 regular session, the Durham County Board of Commissioners approved the January 2, 2018 work session minutes (5-0), reviewed the FY 2018-19 budget calendar while requesting additional work sessions to match the prior year's 28+ hours of deliberations, and unanimously adopted a time-sensitive Joint Resolution with the Social Services and Public Health boards opposing 2018 Farm Bill cuts or cost-shifts to SNAP (5-0). The board proclaimed April 3, 2018 as National Service Recognition Day and March 25, 2018 as Durham CROP Hunger Walk Day (honoring the late Baba Chuck Davis), and unanimously approved consent agenda items 18-0603 through 18-0676 (5-0), highlighting five new Open Space and Trails Matching Grants and a $140,000 Incredible Years parenting program grant. No closed session was held, and officials noted inclement weather could delay the next morning's Joint City-County Committee meeting.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Announcements, and Approval of January 2, 2018 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Wendy Jacobs confirmed the addition of the Joint SNAP Resolution to the agenda and announced JCPC DJJ grant deadlines (March 19), the 16th Annual Women's Forum (March 22), and a water resources legal forum (March 22). The board unanimously approved the January 2, 2018 work session minutes while discussing keeping future minutes concise alongside tracking staff directives.

agenda_items.title: Item 18-0685: Advance Public Comments and FY 2018-19 Budget Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With no citizens signed up to speak—likely due to inclement weather and limited advance notice—staff agreed to carry forward an advance budget comment period to the next meeting. Commissioners requested polling for additional budget work sessions beyond May 24, May 31, June 4, and June 14 so the board could reach at least the 28+ deliberation hours held the prior year ahead of the June 11 public hearing and June 25 adoption.

agenda_items.title: Joint Resolution Supporting SNAP and Federal Nutrition Programs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioner Heidi Carter read a joint resolution with the Durham County Social Services Board and Board of Public Health urging North Carolina's congressional delegation to reject 2018 Farm Bill cuts, cost-shifts, or benefit reductions to SNAP (noting NC's $119 average monthly household benefit and 1.5 million+ recipients). The board unanimously approved the resolution.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Proclamations: National Service Recognition Day and Durham CROP Hunger Walk Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Recognition of IS&T analyst Bert White was deferred due to his absence. Chair Jacobs read proclamations declaring April 3, 2018 as National Service Recognition Day (AmeriCorps, Senior Corps, and NCCU Eagle Corps) and March 25, 2018 as Durham CROP Hunger Walk Day, joined by organizers Karen Johansson, Bob Newlin, and Marge Clemens highlighting the 44th annual walk's dedication to Baba Chuck Davis and Kenyan Safe School Zone fundraising.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 18-0603 through 18-0676)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Commissioners highlighted five new Open Space and Trails Matching Grants (bringing the 26-year program past 100 projects and $1.5 million awarded, including an Eno River canoe launch, Ellerbe Creek land, Lakewood Elementary improvements, Scrap Exchange open space, and 21 acres by Triangle Greenways Council) and a $140,000 grant expanding the Incredible Years program from birth to age eight. The board unanimously approved consent items 18-0603 through 18-0676.

agenda_items.title: Closing Updates: Federal SNAP Protection, Inclement Weather, and Remote Meeting Participation
